speaker: HOTSPUR
text: heart, will he to the King and lay open all our

speaker: HOTSPUR

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: hours.

text: O my good lord, why are you thus alone?

text: For what offense have I this fortnight been

text: A banished woman from my Harry’s bed?

text: And given my treasures and my rights of thee

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: In thy faint slumbers I by thee have watched,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: And heard thee murmur tales of iron wars,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: Speak terms of manage to thy bounding steed,

text: Cry “Courage! To the field!” And thou hast talked

text: Of sallies and retires, of trenches, tents,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: Of palisadoes, frontiers, parapets,

text: Of basilisks, of cannon, culverin,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: Of prisoners’ ransom, and of soldiers slain,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: And all the currents of a heady fight.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: Thy spirit within thee hath been so at war,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: And thus hath so bestirred thee in thy sleep,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: That beads of sweat have stood upon thy brow

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: Like bubbles in a late-disturbèd stream,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: And in thy face strange motions have appeared,

text: Such as we see when men restrain their breath

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: On some great sudden hest. O, what portents are these?

text: Some heavy business hath my lord in hand,

speaker: LADY PERCY

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: What, ho!

text: But hear you, my lord.

text: What say’st thou, my lady?

text: What is it carries you away?

text: Out, you mad-headed ape!

text: As you are tossed with. In faith,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Away!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Away, you trifler. Love, I love thee not.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: I care not for thee, Kate. This is no world

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: To play with mammets and to tilt with lips.

text: I will not love myself. Do you not love me?

text: I must not have you henceforth question me

speaker: HOTSPUR

text: Than Harry Percy’s wife; constant you are,

text: But yet a woman; and for secrecy

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: No lady closer, for I well believe

text: Thou wilt not utter what thou dost not know,

text: And so far will I trust thee, gentle Kate.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text: How? So far?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Not an inch further. But hark you, Kate,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Whither I go, thither shall you go too.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Today will I set forth, tomorrow you.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text: Will this content you, Kate?

text: there no virtue extant?

text: Didst thou never see Titan kiss a dish of

text: sweet tale of the sun’s? If thou didst, then behold

text: that compound.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: You rogue, here’s lime in this

text: sack too.—There is nothing but roguery to be

text: found in villainous man, yet a coward is worse than

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: a cup of sack with lime in it. A villainous coward! Go

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: thy ways, old Jack. Die when thou wilt. If manhood,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: good manhood, be not forgot upon the face of the

text: three good men unhanged in England, and one of

text: world, I say. I would I were a weaver. I could sing

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: still.

speaker: PRINCE
text: How now, woolsack, what mutter you?

text: A king’s son! If I do not beat thee out of thy

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: kingdom with a dagger of lath, and drive all thy

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: Wales!

speaker: PRINCE
text: Why, you whoreson round man, what’s the

speaker: PRINCE
text: matter?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: Are not you a coward? Answer me to that—

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: and Poins there?

speaker: POINS
text: Zounds, you fat paunch, an you call me coward,

speaker: POINS
text: by the Lord, I’ll stab thee.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: I call thee coward? I’ll see thee damned ere

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: I call thee coward, but I would give a thousand

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: pound I could run as fast as thou canst. You are

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: straight enough in the shoulders you care not who

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: sees your back. Call you that backing of your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: friends? A plague upon such backing! Give me them

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: that will face me.—Give me a cup of sack.—I am a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: rogue if I drunk today.

speaker: PRINCE
text: O villain, thy lips are scarce wiped since thou

speaker: PRINCE
text: drunk’st last.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: All is one for that. A plague of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: all cowards, still say I.

speaker: PRINCE
text: What’s the matter?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: What’s the matter? There be four of us here

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: have ta’en a thousand pound this day morning.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Where is it, Jack, where is it?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: Where is it? Taken from us it is. A hundred

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: upon poor four of us.

speaker: PRINCE
text: What, a hundred, man?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: I am a rogue if I were not at half-sword

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: with a dozen of them two hours together. I have

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: ’scaped by miracle. I am eight times thrust through

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: the doublet, four through the hose, my buckler

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: cut through and through, my sword hacked like

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: a handsaw. Ecce signum! I never dealt better since

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: I was a man. All would not do. A plague of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: all cowards! Let them speak.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: If they speak more or

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: less than truth, they are villains, and the sons of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: darkness.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Speak, sirs, how was it?

speaker: BARDOLPH
text: We four set upon some dozen.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: Sixteen at least, my lord.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text: And bound them.

speaker: PETO
text: No, no, they were not bound.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: You rogue, they were bound, every man of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: them, or I am a Jew else, an Ebrew Jew.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text: As we were sharing, some six or seven

speaker: BARDOLPH

text: And unbound the rest, and then come in the

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: PRINCE

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: creature.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Pray God you have not murdered some of

speaker: PRINCE
text: them.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: Nay, that’s past praying for. I have peppered

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: two of them. Two I am sure I have paid, two rogues

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: in buckram suits. I tell thee what, Hal, if I tell thee a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text: lie, spit in my face, call me horse. Thou knowest my

speaker: FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF

text: will not touch the true prince. No, fie!

speaker: PRINCE
text: sword so hacked?

text: behold these exhalations?

speaker: PRINCE

speaker: BARDOLPH

speaker: PRINCE

speaker: PRINCE

text: Prepare we for our marriage; on which day,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: My Lord of Burgundy, we’ll take your oath,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And all the peers’, for surety of our leagues.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Then shall I swear to Kate, and you to me,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And may our oaths well kept and prosp’rous be.

speaker: CHORUS
text: Thus far with rough and all-unable pen

speaker: CHORUS
text: Our bending author hath pursued the story,

speaker: CHORUS
text: In little room confining mighty men,

speaker: CHORUS
text: Mangling by starts the full course of their glory.

speaker: CHORUS
text: Small time, but in that small most greatly lived

speaker: CHORUS
text: This star of England. Fortune made his sword,

speaker: CHORUS
text: By which the world’s best garden he achieved

speaker: CHORUS
text: And of it left his son imperial lord.

speaker: CHORUS
text: Henry the Sixth, in infant bands crowned King

speaker: CHORUS
text: Of France and England, did this king succeed,

speaker: CHORUS
text: Whose state so many had the managing

speaker: CHORUS
text: That they lost France and made his England bleed,

speaker: CHORUS
text: Which oft our stage hath shown. And for their sake,

speaker: CHORUS
text: In your fair minds let this acceptance take.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Hung be the heavens with black, yield day to night!

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Comets, importing change of times and states,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Brandish your crystal tresses in the sky,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: And with them scourge the bad revolting stars

speaker: BEDFORD
text: That have consented unto Henry’s death:

speaker: BEDFORD
text: King Henry the Fifth, too famous to live long.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: England ne’er lost a king of so much worth.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: England ne’er had a king until his time.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Virtue he had, deserving to command;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: His brandished sword did blind men with his beams;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: His arms spread wider than a dragon’s wings;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: His sparkling eyes, replete with wrathful fire,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: More dazzled and drove back his enemies

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Than midday sun fierce bent against their faces.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: What should I say? His deeds exceed all speech.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: He ne’er lift up his hand but conquerèd.

speaker: EXETER
text: We mourn in black; why mourn we not in blood?

speaker: EXETER
text: Henry is dead and never shall revive.

speaker: EXETER
text: Upon a wooden coffin we attend,

speaker: EXETER
text: And Death’s dishonorable victory

speaker: EXETER
text: We with our stately presence glorify,

speaker: EXETER
text: Like captives bound to a triumphant car.

speaker: EXETER
text: What? Shall we curse the planets of mishap

speaker: EXETER
text: That plotted thus our glory’s overthrow?

speaker: EXETER
text: Or shall we think the subtle-witted French

speaker: EXETER
text: Conjurers and sorcerers, that, afraid of him,

speaker: EXETER
text: By magic verses have contrived his end?

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: He was a king blest of the King of kings;

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: Unto the French the dreadful Judgment Day

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: So dreadful will not be as was his sight.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: The battles of the Lord of Hosts he fought;

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: The Church’s prayers made him so prosperous.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: The Church? Where is it? Had not churchmen prayed,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: His thread of life had not so soon decayed.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: None do you like but an effeminate prince

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Whom like a schoolboy you may overawe.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: Gloucester, whate’er we like, thou art Protector

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: And lookest to command the Prince and realm.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: Thy wife is proud; she holdeth thee in awe

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: More than God or religious churchmen may.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Name not religion, for thou lov’st the flesh,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: And ne’er throughout the year to church thou go’st,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Except it be to pray against thy foes.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Cease, cease these jars, and rest your minds in peace!

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Let’s to the altar.—Heralds, wait on us.—

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Instead of gold, we’ll offer up our arms,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Since arms avail not, now that Henry’s dead.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Posterity, await for wretched years

speaker: BEDFORD
text: When at their mothers’ moistened eyes babes shall suck,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Our isle be made a nourish of salt tears,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: And none but women left to wail the dead.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Henry the Fifth, thy ghost I invocate:

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Prosper this realm, keep it from civil broils,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Combat with adverse planets in the heavens.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: A far more glorious star thy soul will make

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Than Julius Caesar or bright—

speaker: MESSENGER
text: My honorable lords, health to you all.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Sad tidings bring I to you out of France,

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Of loss, of slaughter, and discomfiture:

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Guyen, Champaigne, Rheims, Roan, Orleance,

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Paris, Gisors, Poitiers, are all quite lost.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: What say’st thou, man, before dead Henry’s corse?

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Speak softly, or the loss of those great towns

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Will make him burst his lead and rise from death.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Is Paris lost? Is Roan yielded up?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: If Henry were recalled to life again,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: These news would cause him once more yield the ghost.

speaker: EXETER
text: How were they lost? What treachery was used?

speaker: MESSENGER
text: No treachery, but want of men and money.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Amongst the soldiers, this is mutterèd:

speaker: MESSENGER
text: That here you maintain several factions

speaker: MESSENGER
text: And, whilst a field should be dispatched and fought,

speaker: MESSENGER
text: You are disputing of your generals.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: One would have ling’ring wars with little cost;

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Another would fly swift, but wanteth wings;

speaker: MESSENGER
text: A third thinks, without expense at all,

speaker: MESSENGER
text: By guileful fair words peace may be obtained.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Awake, awake, English nobility!

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Let not sloth dim your honors new begot.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Cropped are the flower-de-luces in your arms;

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Of England’s coat, one half is cut away.

speaker: EXETER
text: Were our tears wanting to this funeral,

speaker: EXETER
text: These tidings would call forth her flowing tides.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Me they concern; regent I am of France.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Give me my steelèd coat, I’ll fight for France.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Away with these disgraceful wailing robes.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Wounds will I lend the French instead of eyes

speaker: BEDFORD
text: To weep their intermissive miseries.

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: Lords, view these letters, full of bad mischance.

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: France is revolted from the English quite,

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: Except some petty towns of no import.

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: The Dauphin Charles is crownèd king in Rheims;

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: The Bastard of Orleance with him is joined;

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: Reignier, Duke of Anjou, doth take his part;

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: The Duke of Alanson flieth to his side.

speaker: EXETER
text: The Dauphin crownèd king? All fly to him?

speaker: EXETER
text: O, whither shall we fly from this reproach?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: We will not fly but to our enemies’ throats.—

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Bedford, if thou be slack, I’ll fight it out.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Gloucester, why doubt’st thou of my forwardness?

speaker: BEDFORD
text: An army have I mustered in my thoughts,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Wherewith already France is overrun.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: My gracious lords, to add to your laments,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Wherewith you now bedew King Henry’s hearse,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: I must inform you of a dismal fight

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Betwixt the stout Lord Talbot and the French.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: What? Wherein Talbot overcame, is ’t so?

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: O no, wherein Lord Talbot was o’erthrown.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: The circumstance I’ll tell you more at large.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: The tenth of August last, this dreadful lord,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Retiring from the siege of Orleance,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Having full scarce six thousand in his troop,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: By three and twenty thousand of the French

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Was round encompassèd and set upon.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: No leisure had he to enrank his men.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: He wanted pikes to set before his archers,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Instead whereof, sharp stakes plucked out of hedges

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: They pitchèd in the ground confusedly

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: To keep the horsemen off from breaking in.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: More than three hours the fight continuèd,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Where valiant Talbot, above human thought,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Enacted wonders with his sword and lance.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Hundreds he sent to hell, and none durst stand him;

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Here, there, and everywhere, enraged, he slew.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: The French exclaimed the devil was in arms;

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: All the whole army stood agazed on him.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: His soldiers, spying his undaunted spirit,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: “À Talbot! À Talbot!” cried out amain

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: And rushed into the bowels of the battle.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Here had the conquest fully been sealed up

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: If Sir John Fastolf had not played the coward.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: He, being in the vaward, placed behind

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: With purpose to relieve and follow them,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Cowardly fled, not having struck one stroke.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Hence grew the general wrack and massacre.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Enclosèd were they with their enemies.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: A base Walloon, to win the Dauphin’s grace,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Thrust Talbot with a spear into the back,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Whom all France, with their chief assembled strength,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Durst not presume to look once in the face.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Is Talbot slain then? I will slay myself

speaker: BEDFORD
text: For living idly here, in pomp and ease,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Whilst such a worthy leader, wanting aid,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Unto his dastard foemen is betrayed.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: O, no, he lives, but is took prisoner,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: And Lord Scales with him, and Lord Hungerford;

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Most of the rest slaughtered or took likewise.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: His ransom there is none but I shall pay.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: I’ll hale the Dauphin headlong from his throne;

speaker: BEDFORD
text: His crown shall be the ransom of my friend.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Four of their lords I’ll change for one of ours.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Farewell, my masters; to my task will I.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Bonfires in France forthwith I am to make,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: To keep our great Saint George’s feast withal.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Ten thousand soldiers with me I will take,

speaker: BEDFORD
text: Whose bloody deeds shall make all Europe quake.

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: So you had need; ’fore Orleance besieged,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: The English army is grown weak and faint;

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: The Earl of Salisbury craveth supply

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: And hardly keeps his men from mutiny,

speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
text: Since they so few watch such a multitude.

speaker: EXETER
text: Remember, lords, your oaths to Henry sworn:

speaker: EXETER
text: Either to quell the Dauphin utterly

speaker: EXETER
text: Or bring him in obedience to your yoke.

speaker: BEDFORD
text: I do remember it, and here take my leave

speaker: BEDFORD
text: To go about my preparation.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: I’ll to the Tower with all the haste I can

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: To view th’ artillery and munition,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: And then I will proclaim young Henry king.

speaker: EXETER
text: To Eltham will I, where the young king is,

speaker: EXETER
text: Being ordained his special governor;

speaker: EXETER
text: And for his safety there I’ll best devise.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: Each hath his place and function to attend.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: I am left out; for me nothing remains.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: But long I will not be Jack-out-of-office.

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: The King from Eltham I intend to steal,

speaker: WINCHESTER
text: And sit at chiefest stern of public weal.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Mars his true moving, even as in the heavens

speaker: CHARLES
text: So in the Earth, to this day is not known.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Late did he shine upon the English side;

speaker: CHARLES
text: Now we are victors; upon us he smiles.

speaker: CHARLES
text: What towns of any moment but we have?

speaker: CHARLES
text: At pleasure here we lie, near Orleance.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Otherwhiles, the famished English, like pale ghosts,

speaker: CHARLES
text: Faintly besiege us one hour in a month.

speaker: ALANSON
text: They want their porridge and their fat bull beeves.

speaker: ALANSON
text: Either they must be dieted like mules

speaker: ALANSON
text: And have their provender tied to their mouths,

speaker: ALANSON
text: Or piteous they will look, like drownèd mice.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Let’s raise the siege. Why live we idly here?

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Talbot is taken, whom we wont to fear.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Remaineth none but mad-brained Salisbury,

speaker: REIGNIER
text: And he may well in fretting spend his gall;

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Nor men nor money hath he to make war.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Sound, sound alarum! We will rush on them.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Now for the honor of the forlorn French!

speaker: CHARLES
text: Him I forgive my death that killeth me

speaker: CHARLES
text: When he sees me go back one foot, or fly.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Whoever saw the like? What men have I!

speaker: CHARLES
text: Dogs, cowards, dastards! I would ne’er have fled

speaker: CHARLES
text: But that they left me ’midst my enemies.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Salisbury is a desperate homicide.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: He fighteth as one weary of his life.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: The other lords, like lions wanting food,

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Do rush upon us as their hungry prey.

speaker: ALANSON
text: Froissart, a countryman of ours, records

speaker: ALANSON
text: England all Olivers and Rolands bred

speaker: ALANSON
text: During the time Edward the Third did reign.

speaker: ALANSON
text: More truly now may this be verified,

speaker: ALANSON
text: For none but Samsons and Goliases

speaker: ALANSON
text: It sendeth forth to skirmish. One to ten!

speaker: ALANSON
text: Lean rawboned rascals! Who would e’er suppose

speaker: ALANSON
text: They had such courage and audacity?

speaker: CHARLES
text: Let’s leave this town, for they are hare-brained slaves,

speaker: CHARLES
text: And hunger will enforce them to be more eager.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Of old I know them; rather with their teeth

speaker: CHARLES
text: The walls they’ll tear down than forsake the siege.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: I think by some odd gimmers or device

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Their arms are set, like clocks, still to strike on;

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Else ne’er could they hold out so as they do.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: By my consent, we’ll even let them alone.

speaker: ALANSON
text: Be it so.

speaker: BASTARD
text: Where’s the Prince Dauphin? I have news for him.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Bastard of Orleance, thrice welcome to us.

speaker: BASTARD
text: Methinks your looks are sad, your cheer appalled.

speaker: BASTARD
text: Hath the late overthrow wrought this offence?

speaker: BASTARD
text: Be not dismayed, for succor is at hand.

speaker: BASTARD
text: A holy maid hither with me I bring,

speaker: BASTARD
text: Which, by a vision sent to her from heaven,

speaker: BASTARD
text: Ordainèd is to raise this tedious siege

speaker: BASTARD
text: And drive the English forth the bounds of France.

speaker: BASTARD
text: The spirit of deep prophecy she hath,

speaker: BASTARD
text: Exceeding the nine Sibyls of old Rome.

speaker: BASTARD
text: What’s past and what’s to come she can descry.

speaker: BASTARD
text: Speak, shall I call her in? Believe my words,

speaker: BASTARD
text: For they are certain and unfallible.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Go call her in.

speaker: CHARLES
text: But first, to try her skill,

speaker: CHARLES
text: Reignier, stand thou as Dauphin in my place;

speaker: CHARLES
text: Question her proudly; let thy looks be stern.

speaker: CHARLES
text: By this means shall we sound what skill she hath.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Fair maid, is ’t thou wilt do these wondrous feats?

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Reignier, is ’t thou that thinkest to beguile me?

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Where is the Dauphin?—Come, come from behind.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: I know thee well, though never seen before.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Be not amazed; there’s nothing hid from me.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: In private will I talk with thee apart.—

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Stand back, you lords, and give us leave a while.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: She takes upon her bravely at first dash.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Dauphin, I am by birth a shepherd’s daughter,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: My wit untrained in any kind of art.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Heaven and Our Lady gracious hath it pleased

speaker: PUCELLE
text: To shine on my contemptible estate.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Lo, whilst I waited on my tender lambs,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And to sun’s parching heat displayed my cheeks,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: God’s Mother deignèd to appear to me,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And in a vision full of majesty

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Willed me to leave my base vocation

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And free my country from calamity.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Her aid she promised and assured success.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: In complete glory she revealed herself;

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And whereas I was black and swart before,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: With those clear rays which she infused on me

speaker: PUCELLE
text: That beauty am I blest with, which you may see.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Ask me what question thou canst possible,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And I will answer unpremeditated.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: My courage try by combat, if thou dar’st,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And thou shalt find that I exceed my sex.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Resolve on this: thou shalt be fortunate

speaker: PUCELLE
text: If thou receive me for thy warlike mate.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Thou hast astonished me with thy high terms.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Only this proof I’ll of thy valor make:

speaker: CHARLES
text: In single combat thou shalt buckle with me,

speaker: CHARLES
text: And if thou vanquishest, thy words are true;

speaker: CHARLES
text: Otherwise I renounce all confidence.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: I am prepared. Here is my keen-edged sword,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Decked with fine flower-de-luces on each side—

speaker: PUCELLE
text: The which at Touraine, in Saint Katherine’s churchyard,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Out of a great deal of old iron I chose forth.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Then come, a’ God’s name! I fear no woman.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: And while I live, I’ll ne’er fly from a man.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Stay, stay thy hands! Thou art an Amazon,

speaker: CHARLES
text: And fightest with the sword of Deborah.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Christ’s mother helps me; else I were too weak.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Whoe’er helps thee, ’tis thou that must help me.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Impatiently I burn with thy desire.

speaker: CHARLES
text: My heart and hands thou hast at once subdued.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Excellent Pucelle, if thy name be so,

speaker: CHARLES
text: Let me thy servant and not sovereign be.

speaker: CHARLES
text: ’Tis the French Dauphin sueth to thee thus.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: I must not yield to any rights of love,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: For my profession’s sacred from above.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: When I have chasèd all thy foes from hence,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Then will I think upon a recompense.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Meantime look gracious on thy prostrate thrall.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: My lord, methinks, is very long in talk.

speaker: ALANSON
text: Doubtless he shrives this woman to her smock,

speaker: ALANSON
text: Else ne’er could he so long protract his speech.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Shall we disturb him, since he keeps no mean?

speaker: ALANSON
text: He may mean more than we poor men do know.

speaker: ALANSON
text: These women are shrewd tempters with their tongues.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: My lord, where are you? What devise you on?

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Shall we give o’er Orleance, or no?

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Why, no, I say. Distrustful recreants,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Fight till the last gasp. I’ll be your guard.

speaker: CHARLES
text: What she says I’ll confirm: we’ll fight it out.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Assigned am I to be the English scourge.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: This night the siege assuredly I’ll raise.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Expect Saint Martin’s summer, halcyons’ days,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Since I have enterèd into these wars.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Glory is like a circle in the water,

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Till by broad spreading it disperse to naught.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: With Henry’s death, the English circle ends;

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Dispersèd are the glories it included.

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Now am I like that proud insulting ship

speaker: PUCELLE
text: Which Caesar and his fortune bare at once.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Was Mahomet inspirèd with a dove?

speaker: CHARLES
text: Thou with an eagle art inspirèd then.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Helen, the mother of great Constantine,

speaker: CHARLES
text: Nor yet Saint Philip’s daughters were like thee.

speaker: CHARLES
text: Bright star of Venus, fall’n down on the Earth,

speaker: CHARLES
text: How may I reverently worship thee enough?

speaker: ALANSON
text: Leave off delays, and let us raise the siege.

speaker: REIGNIER
text: Woman, do what thou canst to save our honors.

text: Mount you, my lord; towards Berwick post amain.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Edward and Richard, like a brace of greyhounds

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Having the fearful flying hare in sight,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: With fiery eyes sparkling for very wrath

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: And bloody steel grasped in their ireful hands,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Are at our backs, and therefore hence amain.

speaker: EXETER
text: Away, for Vengeance comes along with them.

speaker: EXETER
text: Nay, stay not to expostulate, make speed;

speaker: EXETER
text: Or else come after; I’ll away before.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Nay, take me with thee, good sweet Exeter;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Not that I fear to stay, but love to go

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Whither the Queen intends. Forward, away!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Here burns my candle out; ay, here it dies,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Which whiles it lasted gave King Henry light.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: O Lancaster, I fear thy overthrow

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: More than my body’s parting with my soul!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: My love and fear glued many friends to thee;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And now I fall, thy tough commixtures melts,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Impairing Henry, strength’ning misproud York;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And whither fly the gnats but to the sun?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And who shines now but Henry’s enemies?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: O Phoebus, hadst thou never given consent

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: That Phaëton should check thy fiery steeds,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Thy burning car never had scorched the Earth!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And Henry, hadst thou swayed as kings should do,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Or as thy father and his father did,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Giving no ground unto the house of York,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: They never then had sprung like summer flies;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: I and ten thousand in this luckless realm

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Had left no mourning widows for our death,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And thou this day hadst kept thy chair in peace.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: For what doth cherish weeds but gentle air?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And what makes robbers bold but too much lenity?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Bootless are plaints, and cureless are my wounds;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: No way to fly, no strength to hold out flight.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: The foe is merciless and will not pity,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: For at their hands I have deserved no pity.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: The air hath got into my deadly wounds,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: And much effuse of blood doth make me faint.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: Come, York and Richard, Warwick and the rest.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text: I stabbed your fathers’ bosoms; split my breast.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Now breathe we, lords. Good fortune bids us pause

speaker: EDWARD
text: And smooth the frowns of war with peaceful looks.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Some troops pursue the bloody-minded queen

speaker: EDWARD
text: That led calm Henry, though he were a king,

speaker: EDWARD
text: As doth a sail filled with a fretting gust

speaker: EDWARD
text: Command an argosy to stem the waves.

speaker: EDWARD
text: But think you, lords, that Clifford fled with them?

speaker: WARWICK
text: No, ’tis impossible he should escape,

speaker: WARWICK
text: For, though before his face I speak the words,

speaker: WARWICK
text: Your brother Richard marked him for the grave,

speaker: WARWICK
text: And wheresoe’er he is, he’s surely dead.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Whose soul is that which takes her heavy leave?

speaker: RICHARD
text: A deadly groan, like life and death’s departing.

speaker: EDWARD
text: See who it is; and, now the battle’s ended,

speaker: EDWARD
text: If friend or foe, let him be gently used.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Revoke that doom of mercy, for ’tis Clifford,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Who not contented that he lopped the branch

speaker: RICHARD
text: In hewing Rutland when his leaves put forth,

speaker: RICHARD
text: But set his murd’ring knife unto the root

speaker: RICHARD
text: From whence that tender spray did sweetly spring,

speaker: RICHARD
text: I mean our princely father, Duke of York.

speaker: WARWICK
text: From off the gates of York fetch down the head,

speaker: WARWICK
text: Your father’s head, which Clifford placèd there;

speaker: WARWICK
text: Instead whereof let this supply the room.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Measure for measure must be answerèd.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Bring forth that fatal screech owl to our house

speaker: EDWARD
text: That nothing sung but death to us and ours;

speaker: EDWARD
text: Now death shall stop his dismal threat’ning sound,

speaker: EDWARD
text: And his ill-boding tongue no more shall speak.

speaker: WARWICK
text: I think his understanding is bereft.—

speaker: WARWICK
text: Speak, Clifford, dost thou know who speaks to thee?—

speaker: WARWICK
text: Dark cloudy death o’ershades his beams of life,

speaker: WARWICK
text: And he nor sees nor hears us what we say.

speaker: RICHARD
text: O, would he did—and so, perhaps, he doth!

speaker: RICHARD
text: ’Tis but his policy to counterfeit,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Because he would avoid such bitter taunts

speaker: RICHARD
text: Which in the time of death he gave our father.

speaker: GEORGE
text: If so thou think’st, vex him with eager words.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Clifford, ask mercy and obtain no grace.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Clifford, repent in bootless penitence.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Clifford, devise excuses for thy faults.

speaker: GEORGE
text: While we devise fell tortures for thy faults.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Thou didst love York, and I am son to York.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Thou pitied’st Rutland; I will pity thee.

speaker: GEORGE
text: Where’s Captain Margaret to fence you now?

speaker: WARWICK
text: They mock thee, Clifford; swear as thou wast wont.

speaker: RICHARD
text: What, not an oath? Nay, then, the world goes hard

speaker: RICHARD
text: When Clifford cannot spare his friends an oath.

speaker: RICHARD
text: I know by that he’s dead; and, by my soul,

speaker: RICHARD
text: If this right hand would buy but two hours’ life

speaker: RICHARD
text: That I in all despite might rail at him,

speaker: RICHARD
text: This hand should chop it off, and with the issuing blood

speaker: RICHARD
text: Stifle the villain whose unstaunchèd thirst

speaker: RICHARD
text: York and young Rutland could not satisfy.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Ay, but he’s dead. Off with the traitor’s head,

speaker: WARWICK
text: And rear it in the place your father’s stands.

speaker: WARWICK
text: And now to London with triumphant march,

speaker: WARWICK
text: There to be crownèd England’s royal king,

speaker: WARWICK
text: From whence shall Warwick cut the sea to France

speaker: WARWICK
text: And ask the Lady Bona for thy queen;

speaker: WARWICK
text: So shalt thou sinew both these lands together,

speaker: WARWICK
text: And having France thy friend, thou shalt not dread

speaker: WARWICK
text: The scattered foe that hopes to rise again;

speaker: WARWICK
text: For though they cannot greatly sting to hurt,

speaker: WARWICK
text: Yet look to have them buzz to offend thine ears.

speaker: WARWICK
text: First will I see the coronation,

speaker: WARWICK
text: And then to Brittany I’ll cross the sea

speaker: WARWICK
text: To effect this marriage, so it please my lord.

speaker: EDWARD
text: Even as thou wilt, sweet Warwick, let it be;

speaker: EDWARD
text: For in thy shoulder do I build my seat,

speaker: EDWARD
text: And never will I undertake the thing

speaker: EDWARD
text: Wherein thy counsel and consent is wanting.—

speaker: EDWARD
text: Richard, I will create thee Duke of Gloucester,

speaker: EDWARD
text: And George, of Clarence. Warwick as ourself

speaker: EDWARD
text: Shall do and undo as him pleaseth best.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Let me be Duke of Clarence, George of Gloucester,

speaker: RICHARD
text: For Gloucester’s dukedom is too ominous.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Tut, that’s a foolish observation.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Richard, be Duke of Gloucester. Now to London,

speaker: WARWICK
text: To see these honors in possession.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Under this thick-grown brake we’ll shroud ourselves,

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: For through this laund anon the deer will come;

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: And in this covert will we make our stand,

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Culling the principal of all the deer.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: I’ll stay above the hill, so both may shoot.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: That cannot be. The noise of thy crossbow

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Will scare the herd, and so my shoot is lost.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Here stand we both, and aim we at the best.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: And for the time shall not seem tedious,

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: I’ll tell thee what befell me on a day

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: In this self place where now we mean to stand.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Here comes a man; let’s stay till he be past.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: From Scotland am I stol’n, even of pure love,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: To greet mine own land with my wishful sight.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: No, Harry, Harry, ’tis no land of thine!

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Thy place is filled, thy scepter wrung from thee,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Thy balm washed off wherewith thou wast anointed.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: No bending knee will call thee Caesar now,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: No humble suitors press to speak for right,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: No, not a man comes for redress of thee;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: For how can I help them an not myself?

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Ay, here’s a deer whose skin’s a keeper’s fee.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: This is the quondam king. Let’s seize upon him.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Let me embrace the sour adversaries,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: For wise men say it is the wisest course.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Why linger we? Let us lay hands upon him.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: Forbear awhile; we’ll hear a little more.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: My queen and son are gone to France for aid,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And, as I hear, the great commanding Warwick

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Is thither gone to crave the French king’s sister

speaker: KING HENRY
text: To wife for Edward. If this news be true,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Poor queen and son, your labor is but lost,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: For Warwick is a subtle orator,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And Lewis a prince soon won with moving words.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: By this account, then, Margaret may win him,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: For she’s a woman to be pitied much.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Her sighs will make a batt’ry in his breast,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Her tears will pierce into a marble heart.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: The tiger will be mild whiles she doth mourn,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And Nero will be tainted with remorse

speaker: KING HENRY
text: To hear and see her plaints, her brinish tears.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Ay, but she’s come to beg, Warwick to give;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: She on his left side craving aid for Henry;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: He on his right asking a wife for Edward.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: She weeps and says her Henry is deposed;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: He smiles and says his Edward is installed;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: That she, poor wretch, for grief can speak no more,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Whiles Warwick tells his title, smooths the wrong,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Inferreth arguments of mighty strength,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And in conclusion wins the King from her

speaker: KING HENRY
text: With promise of his sister and what else

speaker: KING HENRY
text: To strengthen and support King Edward’s place.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: O Margaret, thus ’twill be, and thou, poor soul,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Art then forsaken, as thou went’st forlorn.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Say, what art thou that talk’st of kings and queens?

speaker: KING HENRY
text: More than I seem, and less than I was born to:

speaker: KING HENRY
text: A man at least, for less I should not be;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And men may talk of kings, and why not I?

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Ay, but thou talk’st as if thou wert a king.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Why, so I am in mind, and that’s enough.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: But if thou be a king, where is thy crown?

speaker: KING HENRY
text: My crown is in my heart, not on my head;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Not decked with diamonds and Indian stones,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Nor to be seen. My crown is called content;

speaker: KING HENRY
text: A crown it is that seldom kings enjoy.

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Well, if you be a king crowned with content,

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Your crown content and you must be contented

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: To go along with us. For, as we think,

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: You are the king King Edward hath deposed;

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: And we his subjects sworn in all allegiance

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Will apprehend you as his enemy.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: But did you never swear and break an oath?

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: No, never such an oath, nor will not now.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Where did you dwell when I was King of England?

speaker: SECOND GAMEKEEPER
text: Here in this country, where we now remain.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: I was anointed king at nine months old.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: My father and my grandfather were kings,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And you were sworn true subjects unto me.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And tell me, then, have you not broke your oaths?

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: No, for we were subjects but while you were king.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Why, am I dead? Do I not breathe a man?

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Ah, simple men, you know not what you swear.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Look as I blow this feather from my face

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And as the air blows it to me again,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Obeying with my wind when I do blow

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And yielding to another when it blows,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Commanded always by the greater gust,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Such is the lightness of you common men.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: But do not break your oaths, for of that sin

speaker: KING HENRY
text: My mild entreaty shall not make you guilty.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Go where you will, the King shall be commanded,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And be you kings: command, and I’ll obey.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: We are true subjects to the King, King Edward.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: So would you be again to Henry

speaker: KING HENRY
text: If he were seated as King Edward is.

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: We charge you in God’s name and the King’s

speaker: FIRST GAMEKEEPER
text: To go with us unto the officers.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: In God’s name, lead. Your king’s name be obeyed,

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And what God will, that let your king perform.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: And what he will, I humbly yield unto.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Brother of Gloucester, at Saint Albans field

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: This lady’s husband, Sir Richard Grey, was slain,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: His land then seized on by the conqueror.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Her suit is now to repossess those lands,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Which we in justice cannot well deny,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Because in quarrel of the house of York

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: The worthy gentleman did lose his life.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Your Highness shall do well to grant her suit;

speaker: RICHARD
text: It were dishonor to deny it her.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: It were no less, but yet I’ll make a pause.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Yea, is it so?

speaker: RICHARD
text: I see the lady hath a thing to grant

speaker: RICHARD
text: Before the King will grant her humble suit.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He knows the game; how true he keeps the wind!

speaker: RICHARD
text: Silence!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Widow, we will consider of your suit,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And come some other time to know our mind.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Right gracious lord, I cannot brook delay.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: May it please your Highness to resolve me now,

speaker: LADY GREY
text: And what your pleasure is shall satisfy me.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Ay, widow? Then I’ll warrant you all your lands,

speaker: RICHARD
text: An if what pleases him shall pleasure you.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Fight closer, or, good faith, you’ll catch a blow.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I fear her not, unless she chance to fall.

speaker: RICHARD
text: God forbid that, for he’ll take vantages.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: How many children hast thou, widow? Tell me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I think he means to beg a child of her.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Nay, then, whip me; he’ll rather give her two.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Three, my most gracious lord.

speaker: RICHARD
text: You shall have four if you’ll be ruled by him.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: ’Twere pity they should lose their father’s lands.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Be pitiful, dread lord, and grant it then.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Lords, give us leave. I’ll try this widow’s wit.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Ay, good leave have you, for you will have leave

speaker: RICHARD
text: Till youth take leave and leave you to the crutch.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Now tell me, madam, do you love your children?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Ay, full as dearly as I love myself.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And would you not do much to do them good?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: To do them good I would sustain some harm.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Then get your husband’s lands to do them good.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Therefore I came unto your Majesty.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: I’ll tell you how these lands are to be got.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: So shall you bind me to your Highness’ service.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: What service wilt thou do me if I give them?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: What you command that rests in me to do.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But you will take exceptions to my boon.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: No, gracious lord, except I cannot do it.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Ay, but thou canst do what I mean to ask.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why, then, I will do what your Grace commands.

speaker: RICHARD
text: He plies her hard, and much rain wears the marble.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: As red as fire! Nay, then, her wax must melt.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why stops my lord? Shall I not hear my task?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: An easy task; ’tis but to love a king.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: That’s soon performed because I am a subject.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, then, thy husband’s lands I freely give thee.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: I take my leave with many thousand thanks.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The match is made; she seals it with a cursy.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But stay thee; ’tis the fruits of love I mean.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: The fruits of love I mean, my loving liege.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Ay, but, I fear me, in another sense.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: What love, think’st thou, I sue so much to get?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: My love till death, my humble thanks, my prayers,

speaker: LADY GREY
text: That love which virtue begs and virtue grants.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: No, by my troth, I did not mean such love.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why, then, you mean not as I thought you did.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But now you partly may perceive my mind.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: My mind will never grant what I perceive

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Your Highness aims at, if I aim aright.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: To tell thee plain, I aim to lie with thee.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: To tell you plain, I had rather lie in prison.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, then, thou shalt not have thy husband’s lands.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why, then, mine honesty shall be my dower,

speaker: LADY GREY
text: For by that loss I will not purchase them.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Therein thou wrong’st thy children mightily.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Herein your Highness wrongs both them and me.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: But, mighty lord, this merry inclination

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Accords not with the sadness of my suit.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Please you dismiss me either with ay or no.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Ay, if thou wilt say “ay” to my request;

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: No, if thou dost say “no” to my demand.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Then no, my lord; my suit is at an end.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The widow likes him not; she knits her brows.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He is the bluntest wooer in Christendom.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Her looks doth argue her replete with modesty;

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Her words doth show her wit incomparable;

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: All her perfections challenge sovereignty.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: One way or other, she is for a king,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And she shall be my love or else my queen.—

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Say that King Edward take thee for his queen?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: ’Tis better said than done, my gracious lord.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: I am a subject fit to jest withal,

speaker: LADY GREY
text: But far unfit to be a sovereign.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Sweet widow, by my state I swear to thee

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: I speak no more than what my soul intends,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And that is, to enjoy thee for my love.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: And that is more than I will yield unto.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: I know I am too mean to be your queen

speaker: LADY GREY
text: And yet too good to be your concubine.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You cavil, widow; I did mean my queen.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: ’Twill grieve your Grace my sons should call you father.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: No more than when my daughters call thee mother.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Thou art a widow and thou hast some children,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And, by God’s mother, I, being but a bachelor,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Have other some. Why, ’tis a happy thing

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: To be the father unto many sons.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Answer no more, for thou shalt be my queen.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The ghostly father now hath done his shrift.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: When he was made a shriver, ’twas for shift.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Brothers, you muse what chat we two have had.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The widow likes it not, for she looks very sad.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You’d think it strange if I should marry her.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To who, my lord?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, Clarence, to myself.

speaker: RICHARD

speaker: EMILIA
text: Some cogging, cozening slave, to get some office,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Have not devised this slander. I will be hanged else.

speaker: IAGO
text: Fie, there is no such man. It is impossible.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If any such there be, heaven pardon him.

speaker: EMILIA
text: A halter pardon him, and hell gnaw his bones!

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why should he call her “whore”? Who keeps her company?

speaker: EMILIA
text: What place? What time? What form? What likelihood?

speaker: EMILIA
text: The Moor’s abused by some most villainous knave,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Some base notorious knave, some scurvy fellow.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O heaven, that such companions thou ’dst unfold,

speaker: EMILIA
text: And put in every honest hand a whip

speaker: EMILIA
text: To lash the rascals naked through the world,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Even from the east to th’ west!

speaker: IAGO
text: Speak within door.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O, fie upon them! Some such squire he was

speaker: EMILIA
text: That turned your wit the seamy side without

speaker: EMILIA
text: And made you to suspect me with the Moor.

speaker: IAGO
text: You are a fool. Go to!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Alas, Iago,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: What shall I do to win my lord again?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Good friend, go to him. For by this light of heaven,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I know not how I lost him. Here I kneel.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If e’er my will did trespass ’gainst his love,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Either in discourse of thought or actual deed,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Or that mine eyes, mine ears, or any sense

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Delighted them in any other form,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Or that I do not yet, and ever did,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And ever will—though he do shake me off

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: To beggarly divorcement—love him dearly,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Comfort forswear me! Unkindness may do much,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And his unkindness may defeat my life,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: But never taint my love. I cannot say “whore”—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: It does abhor me now I speak the word.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: To do the act that might the addition earn,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Not the world’s mass of vanity could make me.

speaker: IAGO
text: I pray you be content. ’Tis but his humor.

speaker: IAGO
text: The business of the state does him offense,

speaker: IAGO
text: And he does chide with you.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If ’twere no other—

speaker: IAGO
text: It is but so, I warrant.

speaker: IAGO
text: Hark how these instruments summon to supper.

speaker: IAGO
text: The messengers of Venice stays the meat.

speaker: IAGO
text: Go in and weep not. All things shall be well.

speaker: IAGO
text: How now, Roderigo?

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I do not find

speaker: RODERIGO
text: That thou deal’st justly with me.

speaker: IAGO
text: What in the contrary?

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Every day thou daff’st me with some device,

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Iago, and rather, as it seems to me now,

speaker: RODERIGO
text: keep’st from me all conveniency than suppliest me

speaker: RODERIGO
text: with the least advantage of hope. I will indeed no

speaker: RODERIGO
text: longer endure it. Nor am I yet persuaded to put up

speaker: RODERIGO
text: in peace what already I have foolishly suffered.

speaker: IAGO
text: Will you hear me, Roderigo?

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Faith, I have heard too much, and your

speaker: RODERIGO
text: words and performances are no kin together.

speaker: IAGO
text: You charge me most unjustly.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: With naught but truth. I have wasted myself

speaker: RODERIGO
text: out of my means. The jewels you have had

speaker: RODERIGO
text: from me to deliver to Desdemona would half have

speaker: RODERIGO
text: corrupted a votaress. You have told me she hath

speaker: RODERIGO
text: received them, and returned me expectations and

speaker: RODERIGO
text: comforts of sudden respect and acquaintance, but I

speaker: RODERIGO
text: find none.

speaker: IAGO
text: Well, go to! Very well.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: “Very well.” “Go to!” I cannot go to, man,

speaker: RODERIGO
text: nor ’tis not very well! By this hand, I say ’tis very

speaker: RODERIGO
text: scurvy, and begin to find myself fopped in it.

speaker: IAGO
text: Very well.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I tell you ’tis not very well! I will make

speaker: RODERIGO
text: myself known to Desdemona. If she will return me

speaker: RODERIGO
text: my jewels, I will give over my suit and repent my

speaker: RODERIGO
text: unlawful solicitation. If not, assure yourself I will

speaker: RODERIGO
text: seek satisfaction of you.

speaker: IAGO
text: You have said now.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Ay, and said nothing but what I protest

speaker: RODERIGO
text: intendment of doing.

speaker: IAGO
text: Why, now I see there’s mettle in thee, and even

speaker: IAGO
text: from this instant do build on thee a better opinion

speaker: IAGO
text: than ever before. Give me thy hand, Roderigo.

speaker: IAGO
text: Thou hast taken against me a most just exception,

speaker: IAGO
text: but yet I protest I have dealt most directly in thy

speaker: IAGO
text: affair.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: It hath not appeared.

speaker: IAGO
text: I grant indeed it hath not appeared, and your

speaker: IAGO
text: suspicion is not without wit and judgment. But,

speaker: IAGO
text: Roderigo, if thou hast that in thee indeed which I

speaker: IAGO
text: have greater reason to believe now than ever—I

speaker: IAGO
text: mean purpose, courage, and valor—this night show

speaker: IAGO
text: it. If thou the next night following enjoy not Desdemona,

speaker: IAGO
text: take me from this world with treachery and

speaker: IAGO
text: devise engines for my life.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Well, what is it? Is it within reason and

speaker: RODERIGO
text: compass?

speaker: IAGO
text: Sir, there is especial commission come from

speaker: IAGO
text: Venice to depute Cassio in Othello’s place.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Is that true? Why, then, Othello and Desdemona

speaker: RODERIGO
text: return again to Venice.

speaker: IAGO
text: O, no. He goes into Mauritania and takes away

speaker: IAGO
text: with him the fair Desdemona, unless his abode be

speaker: IAGO
text: lingered here by some accident—wherein none

speaker: IAGO
text: can be so determinate as the removing of Cassio.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: How do you mean, removing him?

speaker: IAGO
text: Why, by making him uncapable of Othello’s

speaker: IAGO
text: place: knocking out his brains.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: And that you would have me to do?

speaker: IAGO
text: Ay, if you dare do yourself a profit and a right. He

speaker: IAGO
text: sups tonight with a harlotry, and thither will I go to

speaker: IAGO
text: him. He knows not yet of his honorable fortune. If

speaker: IAGO
text: you will watch his going thence (which I will

speaker: IAGO
text: fashion to fall out between twelve and one), you may

speaker: IAGO
text: take him at your pleasure. I will be near to second

speaker: IAGO
text: your attempt, and he shall fall between us. Come,

speaker: IAGO
text: stand not amazed at it, but go along with me. I will

speaker: IAGO
text: show you such a necessity in his death that you shall

speaker: IAGO
text: think yourself bound to put it on him. It is now high

speaker: IAGO
text: supper time, and the night grows to waste. About it!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I will hear further reason for this.

speaker: IAGO
text: And you shall be satisfied.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: I do beseech you, sir, trouble yourself no further.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O, pardon me, ’twill do me good to walk.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Madam, good night. I humbly thank your Ladyship.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Your Honor is most welcome.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Will you walk, sir?—O, Desdemona—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Get you to bed on th’ instant. I will be

speaker: OTHELLO
text: returned forthwith. Dismiss your attendant there.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Look ’t be done.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I will, my lord.

speaker: EMILIA
text: How goes it now? He looks gentler than he did.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: He says he will return incontinent,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And hath commanded me to go to bed,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And bade me to dismiss you.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Dismiss me?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: It was his bidding. Therefore, good Emilia,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Give me my nightly wearing, and adieu.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: We must not now displease him.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I would you had never seen him.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: So would not I. My love doth so approve him

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: That even his stubbornness, his checks, his frowns—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Prithee, unpin me—have grace and favor in them.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I have laid those sheets you bade me on the bed.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: All’s one. Good faith, how foolish are our minds!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If I do die before thee, prithee, shroud me

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: In one of those same sheets.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Come, come, you talk!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My mother had a maid called Barbary.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: She was in love, and he she loved proved mad

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And did forsake her. She had a song of willow,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: An old thing ’twas, but it expressed her fortune,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And she died singing it. That song tonight

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Will not go from my mind. I have much to do

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: But to go hang my head all at one side

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And sing it like poor Barbary. Prithee, dispatch.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Shall I go fetch your nightgown?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: No, unpin me here.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: This Lodovico is a proper man.

speaker: EMILIA
text: A very handsome man.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: He speaks well.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I know a lady in Venice would have walked

speaker: EMILIA
text: barefoot to Palestine for a touch of his nether lip.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: The poor soul sat sighing by a sycamore tree,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing all a green willow.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Her hand on her bosom, her head on her knee,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing willow, willow, willow.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: The fresh streams ran by her and murmured her moans,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing willow, willow, willow;

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Her salt tears fell from her, and softened the stones—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Lay by these.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing willow, willow, willow.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Prithee hie thee! He’ll come anon.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing all a green willow must be my garland.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Let nobody blame him, his scorn I approve.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Nay, that’s not next. Hark, who is ’t that knocks?

speaker: EMILIA
text: It’s the wind.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I called my love false love, but what said he then?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Sing willow, willow, willow.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If I court more women, you’ll couch with more men.—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: So, get thee gone. Good night. Mine eyes do itch;

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Doth that bode weeping?

speaker: EMILIA
text: ’Tis neither here nor there.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I have heard it said so. O these men, these men!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Dost thou in conscience think—tell me, Emilia—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: That there be women do abuse their husbands

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: In such gross kind?

speaker: EMILIA
text: There be some such, no question.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why, would not you?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: No, by this heavenly light!

speaker: EMILIA
text: Nor I neither, by this heavenly light.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I might do ’t as well i’ th’ dark.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

speaker: EMILIA
text: The world’s a huge thing. It is a great price

speaker: EMILIA
text: for a small vice.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: In troth, I think thou wouldst not.

speaker: EMILIA
text: In troth, I think I should, and undo ’t when I

speaker: EMILIA
text: had done it. Marry, I would not do such a thing for

speaker: EMILIA
text: a joint ring, nor for measures of lawn, nor for

speaker: EMILIA
text: gowns, petticoats, nor caps, nor any petty exhibition.

speaker: EMILIA
text: But for the whole world—’Uds pity! Who

speaker: EMILIA
text: would not make her husband a cuckold to make

speaker: EMILIA
text: him a monarch? I should venture purgatory for ’t.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Beshrew me if I would do such a wrong

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: for the whole world!

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why, the wrong is but a wrong i’ th’ world;

speaker: EMILIA
text: and, having the world for your labor, ’tis a wrong in

speaker: EMILIA
text: your own world, and you might quickly make it

speaker: EMILIA
text: right.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I do not think there is any such woman.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Yes, a dozen; and as many to th’ vantage as

speaker: EMILIA
text: would store the world they played for.

speaker: EMILIA
text: But I do think it is their husbands’ faults

speaker: EMILIA
text: If wives do fall. Say that they slack their duties,

speaker: EMILIA
text: And pour our treasures into foreign laps;

speaker: EMILIA
text: Or else break out in peevish jealousies,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Throwing restraint upon us. Or say they strike us,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Or scant our former having in despite.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why, we have galls, and though we have some grace,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Yet have we some revenge. Let husbands know

speaker: EMILIA
text: Their wives have sense like them. They see, and smell,

speaker: EMILIA
text: And have their palates both for sweet and sour,

speaker: EMILIA
text: As husbands have. What is it that they do

speaker: EMILIA
text: When they change us for others? Is it sport?

speaker: EMILIA
text: I think it is. And doth affection breed it?

speaker: EMILIA
text: I think it doth. Is ’t frailty that thus errs?

speaker: EMILIA
text: It is so too. And have not we affections,

speaker: EMILIA
text: Desires for sport, and frailty, as men have?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Then let them use us well. Else let them know,

speaker: EMILIA
text: The ills we do, their ills instruct us so.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Good night, good night. God me such uses send,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Not to pick bad from bad, but by bad mend.

speaker: IAGO
text: Here, stand behind this bulk. Straight will he come.

speaker: IAGO
text: Wear thy good rapier bare, and put it home.

speaker: IAGO
text: Quick, quick! Fear nothing. I’ll be at thy elbow.

speaker: IAGO
text: It makes us or it mars us—think on that,

speaker: IAGO
text: And fix most firm thy resolution.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Be near at hand. I may miscarry in ’t.

speaker: IAGO
text: Here, at thy hand. Be bold and take thy stand.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I have no great devotion to the deed,

speaker: RODERIGO
text: And yet he hath given me satisfying reasons.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: ’Tis but a man gone. Forth, my sword! He dies.

speaker: IAGO
text: I have rubbed this young quat almost to the sense,

speaker: IAGO
text: And he grows angry. Now, whether he kill Cassio,

speaker: IAGO
text: Or Cassio him, or each do kill the other,

speaker: IAGO
text: Every way makes my gain. Live Roderigo,

speaker: IAGO
text: He calls me to a restitution large

speaker: IAGO
text: Of gold and jewels that I bobbed from him

speaker: IAGO
text: As gifts to Desdemona.

speaker: IAGO
text: It must not be. If Cassio do remain,

speaker: IAGO
text: He hath a daily beauty in his life

speaker: IAGO
text: That makes me ugly. And besides, the Moor

speaker: IAGO
text: May unfold me to him. There stand I in much peril.

speaker: IAGO
text: No, he must die. Be ’t so. I hear him coming.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I know his gait. ’Tis he!—Villain, thou diest!

speaker: CASSIO
text: That thrust had been mine enemy indeed

speaker: CASSIO
text: But that my coat is better than thou know’st.

speaker: CASSIO
text: I will make proof of thine.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, I am slain!

speaker: CASSIO
text: I am maimed forever! Help, ho! Murder, murder!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: The voice of Cassio! Iago keeps his word.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, villain that I am!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: It is even so.

speaker: CASSIO
text: O, help ho! Light! A surgeon!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: ’Tis he! O brave Iago, honest and just,

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That hast such noble sense of thy friend’s wrong!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Thou teachest me.—Minion, your dear lies dead,

speaker: OTHELLO
text: And your unblest fate hies. Strumpet, I come.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Forth of my heart those charms, thine eyes, are blotted.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Thy bed, lust-stained, shall with lust’s blood be spotted.

speaker: CASSIO
text: What ho! No watch? No passage? Murder, murder!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: ’Tis some mischance. The voice is very direful.

speaker: CASSIO
text: O, help!

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Hark!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O wretched villain!

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Two or three groan. ’Tis heavy night.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: These may be counterfeits. Let’s think ’t unsafe

speaker: LODOVICO
text: To come in to the cry without more help.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Nobody come? Then shall I bleed to death.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Hark!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Here’s one comes in his shirt, with light and weapons.

speaker: IAGO
text: Who’s there? Whose noise is this that cries on murder?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: We do not know.

speaker: IAGO
text: Did not you hear a cry?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Here, here! For heaven’s sake, help me!

speaker: IAGO
text: What’s the matter?

speaker: GRATIANO
text: This is Othello’s ancient, as I take it.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: The same indeed, a very valiant fellow.

speaker: IAGO
text: What are you here that cry so grievously?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Iago? O, I am spoiled, undone by villains.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Give me some help!

speaker: IAGO
text: O me, lieutenant! What villains have done this?

speaker: CASSIO
text: I think that one of them is hereabout

speaker: CASSIO
text: And cannot make away.

speaker: IAGO
text: O treacherous villains!

speaker: IAGO
text: What are you there?

speaker: IAGO
text: Come in, and give some help.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, help me here!

speaker: CASSIO
text: That’s one of them.

speaker: IAGO
text: O murd’rous slave! O villain!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O damned Iago! O inhuman dog!

speaker: IAGO
text: Kill men i’ th’ dark?—Where be these bloody thieves?

speaker: IAGO
text: How silent is this town! Ho, murder, murder!—

speaker: IAGO
text: What may you be? Are you of good or evil?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: As you shall prove us, praise us.

speaker: IAGO
text: Signior Lodovico?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: He, sir.

speaker: IAGO
text: I cry you mercy. Here’s Cassio hurt by villains.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Cassio?

speaker: IAGO
text: How is ’t, brother?

speaker: CASSIO
text: My leg is cut in two.

speaker: IAGO
text: Marry, heaven forbid!

speaker: IAGO
text: Light, gentlemen. I’ll bind it with my shirt.

speaker: BIANCA
text: What is the matter, ho? Who is ’t that cried?

speaker: IAGO
text: Who is ’t that cried?

speaker: BIANCA
text: O, my dear Cassio,

speaker: BIANCA
text: My sweet Cassio! O Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

speaker: IAGO
text: O notable strumpet! Cassio, may you suspect

speaker: IAGO
text: Who they should be that have thus mangled you?

speaker: CASSIO
text: No.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: I am sorry to find you thus; I have been to seek you.

speaker: IAGO
text: Lend me a garter. So.—O for a chair

speaker: IAGO
text: To bear him easily hence!

speaker: BIANCA
text: Alas, he faints. O, Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

speaker: IAGO
text: Gentlemen all, I do suspect this trash

speaker: IAGO
text: To be a party in this injury.—

speaker: IAGO
text: Patience awhile, good Cassio.—Come, come;

speaker: IAGO
text: Lend me a light. Know we this face or no?

speaker: IAGO
text: Alas, my friend and my dear countryman

speaker: IAGO
text: Roderigo? No! Yes, sure. O heaven, Roderigo!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: What, of Venice?

speaker: IAGO
text: Even he, sir. Did you know him?

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Know him? Ay.

speaker: IAGO
text: Signior Gratiano? I cry your gentle pardon.

speaker: IAGO
text: These bloody accidents must excuse my manners

speaker: IAGO
text: That so neglected you.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: I am glad to see you.

speaker: IAGO
text: How do you, Cassio?—O, a chair, a chair!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Roderigo?

speaker: IAGO
text: He, he, ’tis he! O, that’s well said; the chair.—

speaker: IAGO
text: Some good man bear him carefully from hence.

speaker: IAGO
text: I’ll fetch the General’s surgeon.— For you, mistress,

speaker: IAGO
text: Save you your labor.—He that lies slain here, Cassio,

speaker: IAGO
text: Was my dear friend. What malice was between you?

speaker: CASSIO
text: None in the world. Nor do I know the man.

speaker: IAGO
text: What, look you pale?—O, bear him out o’ th’ air.

speaker: IAGO
text: Stay you, good gentlemen.—Look you pale, mistress?—

speaker: IAGO
text: Do you perceive the gastness of her eye?—

speaker: IAGO
text: Nay, if you stare, we shall hear more anon.—

speaker: IAGO
text: Behold her well. I pray you, look upon her.

speaker: IAGO
text: Do you see, gentlemen? Nay, guiltiness will speak

speaker: IAGO
text: Though tongues were out of use.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Alas, what is the matter? What is the matter, husband?

speaker: IAGO
text: Cassio hath here been set on in the dark
