text: Now they believe it and withal whet me

speaker: RICHARD
text: To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey;

speaker: RICHARD
text: But then I sigh and, with a piece of scripture,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Tell them that God bids us do good for evil;

speaker: RICHARD
text: And thus I clothe my naked villainy

speaker: RICHARD
text: With odd old ends stol’n forth of Holy Writ,

speaker: RICHARD
text: And seem a saint when most I play the devil.

speaker: RICHARD
text: But soft, here come my executioners.—

speaker: RICHARD
text: How now, my hardy, stout, resolvèd mates?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Are you now going to dispatch this thing?

speaker: MURDERER
text: We are, my lord, and come to have the warrant

speaker: MURDERER
text: That we may be admitted where he is.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Well thought upon. I have it here about me.

speaker: RICHARD
text: When you have done, repair to Crosby Place.

speaker: RICHARD
text: But, sirs, be sudden in the execution,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Withal obdurate; do not hear him plead,

speaker: RICHARD
text: For Clarence is well-spoken and perhaps

speaker: RICHARD
text: May move your hearts to pity if you mark him.

speaker: MURDERER
text: Tut, tut, my lord, we will not stand to prate.

speaker: MURDERER
text: Talkers are no good doers. Be assured

speaker: MURDERER
text: We go to use our hands and not our tongues.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Your eyes drop millstones when fools’ eyes fall tears.

speaker: RICHARD
text: I like you lads. About your business straight.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Go, go, dispatch.

speaker: MURDERERS
text: We will, my noble lord.

speaker: KEEPER
text: Why looks your Grace so heavily today?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, I have passed a miserable night,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: So full of fearful dreams, of ugly sights,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That, as I am a Christian faithful man,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I would not spend another such a night

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Though ’twere to buy a world of happy days,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: So full of dismal terror was the time.

speaker: KEEPER
text: What was your dream, my lord? I pray you tell me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Methoughts that I had broken from the Tower

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And was embarked to cross to Burgundy,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And in my company my brother Gloucester,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Who from my cabin tempted me to walk

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Upon the hatches. Thence we looked toward England

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And cited up a thousand heavy times,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: During the wars of York and Lancaster,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That had befall’n us. As we paced along

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Upon the giddy footing of the hatches,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Methought that Gloucester stumbled, and in falling

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Struck me, that thought to stay him, overboard

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Into the tumbling billows of the main.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O Lord, methought what pain it was to drown,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: What dreadful noise of waters in my ears,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: What sights of ugly death within my eyes.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Methoughts I saw a thousand fearful wracks,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: A thousand men that fishes gnawed upon,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Wedges of gold, great anchors, heaps of pearl,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Inestimable stones, unvalued jewels,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: All scattered in the bottom of the sea.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Some lay in dead men’s skulls, and in the holes

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Where eyes did once inhabit, there were crept—

speaker: CLARENCE
text: As ’twere in scorn of eyes—reflecting gems,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That wooed the slimy bottom of the deep

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And mocked the dead bones that lay scattered by.

speaker: KEEPER
text: Had you such leisure in the time of death

speaker: KEEPER
text: To gaze upon these secrets of the deep?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Methought I had, and often did I strive

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To yield the ghost, but still the envious flood

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Stopped in my soul and would not let it forth

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To find the empty, vast, and wand’ring air,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: But smothered it within my panting bulk,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Who almost burst to belch it in the sea.

speaker: KEEPER
text: Awaked you not in this sore agony?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: No, no, my dream was lengthened after life.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, then began the tempest to my soul.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I passed, methought, the melancholy flood,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: With that sour ferryman which poets write of,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Unto the kingdom of perpetual night.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: The first that there did greet my stranger-soul

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Was my great father-in-law, renownèd Warwick,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Who spake aloud “What scourge for perjury

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Can this dark monarchy afford false Clarence?”

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And so he vanished. Then came wand’ring by

speaker: CLARENCE
text: A shadow like an angel, with bright hair

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Dabbled in blood, and he shrieked out aloud

speaker: CLARENCE
text: “Clarence is come—false, fleeting, perjured Clarence,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That stabbed me in the field by Tewkesbury.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Seize on him, furies. Take him unto torment.”

speaker: CLARENCE
text: With that, methoughts, a legion of foul fiends

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Environed me and howlèd in mine ears

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Such hideous cries that with the very noise

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I trembling waked, and for a season after

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Could not believe but that I was in hell,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Such terrible impression made my dream.

speaker: KEEPER
text: No marvel, lord, though it affrighted you.

speaker: KEEPER
text: I am afraid, methinks, to hear you tell it.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Ah keeper, keeper, I have done these things,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That now give evidence against my soul,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: For Edward’s sake, and see how he requites me.—

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O God, if my deep prayers cannot appease thee,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: But thou wilt be avenged on my misdeeds,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Yet execute thy wrath in me alone!

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, spare my guiltless wife and my poor children!—

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Keeper, I prithee sit by me awhile.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: My soul is heavy, and I fain would sleep.

speaker: KEEPER
text: I will, my lord. God give your Grace good rest.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: Sorrow breaks seasons and reposing hours,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: Makes the night morning, and the noontide night.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: Princes have but their titles for their glories,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: An outward honor for an inward toil,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: And, for unfelt imaginations,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: They often feel a world of restless cares,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: So that between their titles and low name

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: There’s nothing differs but the outward fame.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Ho, who’s here?

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: What wouldst thou, fellow? And how cam’st thou hither?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: I would speak with Clarence, and I

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: came hither on my legs.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: What, so brief?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: ’Tis better, sir, than to be tedious.—

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Let him see our commission, and talk no more.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: I am in this commanded to deliver

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: The noble Duke of Clarence to your hands.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: I will not reason what is meant hereby

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: Because I will be guiltless from the meaning.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: There lies the Duke asleep, and there the keys.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: I’ll to the King and signify to him

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text: That thus I have resigned to you my charge.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: You may, sir. ’Tis a point of wisdom.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Fare you well.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: What, shall I stab him as he

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: sleeps?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: No. He’ll say ’twas done cowardly,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: when he wakes.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Why, he shall never wake until the

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: great Judgment Day.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Why, then he’ll say we stabbed him

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: sleeping.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: The urging of that word “judgment”

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: hath bred a kind of remorse in me.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: What, art thou afraid?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Not to kill him, having a warrant,

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: but to be damned for killing him, from the which

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: no warrant can defend me.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: I thought thou hadst been resolute.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: So I am—to let him live.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: I’ll back to the Duke of Gloucester

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: and tell him so.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Nay, I prithee stay a little. I hope

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: this passionate humor of mine will change. It was

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: wont to hold me but while one tells twenty.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: How dost thou feel thyself now?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Faith, some certain dregs of conscience

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: are yet within me.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Remember our reward when the

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: deed’s done.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Zounds, he dies! I had forgot the

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: reward.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Where’s thy conscience now?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: O, in the Duke of Gloucester’s

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: purse.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: When he opens his purse to give us

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: our reward, thy conscience flies out.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: ’Tis no matter. Let it go. There’s

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: few or none will entertain it.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: What if it come to thee again?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: I’ll not meddle with it. It makes a

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: man a coward: a man cannot steal but it accuseth

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: him; a man cannot swear but it checks him; a man

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: cannot lie with his neighbor’s wife but it detects

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: him. ’Tis a blushing, shamefaced spirit that mutinies

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: in a man’s bosom. It fills a man full of

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: obstacles. It made me once restore a purse of gold

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: that by chance I found. It beggars any man that

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: keeps it. It is turned out of towns and cities for a

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: dangerous thing, and every man that means to live

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: well endeavors to trust to himself and live without it.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Zounds, ’tis even now at my elbow,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: persuading me not to kill the Duke.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Take the devil in thy mind, and

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: believe him not. He would insinuate with thee but

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: to make thee sigh.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: I am strong-framed. He cannot prevail

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: with me.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Spoke like a tall man that respects

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: thy reputation. Come, shall we fall to work?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Take him on the costard with the

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: hilts of thy sword, and then throw him into the

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: malmsey butt in the next room.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: O, excellent device—and make a

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: sop of him!

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Soft, he wakes.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Strike!

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: No, we’ll reason with him.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Where art thou, keeper? Give me a cup of wine.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: You shall have wine enough, my lord, anon.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: In God’s name, what art thou?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: A man, as you are.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: But not, as I am, royal.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Nor you, as we are, loyal.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Thy voice is thunder, but thy looks are humble.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: My voice is now the King’s, my looks mine own.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: How darkly and how deadly dost thou speak!

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Your eyes do menace me. Why look you pale?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Who sent you hither? Wherefore do you come?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: To, to, to—

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To murder me?

speaker: BOTH
text: Ay, ay.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: You scarcely have the hearts to tell me so

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And therefore cannot have the hearts to do it.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Wherein, my friends, have I offended you?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Offended us you have not, but the King.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I shall be reconciled to him again.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Never, my lord. Therefore prepare to die.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Are you drawn forth among a world of men

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To slay the innocent? What is my offense?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Where is the evidence that doth accuse me?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: What lawful quest have given their verdict up

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Unto the frowning judge? Or who pronounced

speaker: CLARENCE
text: The bitter sentence of poor Clarence’ death

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Before I be convict by course of law?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To threaten me with death is most unlawful.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I charge you, as you hope to have redemption,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: By Christ’s dear blood shed for our grievous sins,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That you depart, and lay no hands on me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: The deed you undertake is damnable.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: What we will do, we do upon command.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: And he that hath commanded is our king.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Erroneous vassals, the great King of kings

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Hath in the table of His law commanded

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That thou shalt do no murder. Will you then

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Spurn at His edict and fulfill a man’s?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Take heed, for He holds vengeance in His hand

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To hurl upon their heads that break His law.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: And that same vengeance doth He hurl on thee

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: For false forswearing and for murder too.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Thou didst receive the sacrament to fight

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: In quarrel of the House of Lancaster.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: And, like a traitor to the name of God,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Didst break that vow, and with thy treacherous blade

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Unrippedst the bowels of thy sovereign’s son.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Whom thou wast sworn to cherish and defend.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: How canst thou urge God’s dreadful law to us

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: When thou hast broke it in such dear degree?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Alas! For whose sake did I that ill deed?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: For Edward, for my brother, for his sake.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He sends you not to murder me for this,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: For in that sin he is as deep as I.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: If God will be avengèd for the deed,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, know you yet He doth it publicly!

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Take not the quarrel from His powerful arm;

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He needs no indirect or lawless course

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To cut off those that have offended Him.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Who made thee then a bloody minister

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: When gallant-springing, brave Plantagenet,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: That princely novice, was struck dead by thee?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: My brother’s love, the devil, and my rage.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Thy brother’s love, our duty, and thy faults

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Provoke us hither now to slaughter thee.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: If you do love my brother, hate not me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I am his brother, and I love him well.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: If you are hired for meed, go back again,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And I will send you to my brother Gloucester,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Who shall reward you better for my life

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Than Edward will for tidings of my death.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: You are deceived. Your brother Gloucester hates you.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O no, he loves me, and he holds me dear.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Go you to him from me.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Ay, so we will.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Tell him, when that our princely father York

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Blessed his three sons with his victorious arm,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He little thought of this divided friendship.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Bid Gloucester think of this, and he will weep.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Ay, millstones, as he lessoned us to weep.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, do not slander him, for he is kind.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Right, as snow in harvest. Come, you deceive yourself.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: ’Tis he that sends us to destroy you here.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: It cannot be, for he bewept my fortune,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And hugged me in his arms, and swore with sobs

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That he would labor my delivery.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Why, so he doth, when he delivers you

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: From this Earth’s thralldom to the joys of heaven.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Make peace with God, for you must die, my lord.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Have you that holy feeling in your souls

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To counsel me to make my peace with God,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And are you yet to your own souls so blind

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That you will war with God by murd’ring me?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O sirs, consider: they that set you on

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To do this deed will hate you for the deed.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: What shall we do?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Relent, and save your souls.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Which of you—if you were a prince’s son

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Being pent from liberty, as I am now—

speaker: CLARENCE
text: If two such murderers as yourselves came to you,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Would not entreat for life? Ay, you would beg,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Were you in my distress.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Relent? No. ’Tis cowardly and womanish.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Not to relent is beastly, savage, devilish.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: My friend, I spy some pity in thy looks.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: O, if thine eye be not a flatterer,

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Come thou on my side and entreat for me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: A begging prince what beggar pities not?

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Look behind you, my lord.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Take that, and that. If all this will not do,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: I’ll drown you in the malmsey butt within.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: A bloody deed, and desperately dispatched.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: How fain, like Pilate, would I wash my hands

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Of this most grievous murder.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: How now? What mean’st thou that thou help’st me not?

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: By heavens, the Duke shall know how slack you have been.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: I would he knew that I had saved his brother.

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: Take thou the fee, and tell him what I say,

speaker: SECOND MURDERER
text: For I repent me that the Duke is slain.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: So do not I. Go, coward as thou art.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Well, I’ll go hide the body in some hole

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: Till that the Duke give order for his burial.

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: And when I have my meed, I will away,

speaker: FIRST MURDERER
text: For this will out, and then I must not stay.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, so. Now have I done a good day’s work.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You peers, continue this united league.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: I every day expect an embassage

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: From my Redeemer to redeem me hence,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And more in peace my soul shall part to heaven

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Since I have made my friends at peace on Earth.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Rivers and Hastings, take each other’s hand.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Dissemble not your hatred. Swear your love.

speaker: RIVERS
text: By heaven, my soul is purged from grudging hate,

speaker: RIVERS
text: And with my hand I seal my true heart’s love.

speaker: HASTINGS
text: So thrive I as I truly swear the like.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Take heed you dally not before your king,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Lest He that is the supreme King of kings

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Confound your hidden falsehood and award

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Either of you to be the other’s end.

speaker: HASTINGS
text: So prosper I as I swear perfect love.

speaker: RIVERS
text: And I as I love Hastings with my heart.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Madam, yourself is not exempt from this,—

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Nor you, son Dorset,—Buckingham, nor you.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You have been factious one against the other.—

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Wife, love Lord Hastings. Let him kiss your hand,

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And what you do, do it unfeignedly.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text: There, Hastings, I will never more remember

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text: Our former hatred, so thrive I and mine.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Dorset, embrace him.—Hastings, love Lord Marquess.

speaker: DORSET
text: This interchange of love, I here protest,

speaker: DORSET
text: Upon my part shall be inviolable.

speaker: HASTINGS
text: And so swear I.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Now, princely Buckingham, seal thou this league

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: With thy embracements to my wife’s allies

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And make me happy in your unity.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: Whenever Buckingham doth turn his hate

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: Upon your Grace, but with all duteous love

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: Doth cherish you and yours, God punish me

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: With hate in those where I expect most love.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: When I have most need to employ a friend,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: And most assurèd that he is a friend,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: Deep, hollow, treacherous, and full of guile

speaker: RICHARD
text: What shall I say more than I have inferred?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Remember whom you are to cope withal,

speaker: RICHARD
text: A sort of vagabonds, rascals, and runaways,

speaker: RICHARD
text: A scum of Bretons and base lackey peasants,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Whom their o’ercloyèd country vomits forth

speaker: RICHARD
text: To desperate adventures and assured destruction.

speaker: RICHARD
text: You sleeping safe, they bring to you unrest;

speaker: RICHARD
text: You having lands and blessed with beauteous wives,

speaker: RICHARD
text: They would restrain the one, distain the other.

speaker: RICHARD
text: And who doth lead them but a paltry fellow,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Long kept in Brittany at our mother’s cost,

speaker: RICHARD
text: A milksop, one that never in his life

speaker: RICHARD
text: Felt so much cold as overshoes in snow?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Let’s whip these stragglers o’er the seas again,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Lash hence these overweening rags of France,

speaker: RICHARD
text: These famished beggars weary of their lives,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Who, but for dreaming on this fond exploit,

speaker: RICHARD
text: For want of means, poor rats, had hanged themselves.

speaker: RICHARD
text: If we be conquered, let men conquer us,

speaker: RICHARD
text: And not these bastard Bretons, whom our fathers

speaker: RICHARD
text: Have in their own land beaten, bobbed, and thumped,

speaker: RICHARD
text: And in record left them the heirs of shame.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Shall these enjoy our lands, lie with our wives,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Ravish our daughters?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Hark, I hear their drum.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Fight, gentlemen of England.—Fight, bold yeomen.—

speaker: RICHARD
text: Draw, archers; draw your arrows to the head.—

speaker: RICHARD
text: Spur your proud horses hard, and ride in blood.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Amaze the welkin with your broken staves.—

speaker: RICHARD
text: What says Lord Stanley? Will he bring his power?

speaker: MESSENGER
text: My lord, he doth deny to come.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Off with his son George’s head!

speaker: NORFOLK
text: My lord, the enemy is past the marsh.

speaker: NORFOLK
text: After the battle let George Stanley die.

speaker: RICHARD
text: A thousand hearts are great within my bosom.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Advance our standards. Set upon our foes.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Our ancient word of courage, fair Saint George,

speaker: RICHARD
text: Inspire us with the spleen of fiery dragons.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Upon them! Victory sits on our helms.

speaker: CATESBY
text: Rescue, my lord of Norfolk, rescue, rescue!

speaker: CATESBY
text: The King enacts more wonders than a man,

speaker: CATESBY
text: Daring an opposite to every danger.

speaker: CATESBY
text: His horse is slain, and all on foot he fights,

speaker: CATESBY
text: Seeking for Richmond in the throat of death.

speaker: CATESBY
text: Rescue, fair lord, or else the day is lost.

speaker: RICHARD
text: A horse, a horse, my kingdom for a horse!

speaker: CATESBY
text: Withdraw, my lord. I’ll help you to a horse.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Slave, I have set my life upon a cast,

speaker: RICHARD
text: And I will stand the hazard of the die.

speaker: RICHARD
text: I think there be six Richmonds in the field;

speaker: RICHARD
text: Five have I slain today instead of him.

speaker: RICHARD
text: A horse, a horse, my kingdom for a horse!

speaker: RICHMOND
text: God and your arms be praised, victorious friends!

speaker: RICHMOND
text: The day is ours; the bloody dog is dead.

speaker: STANLEY
text: Courageous Richmond, well hast thou acquit thee.

speaker: STANLEY
text: Lo, here this long-usurpèd royalty

speaker: STANLEY
text: From the dead temples of this bloody wretch

speaker: STANLEY
text: Have I plucked off, to grace thy brows withal.

speaker: STANLEY
text: Wear it, enjoy it, and make much of it.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Great God of heaven, say amen to all!

speaker: RICHMOND
text: But tell me, is young George Stanley living?

speaker: STANLEY
text: He is, my lord, and safe in Leicester town,

speaker: STANLEY
text: Whither, if it please you, we may now withdraw us.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: What men of name are slain on either side?

speaker: STANLEY
text: John, Duke of Norfolk, Walter, Lord Ferrers,

speaker: STANLEY
text: Sir Robert Brakenbury, and Sir William Brandon.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Inter their bodies as becomes their births.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Proclaim a pardon to the soldiers fled

speaker: RICHMOND
text: That in submission will return to us.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: And then, as we have ta’en the sacrament,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: We will unite the white rose and the red;

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Smile heaven upon this fair conjunction,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: That long have frowned upon their enmity.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: What traitor hears me and says not “Amen”?

speaker: RICHMOND
text: England hath long been mad and scarred herself:

speaker: RICHMOND
text: The brother blindly shed the brother’s blood;

speaker: RICHMOND
text: The father rashly slaughtered his own son;

speaker: RICHMOND
text: The son, compelled, been butcher to the sire.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: All this divided York and Lancaster,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Divided in their dire division.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: O, now let Richmond and Elizabeth,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: The true succeeders of each royal house,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: By God’s fair ordinance conjoin together,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: And let their heirs, God, if Thy will be so,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Enrich the time to come with smooth-faced peace,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: With smiling plenty and fair prosperous days.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Abate the edge of traitors, gracious Lord,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: That would reduce these bloody days again

speaker: RICHMOND
text: And make poor England weep in streams of blood.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Let them not live to taste this land’s increase,

speaker: RICHMOND
text: That would with treason wound this fair land’s peace.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: Now civil wounds are stopped, peace lives again.

speaker: RICHMOND
text: That she may long live here, God say amen.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Two households, both alike in dignity

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: (In fair Verona, where we lay our scene),

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: From ancient grudge break to new mutiny,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: From forth the fatal loins of these two foes

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: A pair of star-crossed lovers take their life;

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Whose misadventured piteous overthrows

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Doth with their death bury their parents’ strife.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: The fearful passage of their death-marked love

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And the continuance of their parents’ rage,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Which, but their children’s end, naught could remove,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Is now the two hours’ traffic of our stage;

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: The which, if you with patient ears attend,

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: What here shall miss, our toil shall strive to mend.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Gregory, on my word we’ll not carry coals.

speaker: GREGORY
text: No, for then we should be colliers.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: I mean, an we be in choler, we’ll draw.

speaker: GREGORY
text: Ay, while you live, draw your neck out of

speaker: GREGORY
text: collar.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: I strike quickly, being moved.

speaker: GREGORY
text: But thou art not quickly moved to strike.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: A dog of the house of Montague moves me.

speaker: GREGORY
text: To move is to stir, and to be valiant is to

speaker: GREGORY
text: stand. Therefore if thou art moved thou runn’st

speaker: GREGORY
text: away.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: A dog of that house shall move me to stand. I

speaker: SAMPSON
text: will take the wall of any man or maid of Montague’s.

speaker: GREGORY
text: That shows thee a weak slave, for the weakest

speaker: GREGORY
text: goes to the wall.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: ’Tis true, and therefore women, being the

speaker: SAMPSON
text: weaker vessels, are ever thrust to the wall. Therefore

speaker: SAMPSON
text: I will push Montague’s men from the wall and

speaker: SAMPSON
text: thrust his maids to the wall.

speaker: GREGORY
text: The quarrel is between our masters and us

speaker: GREGORY
text: their men.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: ’Tis all one. I will show myself a tyrant.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: When I have fought with the men, I will be civil

speaker: SAMPSON
text: with the maids; I will cut off their heads.

speaker: GREGORY
text: The heads of the maids?

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Ay, the heads of the maids, or their maidenheads.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Take it in what sense thou wilt.

speaker: GREGORY
text: They must take it in sense that feel it.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Me they shall feel while I am able to stand,

speaker: SAMPSON
text: and ’tis known I am a pretty piece of flesh.

speaker: GREGORY
text: ’Tis well thou art not fish; if thou hadst, thou

speaker: GREGORY
text: hadst been poor-john. Draw thy tool. Here comes

speaker: GREGORY
text: of the house of Montagues.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: My naked weapon is out. Quarrel, I will back

speaker: SAMPSON
text: thee.

speaker: GREGORY
text: How? Turn thy back and run?

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Fear me not.

speaker: GREGORY
text: No, marry. I fear thee!

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Let us take the law of our sides; let them

speaker: SAMPSON
text: begin.

speaker: GREGORY
text: I will frown as I pass by, and let them take it

speaker: GREGORY
text: as they list.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Nay, as they dare. I will bite my thumb at

speaker: SAMPSON
text: them, which is disgrace to them if they bear it.

speaker: ABRAM
text: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

speaker: SAMPSON
text: I do bite my thumb, sir.

speaker: ABRAM
text: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Is the law of our side if I

speaker: SAMPSON
text: say “Ay”?

speaker: GREGORY
text: No.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: No, sir, I do not bite my thumb at you, sir,

speaker: SAMPSON
text: but I bite my thumb, sir.

speaker: GREGORY
text: Do you quarrel, sir?

speaker: ABRAM
text: Quarrel, sir? No, sir.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: But if you do, sir, I am for you. I serve as

speaker: SAMPSON
text: good a man as you.

speaker: ABRAM
text: No better.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Well, sir.

speaker: GREGORY
text: Say “better”; here comes

speaker: GREGORY
text: one of my master’s kinsmen.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Yes, better, sir.

speaker: ABRAM
text: You lie.

speaker: SAMPSON
text: Draw if you be men.—Gregory, remember

speaker: SAMPSON
text: thy washing blow.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Part, fools!

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Put up your swords. You know not what you do.

speaker: TYBALT
text: What, art thou drawn among these heartless hinds?

speaker: TYBALT
text: Turn thee, Benvolio; look upon thy death.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I do but keep the peace. Put up thy sword,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Or manage it to part these men with me.

speaker: TYBALT
text: What, drawn and talk of peace? I hate the word

speaker: TYBALT
text: As I hate hell, all Montagues, and thee.

speaker: TYBALT
text: Have at thee, coward!

speaker: CITIZENS
text: Clubs, bills, and partisans! Strike! Beat them down!

speaker: CITIZENS
text: Down with the Capulets! Down with the Montagues!

speaker: CAPULET
text: What noise is this? Give me my long sword, ho!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text: A crutch, a crutch! Why call you for a sword?

speaker: CAPULET
text: My sword, I say. Old Montague is come

speaker: CAPULET
text: And flourishes his blade in spite of me.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Thou villain Capulet!—Hold me not; let me go.

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
text: Thou shalt not stir one foot to seek a foe.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Rebellious subjects, enemies to peace,

speaker: PRINCE
text: Profaners of this neighbor-stainèd steel—

speaker: PRINCE
text: Will they not hear?—What ho! You men, you beasts,

speaker: PRINCE
text: That quench the fire of your pernicious rage

speaker: PRINCE
text: With purple fountains issuing from your veins:

speaker: PRINCE
text: On pain of torture, from those bloody hands

speaker: PRINCE
text: Throw your mistempered weapons to the ground,

speaker: PRINCE
text: And hear the sentence of your movèd prince.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Three civil brawls bred of an airy word

speaker: PRINCE
text: By thee, old Capulet, and Montague,

speaker: PRINCE
text: Have thrice disturbed the quiet of our streets

speaker: PRINCE
text: And made Verona’s ancient citizens

speaker: PRINCE
text: Cast by their grave-beseeming ornaments

speaker: PRINCE
text: To wield old partisans in hands as old,

speaker: PRINCE
text: Cankered with peace, to part your cankered hate.

speaker: PRINCE
text: If ever you disturb our streets again,

speaker: PRINCE
text: Your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.

speaker: PRINCE
text: For this time all the rest depart away.

speaker: PRINCE
text: You, Capulet, shall go along with me,

speaker: PRINCE
text: And, Montague, come you this afternoon

speaker: PRINCE
text: To know our farther pleasure in this case,

speaker: PRINCE
text: To old Free-town, our common judgment-place.

speaker: PRINCE
text: Once more, on pain of death, all men depart.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Who set this ancient quarrel new abroach?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Speak, nephew, were you by when it began?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Here were the servants of your adversary,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: And yours, close fighting ere I did approach.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I drew to part them. In the instant came

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: The fiery Tybalt with his sword prepared,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Which, as he breathed defiance to my ears,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: He swung about his head and cut the winds,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Who, nothing hurt withal, hissed him in scorn.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: While we were interchanging thrusts and blows

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Came more and more and fought on part and part,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Till the Prince came, who parted either part.

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
text: O, where is Romeo? Saw you him today?

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
text: Right glad I am he was not at this fray.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Madam, an hour before the worshiped sun

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Peered forth the golden window of the east,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: A troubled mind drove me to walk abroad,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Where underneath the grove of sycamore

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: That westward rooteth from this city side,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: So early walking did I see your son.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Towards him I made, but he was ’ware of me

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: And stole into the covert of the wood.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I, measuring his affections by my own

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: (Which then most sought where most might not be found,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Being one too many by my weary self),

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Pursued my humor, not pursuing his,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: And gladly shunned who gladly fled from me.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Many a morning hath he there been seen,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: With tears augmenting the fresh morning’s dew,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Adding to clouds more clouds with his deep sighs.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: But all so soon as the all-cheering sun

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Should in the farthest east begin to draw

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: The shady curtains from Aurora’s bed,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Away from light steals home my heavy son

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: And private in his chamber pens himself,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Shuts up his windows, locks fair daylight out,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: And makes himself an artificial night.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Black and portentous must this humor prove,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Unless good counsel may the cause remove.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: I neither know it nor can learn of him.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Have you importuned him by any means?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Both by myself and many other friends.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: But he, his own affections’ counselor,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Is to himself—I will not say how true,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: But to himself so secret and so close,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: So far from sounding and discovery,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: As is the bud bit with an envious worm

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Ere he can spread his sweet leaves to the air

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Or dedicate his beauty to the same.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Could we but learn from whence his sorrows grow,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: We would as willingly give cure as know.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: See where he comes. So please you, step aside.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I’ll know his grievance or be much denied.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: I would thou wert so happy by thy stay

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: To hear true shrift.—Come, madam, let’s away.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Good morrow, cousin.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Is the day so young?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: But new struck nine.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Ay me, sad hours seem long.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Was that my father that went hence so fast?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: It was. What sadness lengthens Romeo’s hours?

speaker: ROMEO
text: Not having that which, having, makes them short.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: In love?

speaker: ROMEO
text: Out—

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Of love?

speaker: ROMEO
text: Out of her favor where I am in love.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Alas that love, so gentle in his view,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Should be so tyrannous and rough in proof!

speaker: ROMEO
text: Alas that love, whose view is muffled still,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Should without eyes see pathways to his will!

speaker: ROMEO
text: Where shall we dine?—O me! What fray was here?

speaker: ROMEO
text: Yet tell me not, for I have heard it all.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Here’s much to do with hate, but more with love.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Why then, O brawling love, O loving hate,

speaker: ROMEO
text: O anything of nothing first create!

speaker: ROMEO
text: O heavy lightness, serious vanity,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Misshapen chaos of well-seeming forms,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire, sick health,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Still-waking sleep that is not what it is!

speaker: ROMEO
text: This love feel I, that feel no love in this.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Dost thou not laugh?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: No, coz, I rather weep.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Good heart, at what?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: At thy good heart’s oppression.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Why, such is love’s transgression.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Griefs of mine own lie heavy in my breast,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Which thou wilt propagate to have it pressed

speaker: ROMEO
text: With more of thine. This love that thou hast shown

speaker: ROMEO
text: Doth add more grief to too much of mine own.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Love is a smoke made with the fume of sighs;

speaker: ROMEO
text: Being purged, a fire sparkling in lovers’ eyes;

speaker: ROMEO
text: Being vexed, a sea nourished with loving tears.

speaker: ROMEO
text: What is it else? A madness most discreet,

speaker: ROMEO
text: A choking gall, and a preserving sweet.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Farewell, my coz.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Soft, I will go along.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: An if you leave me so, you do me wrong.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Tut, I have lost myself. I am not here.

speaker: ROMEO
text: This is not Romeo. He’s some other where.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Tell me in sadness, who is that you love?

speaker: ROMEO
text: What, shall I groan and tell thee?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Groan? Why, no. But sadly tell me who.

speaker: ROMEO
text: A sick man in sadness makes his will—

speaker: ROMEO
text: A word ill urged to one that is so ill.

speaker: ROMEO
text: In sadness, cousin, I do love a woman.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I aimed so near when I supposed you loved.

speaker: ROMEO
text: A right good markman! And she’s fair I love.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: A right fair mark, fair coz, is soonest hit.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Well in that hit you miss. She’ll not be hit

speaker: ROMEO
text: With Cupid’s arrow. She hath Dian’s wit,

speaker: ROMEO
text: And, in strong proof of chastity well armed,

speaker: ROMEO
text: From love’s weak childish bow she lives uncharmed.

speaker: ROMEO
text: She will not stay the siege of loving terms,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Nor bide th’ encounter of assailing eyes,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Nor ope her lap to saint-seducing gold.

speaker: ROMEO
text: O, she is rich in beauty, only poor

speaker: ROMEO
text: That, when she dies, with beauty dies her store.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Then she hath sworn that she will still live chaste?

speaker: ROMEO
text: She hath, and in that sparing makes huge waste;

speaker: ROMEO
text: For beauty, starved with her severity,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Cuts beauty off from all posterity.

speaker: ROMEO
text: She is too fair, too wise, wisely too fair,

speaker: ROMEO
text: To merit bliss by making me despair.

speaker: ROMEO
text: She hath forsworn to love, and in that vow

speaker: ROMEO
text: Do I live dead, that live to tell it now.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Be ruled by me. Forget to think of her.

speaker: ROMEO
text: O, teach me how I should forget to think!

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: By giving liberty unto thine eyes.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: Examine other beauties.

speaker: ROMEO
text: ’Tis the way

speaker: ROMEO
text: To call hers, exquisite, in question more.

speaker: ROMEO
text: These happy masks that kiss fair ladies’ brows,

speaker: ROMEO
text: Being black, puts us in mind they hide the fair.

speaker: ROMEO
text: He that is strucken blind cannot forget

speaker: ROMEO
text: The precious treasure of his eyesight lost.

speaker: ROMEO
text: Show me a mistress that is passing fair;

speaker: ROMEO
text: What doth her beauty serve but as a note

speaker: ROMEO
text: Where I may read who passed that passing fair?

speaker: ROMEO
text: Farewell. Thou canst not teach me to forget.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text: I’ll pay that doctrine or else die in debt.

speaker: CAPULET
text: But Montague is bound as well as I,

speaker: CAPULET
text: In penalty alike, and ’tis not hard, I think,

speaker: CAPULET
text: For men so old as we to keep the peace.

speaker: PARIS
text: Of honorable reckoning are you both,

speaker: PARIS
text: And pity ’tis you lived at odds so long.

speaker: PARIS
text: But now, my lord, what say you to my suit?

speaker: CAPULET
text: But saying o’er what I have said before.

speaker: CAPULET
text: My child is yet a stranger in the world.

speaker: CAPULET

speaker: EGEON
text: In Syracusa was I born, and wed

speaker: EGEON
text: Unto a woman happy but for me,

speaker: EGEON
text: And by me, had not our hap been bad.

speaker: EGEON
text: With her I lived in joy. Our wealth increased

speaker: EGEON
text: By prosperous voyages I often made

speaker: EGEON
text: To Epidamium, till my factor’s death

speaker: EGEON
text: And the great care of goods at random left

speaker: EGEON
text: Drew me from kind embracements of my spouse;

speaker: EGEON
text: From whom my absence was not six months old

speaker: EGEON
text: Before herself—almost at fainting under

speaker: EGEON
text: The pleasing punishment that women bear—

speaker: EGEON
text: Had made provision for her following me

speaker: EGEON
text: And soon and safe arrivèd where I was.

speaker: EGEON
text: There had she not been long but she became

speaker: EGEON
text: A joyful mother of two goodly sons,

speaker: EGEON
text: And, which was strange, the one so like the other

speaker: EGEON
text: As could not be distinguished but by names.

speaker: EGEON
text: That very hour, and in the selfsame inn,

speaker: EGEON
text: A mean woman was deliverèd

speaker: EGEON
text: Of such a burden, male twins, both alike.

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON
text: I bought and brought up to attend my sons.

speaker: EGEON
text: My wife, not meanly proud of two such boys,

speaker: EGEON
text: Made daily motions for our home return.

speaker: EGEON
text: Unwilling, I agreed. Alas, too soon

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON
text: Yet the incessant weepings of my wife,

speaker: EGEON
text: Weeping before for what she saw must come,

speaker: EGEON
text: And piteous plainings of the pretty babes,

speaker: EGEON
text: That mourned for fashion, ignorant what to fear,

speaker: EGEON
text: Forced me to seek delays for them and me.

speaker: EGEON
text: And this it was, for other means was none:

speaker: EGEON
text: The sailors sought for safety by our boat

speaker: EGEON
text: And left the ship, then sinking-ripe, to us.

speaker: EGEON
text: My wife, more careful for the latter-born,

speaker: EGEON
text: Had fastened him unto a small spare mast,

speaker: EGEON
text: Such as seafaring men provide for storms.

speaker: EGEON
text: To him one of the other twins was bound,

speaker: EGEON
text: Whilst I had been like heedful of the other.

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON
text: Fixing our eyes on whom our care was fixed,

speaker: EGEON
text: Fastened ourselves at either end the mast

speaker: EGEON
text: And, floating straight, obedient to the stream,

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON
text: And by the benefit of his wished light

speaker: EGEON

text: Two ships from far, making amain to us,

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON

speaker: EGEON
