text: As nimble jugglers that deceive the eye,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Dark-working sorcerers that change the mind,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Soul-killing witches that deform the body,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Disguisèd cheaters, prating mountebanks,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And many suchlike liberties of sin.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: If it prove so, I will be gone the sooner.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll to the Centaur to go seek this slave.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I greatly fear my money is not safe.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Neither my husband nor the slave returned

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That in such haste I sent to seek his master?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Sure, Luciana, it is two o’clock.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Perhaps some merchant hath invited him,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: And from the mart he’s somewhere gone to dinner.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Good sister, let us dine, and never fret.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: A man is master of his liberty;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Time is their master, and when they see time

speaker: LUCIANA
text: They’ll go or come. If so, be patient, sister.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Why should their liberty than ours be more?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Because their business still lies out o’ door.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Look when I serve him so, he takes it ill.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: O, know he is the bridle of your will.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: There’s none but asses will be bridled so.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Why, headstrong liberty is lashed with woe.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: There’s nothing situate under heaven’s eye

speaker: LUCIANA
text: But hath his bound in earth, in sea, in sky.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: The beasts, the fishes, and the wingèd fowls

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Are their males’ subjects and at their controls.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Man, more divine, the master of all these,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Lord of the wide world and wild wat’ry seas,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Endued with intellectual sense and souls,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Of more preeminence than fish and fowls,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Are masters to their females, and their lords.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Then let your will attend on their accords.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: This servitude makes you to keep unwed.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Not this, but troubles of the marriage bed.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But, were you wedded, you would bear some sway.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Ere I learn love, I’ll practice to obey.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: How if your husband start some otherwhere?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Till he come home again, I would forbear.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Patience unmoved! No marvel though she pause;

speaker: ADRIANA
text: They can be meek that have no other cause.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: A wretched soul bruised with adversity

speaker: ADRIANA
text: We bid be quiet when we hear it cry,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But were we burdened with like weight of pain,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: As much or more we should ourselves complain.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: So thou, that hast no unkind mate to grieve thee,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: With urging helpless patience would relieve me;

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But if thou live to see like right bereft,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: This fool-begged patience in thee will be left.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Well, I will marry one day, but to try.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Here comes your man. Now is your husband nigh.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Say, is your tardy master now at hand?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Nay, he’s at two hands with me,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: and that my two ears can witness.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Say, didst thou speak with him? Know’st thou his mind?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Ay, ay, he told his mind upon mine ear.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Beshrew his hand, I scarce could understand it.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Spake he so doubtfully thou couldst not feel

speaker: LUCIANA
text: his meaning?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Nay, he struck so plainly I could

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: too well feel his blows, and withal so doubtfully

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: that I could scarce understand them.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But say, I prithee, is he coming home?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: It seems he hath great care to please his wife.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Why, mistress, sure my master is horn mad.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Horn mad, thou villain?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: I mean not cuckold mad,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: But sure he is stark mad.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: When I desired him to come home to dinner,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: He asked me for a thousand marks in gold.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “’Tis dinnertime,” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “Your meat doth burn,” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “Will you come?” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “Where is the thousand marks I gave thee, villain?”

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “The pig,” quoth I, “is burned.” “My gold,” quoth he.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “My mistress, sir,” quoth I. “Hang up thy mistress!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: I know not thy mistress. Out on thy mistress!”

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Quoth who?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Quoth my master.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: “I know,” quoth he, “no house, no wife, no mistress.”

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: So that my errand, due unto my tongue,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: I thank him, I bare home upon my shoulders,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: For, in conclusion, he did beat me there.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Go back again, thou slave, and fetch him home.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Go back again and be new beaten home?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: For God’s sake, send some other messenger.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Back, slave, or I will break thy pate across.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: And he will bless that cross with other beating.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Between you, I shall have a holy head.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Hence, prating peasant. Fetch thy master home.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Am I so round with you as you with me,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: That like a football you do spurn me thus?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: You spurn me hence, and he will spurn me hither.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: If I last in this service, you must case me in leather.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Fie, how impatience loureth in your face.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: His company must do his minions grace,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Whilst I at home starve for a merry look.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Hath homely age th’ alluring beauty took

speaker: ADRIANA
text: From my poor cheek? Then he hath wasted it.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Are my discourses dull? Barren my wit?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: If voluble and sharp discourse be marred,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Unkindness blunts it more than marble hard.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Do their gay vestments his affections bait?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That’s not my fault; he’s master of my state.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: What ruins are in me that can be found

speaker: ADRIANA
text: By him not ruined? Then is he the ground

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Of my defeatures. My decayèd fair

speaker: ADRIANA
text: A sunny look of his would soon repair.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But, too unruly deer, he breaks the pale

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And feeds from home. Poor I am but his stale.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Self-harming jealousy, fie, beat it hence.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Unfeeling fools can with such wrongs dispense.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I know his eye doth homage otherwhere,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Or else what lets it but he would be here?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Sister, you know he promised me a chain.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Would that alone o’ love he would detain,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: So he would keep fair quarter with his bed.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I see the jewel best enamelèd

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Will lose his beauty. Yet the gold bides still

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That others touch, and often touching will

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Wear gold; yet no man that hath a name

speaker: ADRIANA
text: By falsehood and corruption doth it shame.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Since that my beauty cannot please his eye,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I’ll weep what’s left away, and weeping die.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: How many fond fools serve mad jealousy!

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: The gold I gave to Dromio is laid up

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Safe at the Centaur, and the heedful slave

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Is wandered forth in care to seek me out.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: By computation and mine host’s report,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I could not speak with Dromio since at first

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I sent him from the mart. See, here he comes.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: How now, sir? Is your merry humor altered?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: As you love strokes, so jest with me again.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: You know no Centaur? You received no gold?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Your mistress sent to have me home to dinner?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: My house was at the Phoenix? Wast thou mad,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: That thus so madly thou didst answer me?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: What answer, sir? When spake I such a word?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Even now, even here, not half an hour since.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I did not see you since you sent me hence,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Home to the Centaur with the gold you gave me.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Villain, thou didst deny the gold’s receipt

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And told’st me of a mistress and a dinner,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: For which I hope thou felt’st I was displeased.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I am glad to see you in this merry vein.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: What means this jest, I pray you, master, tell me?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Yea, dost thou jeer and flout me in the teeth?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Think’st thou I jest? Hold, take thou that and that.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Hold, sir, for God’s sake! Now your jest is earnest.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Upon what bargain do you give it me?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Because that I familiarly sometimes

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Do use you for my fool and chat with you,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Your sauciness will jest upon my love

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And make a common of my serious hours.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: When the sun shines, let foolish gnats make sport,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: But creep in crannies when he hides his beams.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: If you will jest with me, know my aspect,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And fashion your demeanor to my looks,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Or I will beat this method in your sconce.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: “Sconce” call you it? So you

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: would leave battering, I had rather have it a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: “head.” An you use these blows long, I must get a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: sconce for my head and ensconce it too, or else I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: shall seek my wit in my shoulders. But I pray, sir,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: why am I beaten?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Dost thou not know?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Nothing, sir, but that I am

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: beaten.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Shall I tell you why?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Ay, sir, and wherefore, for they

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: say every why hath a wherefore.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: “Why” first: for flouting

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: me; and then “wherefore”: for urging it the second

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: time to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Was there ever any man thus beaten out of season,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: When in the “why” and the “wherefore” is neither rhyme nor reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Well, sir, I thank you.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thank me, sir, for what?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, for this something

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: that you gave me for nothing.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll make you amends next,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: to give you nothing for something. But say, sir, is it

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: dinnertime?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No, sir, I think the meat wants

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: that I have.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: In good time, sir, what’s

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: that?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Basting.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Well, sir, then ’twill be dry.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: If it be, sir, I pray you eat none of

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Your reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Lest it make you choleric and

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: purchase me another dry basting.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Well, sir, learn to jest in

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: good time. There’s a time for all things.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I durst have denied that before

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: you were so choleric.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: By what rule, sir?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, by a rule as plain as

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: the plain bald pate of Father Time himself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Let’s hear it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: There’s no time for a man to

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: recover his hair that grows bald by nature.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: May he not do it by fine and

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: recovery?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Yes, to pay a fine for a periwig,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: and recover the lost hair of another man.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Why is Time such a niggard

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: of hair, being, as it is, so plentiful an excrement?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Because it is a blessing that he

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: bestows on beasts, and what he hath scanted men

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: in hair, he hath given them in wit.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Why, but there’s many a

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: man hath more hair than wit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Not a man of those but he hath

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: the wit to lose his hair.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Why, thou didst conclude

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: hairy men plain dealers without wit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The plainer dealer, the sooner

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: lost. Yet he loseth it in a kind of jollity.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: For what reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: For two, and sound ones too.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Nay, not sound, I pray you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Sure ones, then.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Nay, not sure, in a thing

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: falsing.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Certain ones, then.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Name them.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The one, to save the money that

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: he spends in tiring; the other, that at dinner they

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: should not drop in his porridge.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: You would all this time

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: have proved there is no time for all things.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, and did, sir: namely, e’en

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: no time to recover hair lost by nature.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: But your reason was not

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: substantial why there is no time to recover.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Thus I mend it: Time himself is

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: bald and therefore, to the world’s end, will have

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: bald followers.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I knew ’twould be a bald

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: conclusion. But soft, who wafts us yonder?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ay, ay, Antipholus, look strange and frown.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Some other mistress hath thy sweet aspects.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I am not Adriana, nor thy wife.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: The time was once when thou unurged wouldst vow

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That never words were music to thine ear,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That never object pleasing in thine eye,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That never touch well welcome to thy hand,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That never meat sweet-savored in thy taste,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Unless I spake, or looked, or touched, or carved to thee.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: How comes it now, my husband, O, how comes it

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That thou art then estrangèd from thyself?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: “Thyself” I call it, being strange to me,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That, undividable, incorporate,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Am better than thy dear self’s better part.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ah, do not tear away thyself from me!

speaker: ADRIANA
text: For know, my love, as easy mayst thou fall

speaker: ADRIANA
text: A drop of water in the breaking gulf,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And take unmingled thence that drop again

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Without addition or diminishing,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: As take from me thyself and not me too.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: How dearly would it touch thee to the quick,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Shouldst thou but hear I were licentious

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And that this body, consecrate to thee,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: By ruffian lust should be contaminate!

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Wouldst thou not spit at me, and spurn at me,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And hurl the name of husband in my face,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And tear the stained skin off my harlot brow,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And from my false hand cut the wedding ring,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And break it with a deep-divorcing vow?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I know thou canst, and therefore see thou do it.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I am possessed with an adulterate blot;

speaker: ADRIANA
text: My blood is mingled with the crime of lust;

speaker: ADRIANA
text: For if we two be one, and thou play false,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I do digest the poison of thy flesh,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Being strumpeted by thy contagion.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Keep then fair league and truce with thy true bed,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I live distained, thou undishonorèd.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Plead you to me, fair dame? I know you not.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: In Ephesus I am but two hours old,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: As strange unto your town as to your talk,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Who, every word by all my wit being scanned,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Wants wit in all one word to understand.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Fie, brother, how the world is changed with you!

speaker: LUCIANA
text: When were you wont to use my sister thus?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: She sent for you by Dromio home to dinner.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: By Dromio?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: By me?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: By thee; and this thou didst return from him:

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That he did buffet thee and, in his blows,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Denied my house for his, me for his wife.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Did you converse, sir, with this gentlewoman?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What is the course and drift of your compact?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I, sir? I never saw her till this time.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Villain, thou liest, for even her very words

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Didst thou deliver to me on the mart.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I never spake with her in all my life.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: How can she thus then call us by our names—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Unless it be by inspiration?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: How ill agrees it with your gravity

speaker: ADRIANA
text: To counterfeit thus grossly with your slave,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Abetting him to thwart me in my mood.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Be it my wrong you are from me exempt,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: But wrong not that wrong with a more contempt.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Come, I will fasten on this sleeve of thine.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Thou art an elm, my husband, I a vine,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Whose weakness, married to thy stronger state,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Makes me with thy strength to communicate.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: If aught possess thee from me, it is dross,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Usurping ivy, brier, or idle moss,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Who, all for want of pruning, with intrusion

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Infect thy sap and live on thy confusion.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: To me she speaks; she moves me for her theme.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What, was I married to her in my dream?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Or sleep I now and think I hear all this?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What error drives our eyes and ears amiss?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Until I know this sure uncertainty

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll entertain the offered fallacy.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Dromio, go bid the servants spread for dinner.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: O, for my beads! I cross me for a sinner.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: This is the fairy land. O spite of spites!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: We talk with goblins, owls, and sprites.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: If we obey them not, this will ensue:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: They’ll suck our breath, or pinch us black and blue.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Why prat’st thou to thyself and answer’st not?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Dromio—thou, Dromio—thou snail, thou slug, thou sot.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I am transformèd, master, am I not?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I think thou art in mind, and so am I.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Nay, master, both in mind and in my shape.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thou hast thine own form.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No, I am an ape.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: If thou art changed to aught, ’tis to an ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: ’Tis true. She rides me, and I long for grass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: ’Tis so. I am an ass; else it could never be

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: But I should know her as well as she knows me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Come, come, no longer will I be a fool,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: To put the finger in the eye and weep

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Whilst man and master laughs my woes to scorn.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Come, sir, to dinner.—Dromio, keep the gate.—

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Husband, I’ll dine above with you today,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And shrive you of a thousand idle pranks.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Sirrah, if any ask you for your master,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Say he dines forth, and let no creature enter.—

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Come, sister.—Dromio, play the porter well.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Am I in Earth, in heaven, or in hell?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Sleeping or waking, mad or well-advised?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Known unto these, and to myself disguised!

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll say as they say, and persever so,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And in this mist at all adventures go.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Master, shall I be porter at the gate?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ay, and let none enter, lest I break your pate.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Come, come, Antipholus, we dine too late.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Good Signior Angelo, you must excuse us all;

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: My wife is shrewish when I keep not hours.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Say that I lingered with you at your shop

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: To see the making of her carcanet,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And that tomorrow you will bring it home.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But here’s a villain that would face me down

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: He met me on the mart, and that I beat him

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And charged him with a thousand marks in gold,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And that I did deny my wife and house.—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Thou drunkard, thou, what didst thou mean by this?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Say what you will, sir, but I know what I know.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: That you beat me at the mart I have your hand to show;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: If the skin were parchment and the blows you gave were ink,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Your own handwriting would tell you what I think.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I think thou art an ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Marry, so it doth appear

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: By the wrongs I suffer and the blows I bear.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: I should kick being kicked and, being at that pass,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: You would keep from my heels and beware of an ass.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: You’re sad, Signior Balthasar. Pray God our cheer

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: May answer my goodwill and your good welcome here.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: I hold your dainties cheap, sir, and your welcome dear.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: O Signior Balthasar, either at flesh or fish

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: A table full of welcome makes scarce one dainty dish.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Good meat, sir, is common; that every churl affords.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And welcome more common, for that’s nothing but words.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Small cheer and great welcome makes a merry feast.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Ay, to a niggardly host and more sparing guest.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But though my cates be mean, take them in good part.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Better cheer may you have, but not with better heart.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But soft! My door is locked. Go, bid them let us in.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Maud, Bridget, Marian, Ciceley, Gillian, Ginn!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Mome, malt-horse, capon, coxcomb, idiot, patch!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Either get thee from the door or sit down at the hatch.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Dost thou conjure for wenches, that thou call’st for such store

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: When one is one too many? Go, get thee from the door.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: What patch is made our porter? My master stays in the street.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Let him walk from whence he came, lest he catch cold on ’s feet.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Who talks within there? Ho, open the door.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Right, sir, I’ll tell you when an you’ll tell me wherefore.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Wherefore? For my dinner. I have not dined today.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Nor today here you must not. Come again when you may.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: What art thou that keep’st me out from the house I owe?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The porter for this time, sir, and my name is Dromio.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: O villain, thou hast stolen both mine office and my name!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: The one ne’er got me credit, the other mickle blame.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: If thou hadst been Dromio today in my place,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Thou wouldst have changed thy face for a name, or thy name for an ass.

speaker: LUCE
text: What a coil is there, Dromio! Who are those at the gate?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Let my master in, Luce.

speaker: LUCE
text: Faith, no, he comes too late,

speaker: LUCE
text: And so tell your master.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: O Lord, I must laugh.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Have at you with a proverb: shall I set in my staff?

speaker: LUCE
text: Have at you with another: that’s—When, can you tell?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: If thy name be called “Luce,” Luce, thou hast answered him well.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Do you hear, you minion? You’ll let us in, I hope?

speaker: LUCE
text: I thought to have asked you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: And you said no.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: So, come help. Well struck! There was blow for blow.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Thou baggage, let me in.

speaker: LUCE
text: Can you tell for whose sake?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Master, knock the door hard.

speaker: LUCE
text: Let him knock till it ache.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: You’ll cry for this, minion, if I beat the door down.

speaker: LUCE
text: What needs all that, and a pair of stocks in the town?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Who is that at the door that keeps all this noise?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: By my troth, your town is troubled with unruly boys.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Are you there, wife? You might have come before.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Your wife, sir knave? Go, get you from the door.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: If you went in pain, master, this knave would go sore.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Here is neither cheer, sir, nor welcome. We would fain have either.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: In debating which was best, we shall part with neither.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: They stand at the door, master. Bid them welcome hither.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: There is something in the wind, that we cannot get in.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: You would say so, master, if your garments were thin.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Your cake here is warm within; you stand here in the cold.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: It would make a man mad as a buck to be so bought and sold.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Go, fetch me something. I’ll break ope the gate.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Break any breaking here, and I’ll break your knave’s pate.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: A man may break a word with you, sir, and words are but wind,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Ay, and break it in your face, so he break it not behind.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: It seems thou want’st breaking. Out upon thee, hind!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: Here’s too much “Out upon thee!” I pray thee, let me in.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Ay, when fowls have no feathers and fish have no fin.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Well, I’ll break in. Go, borrow me a crow.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: A crow without feather? Master, mean you so?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: For a fish without a fin, there’s a fowl without a feather.—

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: If a crow help us in, sirrah, we’ll pluck a crow together.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Go, get thee gone. Fetch me an iron crow.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Have patience, sir. O, let it not be so.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Herein you war against your reputation,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And draw within the compass of suspect

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Th’ unviolated honor of your wife.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Once this: your long experience of her wisdom,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Her sober virtue, years, and modesty

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Plead on her part some cause to you unknown.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And doubt not, sir, but she will well excuse

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Why at this time the doors are made against you.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Be ruled by me; depart in patience,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And let us to the Tiger all to dinner,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And about evening come yourself alone

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: To know the reason of this strange restraint.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: If by strong hand you offer to break in

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Now in the stirring passage of the day,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: A vulgar comment will be made of it;

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And that supposèd by the common rout

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Against your yet ungallèd estimation

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: That may with foul intrusion enter in

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: And dwell upon your grave when you are dead;

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: For slander lives upon succession,

speaker: BALTHASAR
text: Forever housèd where it gets possession.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: You have prevailed. I will depart in quiet

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And, in despite of mirth, mean to be merry.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I know a wench of excellent discourse,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Pretty and witty, wild and yet, too, gentle.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: There will we dine. This woman that I mean,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: My wife—but, I protest, without desert—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Hath oftentimes upbraided me withal;

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: To her will we to dinner. Get you home

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And fetch the chain; by this, I know, ’tis made.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Bring it, I pray you, to the Porpentine,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: For there’s the house. That chain will I bestow—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Be it for nothing but to spite my wife—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Upon mine hostess there. Good sir, make haste.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Since mine own doors refuse to entertain me,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I’ll knock elsewhere, to see if they’ll disdain me.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I’ll meet you at that place some hour hence.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Do so. This jest shall cost me some expense.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: And may it be that you have quite forgot

speaker: LUCIANA
text: A husband’s office? Shall, Antipholus,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Even in the spring of love thy love-springs rot?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Shall love, in building, grow so ruinous?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: If you did wed my sister for her wealth,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Then for her wealth’s sake use her with more kindness.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Or if you like elsewhere, do it by stealth —

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Muffle your false love with some show of blindness.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Let not my sister read it in your eye;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Be not thy tongue thy own shame’s orator;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Look sweet, speak fair, become disloyalty;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Apparel vice like virtue’s harbinger.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Bear a fair presence, though your heart be tainted.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Teach sin the carriage of a holy saint.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Be secret-false. What need she be acquainted?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: What simple thief brags of his own attaint?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: ’Tis double wrong to truant with your bed

speaker: LUCIANA
text: And let her read it in thy looks at board.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Shame hath a bastard fame, well managèd;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Ill deeds is doubled with an evil word.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Alas, poor women, make us but believe,

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Being compact of credit, that you love us.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Though others have the arm, show us the sleeve;

speaker: LUCIANA
text: We in your motion turn, and you may move us.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Then, gentle brother, get you in again.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Comfort my sister, cheer her, call her wife.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: ’Tis holy sport to be a little vain

speaker: LUCIANA
text: When the sweet breath of flattery conquers strife.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Sweet mistress—what your name is else I know not,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Nor by what wonder you do hit of mine—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Less in your knowledge and your grace you show not

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Than our Earth’s wonder, more than Earth divine.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Teach me, dear creature, how to think and speak.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Lay open to my earthy gross conceit,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Smothered in errors, feeble, shallow, weak,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: The folded meaning of your words’ deceit.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Against my soul’s pure truth why labor you

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: To make it wander in an unknown field?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Are you a god? Would you create me new?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Transform me, then, and to your power I’ll yield.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: But if that I am I, then well I know

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Your weeping sister is no wife of mine,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Nor to her bed no homage do I owe.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Far more, far more, to you do I decline.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: O, train me not, sweet mermaid, with thy note

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: To drown me in thy sister’s flood of tears.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Sing, Siren, for thyself, and I will dote.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Spread o’er the silver waves thy golden hairs,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And as a bed I’ll take them and there lie,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And in that glorious supposition think

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: He gains by death that hath such means to die.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Let love, being light, be drownèd if she sink.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: What, are you mad that you do reason so?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Not mad, but mated—how, I do not know.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: It is a fault that springeth from your eye.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: For gazing on your beams, fair sun, being by.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Gaze when you should, and that will clear your sight.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: As good to wink, sweet love, as look on night.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Why call you me “love”? Call my sister so.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thy sister’s sister.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: That’s my sister.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: No,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: It is thyself, mine own self’s better part,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Mine eye’s clear eye, my dear heart’s dearer heart,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: My food, my fortune, and my sweet hope’s aim,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: My sole Earth’s heaven, and my heaven’s claim.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: All this my sister is, or else should be.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Call thyself “sister,” sweet, for I am thee.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thee will I love, and with thee lead my life;

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thou hast no husband yet, nor I no wife.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Give me thy hand.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: O soft, sir. Hold you still.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: I’ll fetch my sister to get her goodwill.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Why, how now, Dromio.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where runn’st thou so fast?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Do you know me, sir? Am I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Dromio? Am I your man? Am I myself?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Thou art Dromio, thou art

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: my man, thou art thyself.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I am an ass, I am a woman’s

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: man, and besides myself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What woman’s man? And

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: how besides thyself?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, besides myself I am

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: due to a woman, one that claims me, one that

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: haunts me, one that will have me.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What claim lays she to thee?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, such claim as you

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: would lay to your horse, and she would have me as

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: a beast; not that I being a beast she would have me,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: but that she, being a very beastly creature, lays

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: claim to me.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What is she?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A very reverend body, ay, such a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: one as a man may not speak of without he say

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: “sir-reverence.” I have but lean luck in the match,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: and yet is she a wondrous fat marriage.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: How dost thou mean a “fat

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: marriage”?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, she’s the kitchen

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: wench, and all grease, and I know not what use to

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: put her to but to make a lamp of her and run from

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: her by her own light. I warrant her rags and the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: tallow in them will burn a Poland winter. If she lives

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: till doomsday, she’ll burn a week longer than the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: whole world.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What complexion is she of?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Swart like my shoe, but her face

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: nothing like so clean kept. For why? She sweats. A

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: man may go overshoes in the grime of it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: That’s a fault that water will

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: mend.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No, sir, ’tis in grain; Noah’s flood

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: could not do it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What’s her name?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Nell, sir, but her name and

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: three quarters—that’s an ell and three quarters—

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: will not measure her from hip to hip.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Then she bears some

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: breadth?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No longer from head to foot than

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: from hip to hip. She is spherical, like a globe. I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: could find out countries in her.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: In what part of her body

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: stands Ireland?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Marry, sir, in her buttocks. I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: found it out by the bogs.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where Scotland?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I found it by the barrenness,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: hard in the palm of the hand.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where France?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: In her forehead, armed and

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: reverted, making war against her heir.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where England?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I looked for the chalky cliffs, but

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I could find no whiteness in them. But I guess it

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: stood in her chin, by the salt rheum that ran

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: between France and it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where Spain?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Faith, I saw it not, but I felt it hot

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: in her breath.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where America, the Indies?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: O, sir, upon her nose, all o’erembellished

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: with rubies, carbuncles, sapphires,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: declining their rich aspect to the hot breath of

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Spain, who sent whole armadas of carracks to be

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: ballast at her nose.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where stood Belgia, the

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Netherlands?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: O, sir, I did not look so low. To

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: conclude: this drudge or diviner laid claim to me,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: called me Dromio, swore I was assured to her, told

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: me what privy marks I had about me, as the mark

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: of my shoulder, the mole in my neck, the great wart

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: on my left arm, that I, amazed, ran from her as a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: witch.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: And, I think, if my breast had not been made of faith, and my heart of steel,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: She had transformed me to a curtal dog and made me turn i’ th’ wheel.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Go, hie thee presently. Post to the road.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: An if the wind blow any way from shore,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I will not harbor in this town tonight.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: If any bark put forth, come to the mart,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Where I will walk till thou return to me.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: If everyone knows us, and we know none,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: ’Tis time, I think, to trudge, pack, and be gone.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: As from a bear a man would run for life,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: So fly I from her that would be my wife.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: There’s none but witches do inhabit here,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And therefore ’tis high time that I were hence.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: She that doth call me husband, even my soul

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Doth for a wife abhor. But her fair sister,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Possessed with such a gentle sovereign grace,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Of such enchanting presence and discourse,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Hath almost made me traitor to myself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: But lest myself be guilty to self wrong,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll stop mine ears against the mermaid’s song.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Master Antipholus.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Ay, that’s my name.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I know it well, sir. Lo, here’s the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I thought to have ta’en you at the Porpentine;

speaker: ANGELO
text: The chain unfinished made me stay thus long.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What is your will that I shall do with this?

speaker: ANGELO
text: What please yourself, sir. I have made it for you.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Made it for me, sir? I bespoke it not.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Not once, nor twice, but twenty times you have.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Go home with it, and please your wife withal,

speaker: ANGELO
text: And soon at supper time I’ll visit you

speaker: ANGELO
text: And then receive my money for the chain.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I pray you, sir, receive the money now,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: For fear you ne’er see chain nor money more.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You are a merry man, sir. Fare you well.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What I should think of this I cannot tell,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: But this I think: there’s no man is so vain

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: That would refuse so fair an offered chain.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I see a man here needs not live by shifts

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: When in the streets he meets such golden gifts.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I’ll to the mart, and there for Dromio stay.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: If any ship put out, then straight away.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: You know since Pentecost the sum is due,

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: And since I have not much importuned you,

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: Nor now I had not, but that I am bound

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: To Persia and want guilders for my voyage.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: Therefore make present satisfaction,

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: Or I’ll attach you by this officer.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Even just the sum that I do owe to you

speaker: ANGELO
text: Is growing to me by Antipholus.

speaker: ANGELO
text: And in the instant that I met with you,

speaker: ANGELO
text: He had of me a chain. At five o’clock

speaker: ANGELO
text: I shall receive the money for the same.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Pleaseth you walk with me down to his house,

speaker: ANGELO
text: I will discharge my bond and thank you too.

speaker: OFFICER
text: That labor may you save. See where he comes.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: While I go to the goldsmith’s house, go thou

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And buy a rope’s end. That will I bestow

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Among my wife and her confederates

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: For locking me out of my doors by day.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But soft. I see the goldsmith. Get thee gone.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Buy thou a rope, and bring it home to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text: I buy a thousand pound a year! I buy a rope!

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: A man is well holp up that trusts to you!

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I promisèd your presence and the chain,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But neither chain nor goldsmith came to me.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Belike you thought our love would last too long

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: If it were chained together, and therefore came not.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Saving your merry humor, here’s the note

speaker: ANGELO
text: How much your chain weighs to the utmost carat,

speaker: ANGELO
text: The fineness of the gold, and chargeful fashion,

speaker: ANGELO
text: Which doth amount to three-odd ducats more

speaker: ANGELO
text: Than I stand debted to this gentleman.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I pray you, see him presently discharged,

speaker: ANGELO
text: For he is bound to sea, and stays but for it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I am not furnished with the present money.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Besides, I have some business in the town.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Good signior, take the stranger to my house,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And with you take the chain, and bid my wife

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Disburse the sum on the receipt thereof.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Perchance I will be there as soon as you.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Then you will bring the chain to her yourself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: No, bear it with you lest I come not time enough.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Well, sir, I will. Have you the chain about you?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: An if I have not, sir, I hope you have,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Or else you may return without your money.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Nay, come, I pray you, sir, give me the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Both wind and tide stays for this gentleman,

speaker: ANGELO
text: And I, to blame, have held him here too long.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Good Lord! You use this dalliance to excuse

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Your breach of promise to the Porpentine.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I should have chid you for not bringing it,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But, like a shrew, you first begin to brawl.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: The hour steals on. I pray you, sir, dispatch.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You hear how he importunes me. The chain!

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Why, give it to my wife, and fetch your money.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Come, come. You know I gave it you even now.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Either send the chain, or send by me some token.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Fie, now you run this humor out of breath.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Come, where’s the chain? I pray you, let me see it.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: My business cannot brook this dalliance.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: Good sir, say whe’er you’ll answer me or no.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: If not, I’ll leave him to the Officer.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I answer you? What should I answer you?

speaker: ANGELO
text: The money that you owe me for the chain.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I owe you none till I receive the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You know I gave it you half an hour since.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: You gave me none. You wrong me much to say so.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You wrong me more, sir, in denying it.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Consider how it stands upon my credit.

speaker: SECOND MERCHANT
text: Well, officer, arrest him at my suit.

speaker: OFFICER
text: I do, and charge you in the Duke’s name to obey me.

speaker: ANGELO
text: This touches me in reputation.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Either consent to pay this sum for me,

speaker: ANGELO
text: Or I attach you by this officer.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Consent to pay thee that I never had?—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Arrest me, foolish fellow, if thou dar’st.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Here is thy fee. Arrest him, officer.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I would not spare my brother in this case

speaker: ANGELO
text: If he should scorn me so apparently.

speaker: OFFICER
text: I do arrest you, sir. You hear the suit.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I do obey thee till I give thee bail.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: But, sirrah, you shall buy this sport as dear

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: As all the metal in your shop will answer.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Sir, sir, I shall have law in Ephesus,

speaker: ANGELO
text: To your notorious shame, I doubt it not.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Master, there’s a bark of Epidamium

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: That stays but till her owner comes aboard,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: And then, sir, she bears away. Our fraughtage, sir,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I have conveyed aboard, and I have bought

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The oil, the balsamum, and aqua vitae.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The ship is in her trim; the merry wind

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Blows fair from land. They stay for naught at all

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: But for their owner, master, and yourself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: How now? A madman? Why, thou peevish sheep,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: What ship of Epidamium stays for me?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A ship you sent me to, to hire waftage.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Thou drunken slave, I sent thee for a rope

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And told thee to what purpose and what end.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: You sent me for a rope’s end as soon.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: You sent me to the bay, sir, for a bark.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: I will debate this matter at more leisure

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And teach your ears to list me with more heed.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: To Adriana, villain, hie thee straight.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Give her this key, and tell her in the desk

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: That’s covered o’er with Turkish tapestry

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: There is a purse of ducats. Let her send it.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: Tell her I am arrested in the street,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: And that shall bail me. Hie thee, slave. Begone.—

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
text: On, officer, to prison till it come.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: To Adriana. That is where we dined,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Where Dowsabel did claim me for her husband.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: She is too big, I hope, for me to compass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Thither I must, although against my will,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: For servants must their masters’ minds fulfill.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ah, Luciana, did he tempt thee so?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Might’st thou perceive austerely in his eye

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That he did plead in earnest, yea or no?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Looked he or red or pale, or sad or merrily?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: What observation mad’st thou in this case

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Of his heart’s meteors tilting in his face?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: First he denied you had in him no right.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: He meant he did me none; the more my spite.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Then swore he that he was a stranger here.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And true he swore, though yet forsworn he were.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Then pleaded I for you.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And what said he?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: That love I begged for you he begged of me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: With what persuasion did he tempt thy love?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: With words that in an honest suit might move.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: First he did praise my beauty, then my speech.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Did’st speak him fair?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Have patience, I beseech.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: I cannot, nor I will not hold me still.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: My tongue, though not my heart, shall have his will.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: He is deformèd, crooked, old, and sere,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ill-faced, worse-bodied, shapeless everywhere,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Vicious, ungentle, foolish, blunt, unkind,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Stigmatical in making, worse in mind.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: Who would be jealous, then, of such a one?

speaker: LUCIANA
text: No evil lost is wailed when it is gone.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Ah, but I think him better than I say,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And yet would herein others’ eyes were worse.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Far from her nest the lapwing cries away.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: My heart prays for him, though my tongue do curse.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Here, go—the desk, the purse! Sweet, now make haste.

speaker: LUCIANA
text: How hast thou lost thy breath?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: By running fast.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Where is thy master, Dromio? Is he well?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No, he’s in Tartar limbo, worse than hell.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A devil in an everlasting garment hath him,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: One whose hard heart is buttoned up with steel;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A fiend, a fairy, pitiless and rough;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A wolf, nay, worse, a fellow all in buff;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A backfriend, a shoulder clapper, one that countermands

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: The passages of alleys, creeks, and narrow lands;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A hound that runs counter and yet draws dryfoot well,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: One that before the judgment carries poor souls to hell.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Why, man, what is the matter?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I do not know the matter. He is ’rested on the case.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: What, is he arrested? Tell me at whose suit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: I know not at whose suit he is arrested well,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: But is in a suit of buff which ’rested him; that can I tell.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Will you send him, mistress, redemption—the money in his desk?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Go fetch it, sister. This I wonder at,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: That he, unknown to me, should be in debt.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Tell me, was he arrested on a band?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Not on a band, but on a stronger thing:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: A chain, a chain. Do you not hear it ring?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: What, the chain?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No, no, the bell. ’Tis time that I were gone.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: It was two ere I left him, and now the clock strikes one.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: The hours come back. That did I never hear.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: O yes, if any hour meet a sergeant, he turns back for very fear.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: As if time were in debt. How fondly dost thou reason!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Time is a very bankrout and owes more than he’s worth to season.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Nay, he’s a thief too. Have you not heard men say

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: That time comes stealing on by night and day?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: If he be in debt and theft, and a sergeant in the way,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Hath he not reason to turn back an hour in a day?

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Go, Dromio. There’s the money. Bear it straight,

speaker: ADRIANA
text: And bring thy master home immediately.

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Come, sister, I am pressed down with conceit:

speaker: ADRIANA
text: Conceit, my comfort and my injury.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: There’s not a man I meet but doth salute me

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: As if I were their well-acquainted friend,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And everyone doth call me by my name.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Some tender money to me; some invite me;

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Some other give me thanks for kindnesses;

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Some offer me commodities to buy.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Even now a tailor called me in his shop

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And showed me silks that he had bought for me,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And therewithal took measure of my body.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Sure these are but imaginary wiles,

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: And Lapland sorcerers inhabit here.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Master, here’s the gold you sent

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: me for. What, have you got the picture of old Adam

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: new-appareled?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What gold is this? What Adam dost thou mean?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Not that Adam that kept the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Paradise, but that Adam that keeps the prison; he

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: that goes in the calf’s skin that was killed for the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Prodigal; he that came behind you, sir, like an evil

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: angel, and bid you forsake your liberty.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: I understand thee not.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: No? Why, ’tis a plain case: he

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: that went like a bass viol in a case of leather; the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: man, sir, that, when gentlemen are tired, gives

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: them a sob and ’rests them; he, sir, that takes pity

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: on decayed men and gives them suits of durance; he

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: that sets up his rest to do more exploits with his

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: mace than a morris-pike.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: What, thou mean’st an

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: officer?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: Ay, sir, the sergeant of the band;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: he that brings any man to answer it that breaks his

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: band; one that thinks a man always going to bed

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text: and says “God give you good rest.”

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: Well, sir, there rest in your

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
text: foolery. Is there any ships puts forth tonight? May
