text: At first I did adore a twinkling star,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But now I worship a celestial sun;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Unheedful vows may heedfully be broken,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And he wants wit that wants resolvèd will

speaker: PROTEUS
text: To learn his wit t’ exchange the bad for better.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Fie, fie, unreverend tongue, to call her bad

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Whose sovereignty so oft thou hast preferred

speaker: PROTEUS
text: With twenty thousand soul-confirming oaths.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I cannot leave to love, and yet I do.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But there I leave to love where I should love.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Julia I lose, and Valentine I lose;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: If I keep them, I needs must lose myself;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: If I lose them, thus find I by their loss:

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For Valentine, myself; for Julia, Sylvia.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I to myself am dearer than a friend,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For love is still most precious in itself,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And Sylvia—witness heaven that made her fair—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Shows Julia but a swarthy Ethiope.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I will forget that Julia is alive,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Rememb’ring that my love to her is dead;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And Valentine I’ll hold an enemy,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Aiming at Sylvia as a sweeter friend.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I cannot now prove constant to myself

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Without some treachery used to Valentine.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: This night he meaneth with a corded ladder

speaker: PROTEUS
text: To climb celestial Sylvia’s chamber window,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Myself in counsel his competitor.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Now presently I’ll give her father notice

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Of their disguising and pretended flight,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Who, all enraged, will banish Valentine,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For Thurio he intends shall wed his daughter.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But Valentine being gone, I’ll quickly cross

speaker: PROTEUS
text: By some sly trick blunt Thurio’s dull proceeding.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Love, lend me wings to make my purpose swift,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: As thou hast lent me wit to plot this drift.

speaker: JULIA
text: Counsel, Lucetta. Gentle girl, assist me;

speaker: JULIA
text: And ev’n in kind love I do conjure thee—

speaker: JULIA
text: Who art the table wherein all my thoughts

speaker: JULIA
text: Are visibly charactered and engraved—

speaker: JULIA
text: To lesson me and tell me some good mean

speaker: JULIA
text: How with my honor I may undertake

speaker: JULIA
text: A journey to my loving Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Alas, the way is wearisome and long.

speaker: JULIA
text: A true-devoted pilgrim is not weary

speaker: JULIA
text: To measure kingdoms with his feeble steps;

speaker: JULIA
text: Much less shall she that hath Love’s wings to fly,

speaker: JULIA
text: And when the flight is made to one so dear,

speaker: JULIA
text: Of such divine perfection, as Sir Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Better forbear till Proteus make return.

speaker: JULIA
text: O, know’st thou not his looks are my soul’s food?

speaker: JULIA
text: Pity the dearth that I have pinèd in

speaker: JULIA
text: By longing for that food so long a time.

speaker: JULIA
text: Didst thou but know the inly touch of love,

speaker: JULIA
text: Thou wouldst as soon go kindle fire with snow

speaker: JULIA
text: As seek to quench the fire of love with words.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: I do not seek to quench your love’s hot fire,

speaker: LUCETTA
text: But qualify the fire’s extreme rage,

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Lest it should burn above the bounds of reason.

speaker: JULIA
text: The more thou damm’st it up, the more it burns.

speaker: JULIA
text: The current that with gentle murmur glides,

speaker: JULIA
text: Thou know’st, being stopped, impatiently doth rage,

speaker: JULIA
text: But when his fair course is not hinderèd,

speaker: JULIA
text: He makes sweet music with th’ enameled stones,

speaker: JULIA
text: Giving a gentle kiss to every sedge

speaker: JULIA
text: He overtaketh in his pilgrimage;

speaker: JULIA
text: And so by many winding nooks he strays

speaker: JULIA
text: With willing sport to the wild ocean.

speaker: JULIA
text: Then let me go and hinder not my course.

speaker: JULIA
text: I’ll be as patient as a gentle stream

speaker: JULIA
text: And make a pastime of each weary step

speaker: JULIA
text: Till the last step have brought me to my love,

speaker: JULIA
text: And there I’ll rest as after much turmoil

speaker: JULIA
text: A blessèd soul doth in Elysium.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: But in what habit will you go along?

speaker: JULIA
text: Not like a woman, for I would prevent

speaker: JULIA
text: The loose encounters of lascivious men.

speaker: JULIA
text: Gentle Lucetta, fit me with such weeds

speaker: JULIA
text: As may beseem some well-reputed page.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Why, then, your Ladyship must cut your hair.

speaker: JULIA
text: No, girl, I’ll knit it up in silken strings

speaker: JULIA
text: With twenty odd-conceited true-love knots.

speaker: JULIA
text: To be fantastic may become a youth

speaker: JULIA
text: Of greater time than I shall show to be.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: What fashion, madam, shall I make your breeches?

speaker: JULIA
text: That fits as well as “Tell me, good my lord,

speaker: JULIA
text: What compass will you wear your farthingale?”

speaker: JULIA
text: Why, ev’n what fashion thou best likes, Lucetta.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: You must needs have them with a codpiece, madam.

speaker: JULIA
text: Out, out, Lucetta. That will be ill-favored.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: A round hose, madam, now’s not worth a pin

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Unless you have a codpiece to stick pins on.

speaker: JULIA
text: Lucetta, as thou lov’st me, let me have

speaker: JULIA
text: What thou think’st meet and is most mannerly.

speaker: JULIA
text: But tell me, wench, how will the world repute me

speaker: JULIA
text: For undertaking so unstaid a journey?

speaker: JULIA
text: I fear me it will make me scandalized.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: If you think so, then stay at home and go not.

speaker: JULIA
text: Nay, that I will not.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Then never dream on infamy, but go.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: If Proteus like your journey when you come,

speaker: LUCETTA
text: No matter who’s displeased when you are gone.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: I fear me he will scarce be pleased withal.

speaker: JULIA
text: That is the least, Lucetta, of my fear.

speaker: JULIA
text: A thousand oaths, an ocean of his tears,

speaker: JULIA
text: And instances of infinite of love

speaker: JULIA
text: Warrant me welcome to my Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: All these are servants to deceitful men.

speaker: JULIA
text: Base men that use them to so base effect!

speaker: JULIA
text: But truer stars did govern Proteus’ birth.

speaker: JULIA
text: His words are bonds, his oaths are oracles,

speaker: JULIA
text: His love sincere, his thoughts immaculate,

speaker: JULIA
text: His tears pure messengers sent from his heart,

speaker: JULIA
text: His heart as far from fraud as heaven from Earth.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Pray heav’n he prove so when you come to him.

speaker: JULIA
text: Now, as thou lov’st me, do him not that wrong

speaker: JULIA
text: To bear a hard opinion of his truth.

speaker: JULIA
text: Only deserve my love by loving him.

speaker: JULIA
text: And presently go with me to my chamber

speaker: JULIA
text: To take a note of what I stand in need of

speaker: JULIA
text: To furnish me upon my longing journey.

speaker: JULIA
text: All that is mine I leave at thy dispose,

speaker: JULIA
text: My goods, my lands, my reputation.

speaker: JULIA
text: Only, in lieu thereof, dispatch me hence.

speaker: JULIA
text: Come, answer not, but to it presently.

speaker: JULIA
text: I am impatient of my tarriance.

speaker: DUKE
text: Sir Thurio, give us leave, I pray, awhile;

speaker: DUKE
text: We have some secrets to confer about.

speaker: DUKE
text: Now tell me, Proteus, what’s your will with me?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: My gracious lord, that which I would discover

speaker: PROTEUS
text: The law of friendship bids me to conceal,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But when I call to mind your gracious favors

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Done to me, undeserving as I am,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: My duty pricks me on to utter that

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Which else no worldly good should draw from me.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Know, worthy prince, Sir Valentine my friend

speaker: PROTEUS
text: This night intends to steal away your daughter;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Myself am one made privy to the plot.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I know you have determined to bestow her

speaker: PROTEUS
text: On Thurio, whom your gentle daughter hates,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And should she thus be stol’n away from you,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: It would be much vexation to your age.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Thus, for my duty’s sake, I rather chose

speaker: PROTEUS
text: To cross my friend in his intended drift

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Than, by concealing it, heap on your head

speaker: PROTEUS
text: A pack of sorrows which would press you down,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Being unprevented, to your timeless grave.

speaker: DUKE
text: Proteus, I thank thee for thine honest care,

speaker: DUKE
text: Which to requite command me while I live.

speaker: DUKE
text: This love of theirs myself have often seen,

speaker: DUKE
text: Haply when they have judged me fast asleep,

speaker: DUKE
text: And oftentimes have purposed to forbid

speaker: DUKE
text: Sir Valentine her company and my court.

speaker: DUKE
text: But fearing lest my jealous aim might err

speaker: DUKE
text: And so, unworthily, disgrace the man—

speaker: DUKE
text: A rashness that I ever yet have shunned—

speaker: DUKE
text: I gave him gentle looks, thereby to find

speaker: DUKE
text: That which thyself hast now disclosed to me.

speaker: DUKE
text: And that thou mayst perceive my fear of this,

speaker: DUKE
text: Knowing that tender youth is soon suggested,

speaker: DUKE
text: I nightly lodge her in an upper tower,

speaker: DUKE
text: The key whereof myself have ever kept,

speaker: DUKE
text: And thence she cannot be conveyed away.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Know, noble lord, they have devised a mean

speaker: PROTEUS
text: How he her chamber-window will ascend

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And with a corded ladder fetch her down;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For which the youthful lover now is gone,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And this way comes he with it presently,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Where, if it please you, you may intercept him.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But, good my lord, do it so cunningly

speaker: PROTEUS
text: That my discovery be not aimèd at;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For love of you, not hate unto my friend,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Hath made me publisher of this pretense.

speaker: DUKE
text: Upon mine honor, he shall never know

speaker: DUKE
text: That I had any light from thee of this.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Adieu, my lord. Sir Valentine is coming.

speaker: DUKE
text: Sir Valentine, whither away so fast?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Please it your Grace, there is a messenger

speaker: VALENTINE
text: That stays to bear my letters to my friends,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And I am going to deliver them.

speaker: DUKE
text: Be they of much import?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: The tenor of them doth but signify

speaker: VALENTINE
text: My health and happy being at your court.

speaker: DUKE
text: Nay then, no matter. Stay with me awhile;

speaker: DUKE
text: I am to break with thee of some affairs

speaker: DUKE
text: That touch me near, wherein thou must be secret.

speaker: DUKE
text: ’Tis not unknown to thee that I have sought

speaker: DUKE
text: To match my friend Sir Thurio to my daughter.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I know it well, my lord, and sure the match

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Were rich and honorable. Besides, the gentleman

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Is full of virtue, bounty, worth, and qualities

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Beseeming such a wife as your fair daughter.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Cannot your Grace win her to fancy him?

speaker: DUKE
text: No. Trust me, she is peevish, sullen, froward,

speaker: DUKE
text: Proud, disobedient, stubborn, lacking duty,

speaker: DUKE
text: Neither regarding that she is my child

speaker: DUKE
text: Nor fearing me as if I were her father;

speaker: DUKE
text: And may I say to thee, this pride of hers,

speaker: DUKE
text: Upon advice, hath drawn my love from her,

speaker: DUKE
text: And where I thought the remnant of mine age

speaker: DUKE
text: Should have been cherished by her childlike duty,

speaker: DUKE
text: I now am full resolved to take a wife

speaker: DUKE
text: And turn her out to who will take her in.

speaker: DUKE
text: Then let her beauty be her wedding dower,

speaker: DUKE
text: For me and my possessions she esteems not.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What would your Grace have me to do in this?

speaker: DUKE
text: There is a lady in Verona here

speaker: DUKE
text: Whom I affect; but she is nice, and coy,

speaker: DUKE
text: And nought esteems my agèd eloquence.

speaker: DUKE
text: Now therefore would I have thee to my tutor—

speaker: DUKE
text: For long agone I have forgot to court;

speaker: DUKE
text: Besides, the fashion of the time is changed—

speaker: DUKE
text: How and which way I may bestow myself

speaker: DUKE
text: To be regarded in her sun-bright eye.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Win her with gifts if she respect not words;

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Dumb jewels often in their silent kind

speaker: VALENTINE
text: More than quick words do move a woman’s mind.

speaker: DUKE
text: But she did scorn a present that I sent her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: A woman sometime scorns what best contents her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Send her another; never give her o’er,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: For scorn at first makes after-love the more.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If she do frown, ’tis not in hate of you,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: But rather to beget more love in you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If she do chide, ’tis not to have you gone,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Forwhy the fools are mad if left alone.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Take no repulse, whatever she doth say;

speaker: VALENTINE
text: For “get you gone” she doth not mean “away.”

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Flatter and praise, commend, extol their graces;

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Though ne’er so black, say they have angels’ faces.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: That man that hath a tongue, I say, is no man

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If with his tongue he cannot win a woman.

speaker: DUKE
text: But she I mean is promised by her friends

speaker: DUKE
text: Unto a youthful gentleman of worth

speaker: DUKE
text: And kept severely from resort of men,

speaker: DUKE
text: That no man hath access by day to her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, then, I would resort to her by night.

speaker: DUKE
text: Ay, but the doors be locked and keys kept safe,

speaker: DUKE
text: That no man hath recourse to her by night.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What lets but one may enter at her window?

speaker: DUKE
text: Her chamber is aloft, far from the ground,

speaker: DUKE
text: And built so shelving that one cannot climb it

speaker: DUKE
text: Without apparent hazard of his life.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, then a ladder quaintly made of cords

speaker: VALENTINE
text: To cast up, with a pair of anchoring hooks,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Would serve to scale another Hero’s tower,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: So bold Leander would adventure it.

speaker: DUKE
text: Now, as thou art a gentleman of blood,

speaker: DUKE
text: Advise me where I may have such a ladder.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: When would you use it? Pray sir, tell me that.

speaker: DUKE
text: This very night; for love is like a child

speaker: DUKE
text: That longs for everything that he can come by.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: By seven o’clock I’ll get you such a ladder.

speaker: DUKE
text: But hark thee: I will go to her alone;

speaker: DUKE
text: How shall I best convey the ladder thither?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: It will be light, my lord, that you may bear it

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Under a cloak that is of any length.

speaker: DUKE
text: A cloak as long as thine will serve the turn?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Ay, my good lord.

speaker: DUKE
text: Then let me see thy cloak;

speaker: DUKE
text: I’ll get me one of such another length.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, any cloak will serve the turn, my lord.

speaker: DUKE
text: How shall I fashion me to wear a cloak?

speaker: DUKE
text: I pray thee, let me feel thy cloak upon me.

speaker: DUKE
text: What letter is this same? What’s here? To Sylvia .

speaker: DUKE
text: And here an engine fit for my proceeding.

speaker: DUKE
text: I’ll be so bold to break the seal for once.

speaker: DUKE
text: My thoughts do harbor with my Sylvia nightly,

speaker: DUKE
text: And slaves they are to me that send them flying.

speaker: DUKE
text: O, could their master come and go as lightly,

speaker: DUKE
text: Himself would lodge where, senseless, they are lying.

speaker: DUKE
text: My herald thoughts in thy pure bosom rest them,

speaker: DUKE
text: While I, their king, that thither them importune,

speaker: DUKE
text: Do curse the grace that with such grace hath blest them,

speaker: DUKE
text: Because myself do want my servants’ fortune.

speaker: DUKE
text: I curse myself, for they are sent by me,

speaker: DUKE
text: That they should harbor where their lord should be.

speaker: DUKE
text: What’s here?

speaker: DUKE
text: Sylvia, this night I will enfranchise thee.

speaker: DUKE
text: ’Tis so. And here’s the ladder for the purpose.

speaker: DUKE
text: Why, Phaëton—for thou art Merops’ son—

speaker: DUKE
text: Wilt thou aspire to guide the heavenly car

speaker: DUKE
text: And with thy daring folly burn the world?

speaker: DUKE
text: Wilt thou reach stars because they shine on thee?

speaker: DUKE
text: Go, base intruder, overweening slave,

speaker: DUKE
text: Bestow thy fawning smiles on equal mates

speaker: DUKE
text: And think my patience, more than thy desert,

speaker: DUKE
text: Is privilege for thy departure hence.

speaker: DUKE
text: Thank me for this more than for all the favors

speaker: DUKE
text: Which all too much I have bestowed on thee.

speaker: DUKE
text: But if thou linger in my territories

speaker: DUKE
text: Longer than swiftest expedition

speaker: DUKE
text: Will give thee time to leave our royal court,

speaker: DUKE
text: By heaven, my wrath shall far exceed the love

speaker: DUKE
text: I ever bore my daughter or thyself.

speaker: DUKE
text: Begone. I will not hear thy vain excuse,

speaker: DUKE
text: But, as thou lov’st thy life, make speed from hence.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And why not death, rather than living torment?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: To die is to be banished from myself,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And Sylvia is myself; banished from her

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Is self from self—a deadly banishment.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What light is light if Sylvia be not seen?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What joy is joy if Sylvia be not by—

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Unless it be to think that she is by

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And feed upon the shadow of perfection?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Except I be by Sylvia in the night,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: There is no music in the nightingale.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Unless I look on Sylvia in the day,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: There is no day for me to look upon.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: She is my essence, and I leave to be

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If I be not by her fair influence

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Fostered, illumined, cherished, kept alive.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I fly not death, to fly his deadly doom;

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Tarry I here, I but attend on death,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: But fly I hence, I fly away from life.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Run, boy, run, run, and seek him out.

speaker: LANCE
text: So-ho, so-ho!

speaker: PROTEUS
text: What seest thou?

speaker: LANCE
text: Him we go to find. There’s not a hair on ’s head

speaker: LANCE
text: but ’tis a Valentine.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Valentine?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Who then? His spirit?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Neither.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: What then?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Nothing.

speaker: LANCE
text: Can nothing speak? Master, shall I strike?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Who wouldst thou strike?

speaker: LANCE
text: Nothing.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Villain, forbear.

speaker: LANCE
text: Why, sir, I’ll strike nothing. I pray you—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Sirrah, I say forbear.—Friend Valentine, a word.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: My ears are stopped and cannot hear good news,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: So much of bad already hath possessed them.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Then in dumb silence will I bury mine,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: For they are harsh, untunable, and bad.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Is Sylvia dead?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: No, Valentine.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No Valentine indeed for sacred Sylvia.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Hath she forsworn me?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: No, Valentine.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No Valentine if Sylvia have forsworn me.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What is your news?

speaker: LANCE
text: Sir, there is a proclamation that you are

speaker: LANCE
text: vanished.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: That thou art banishèd—O, that’s the news—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: From hence, from Sylvia, and from me thy friend.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: O, I have fed upon this woe already,

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And now excess of it will make me surfeit.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Doth Sylvia know that I am banishèd?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Ay, ay, and she hath offered to the doom—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Which unreversed stands in effectual force—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: A sea of melting pearl, which some call tears;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Those at her father’s churlish feet she tendered,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: With them, upon her knees, her humble self,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Wringing her hands, whose whiteness so became them

speaker: PROTEUS
text: As if but now they waxèd pale for woe.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But neither bended knees, pure hands held up,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Sad sighs, deep groans, nor silver-shedding tears

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Could penetrate her uncompassionate sire;

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But Valentine, if he be ta’en, must die.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Besides, her intercession chafed him so,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: When she for thy repeal was suppliant,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: That to close prison he commanded her

speaker: PROTEUS
text: With many bitter threats of biding there.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No more, unless the next word that thou speak’st

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Have some malignant power upon my life.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If so, I pray thee breathe it in mine ear

speaker: VALENTINE
text: As ending anthem of my endless dolor.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Cease to lament for that thou canst not help,

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And study help for that which thou lament’st.

speaker: PROTEUS

text: Would make such fearful and confusèd cries

speaker: TAMORA
text: As any mortal body hearing it

speaker: TAMORA
text: Should straight fall mad, or else die suddenly.

speaker: TAMORA
text: No sooner had they told this hellish tale

speaker: TAMORA
text: But straight they told me they would bind me here

speaker: TAMORA
text: Unto the body of a dismal yew

speaker: TAMORA
text: And leave me to this miserable death.

speaker: TAMORA
text: And then they called me foul adulteress,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Lascivious Goth, and all the bitterest terms

speaker: TAMORA
text: That ever ear did hear to such effect.

speaker: TAMORA
text: And had you not by wondrous fortune come,

speaker: TAMORA
text: This vengeance on me had they executed.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Revenge it as you love your mother’s life,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Or be you not henceforth called my children.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: This is a witness that I am thy son.

speaker: CHIRON
text: And this for me, struck home to show my strength.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Ay, come, Semiramis, nay, barbarous Tamora,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: For no name fits thy nature but thy own!

speaker: TAMORA
text: Give me the poniard! You shall know, my boys,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Your mother’s hand shall right your mother’s wrong.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: Stay, madam, here is more belongs to her.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: First thrash the corn, then after burn the straw.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: This minion stood upon her chastity,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: Upon her nuptial vow, her loyalty,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: And with that painted hope braves your mightiness;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: And shall she carry this unto her grave?

speaker: CHIRON
text: And if she do, I would I were an eunuch!

speaker: CHIRON
text: Drag hence her husband to some secret hole,

speaker: CHIRON
text: And make his dead trunk pillow to our lust.

speaker: TAMORA
text: But when you have the honey you desire,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Let not this wasp outlive, us both to sting.

speaker: CHIRON
text: I warrant you, madam, we will make that sure.—

speaker: CHIRON
text: Come, mistress, now perforce we will enjoy

speaker: CHIRON
text: That nice-preservèd honesty of yours.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O Tamora, thou bearest a woman’s face—

speaker: TAMORA
text: I will not hear her speak. Away with her.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Sweet lords, entreat her hear me but a word.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: Listen, fair madam. Let it be your glory

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: To see her tears, but be your heart to them

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: As unrelenting flint to drops of rain.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: When did the tiger’s young ones teach the dam?

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O, do not learn her wrath; she taught it thee.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: The milk thou suck’st from her did turn to marble.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Even at thy teat thou hadst thy tyranny.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Yet every mother breeds not sons alike.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Do thou entreat her show a woman’s pity.

speaker: CHIRON
text: What, wouldst thou have me prove myself a bastard?

speaker: LAVINIA
text: ’Tis true; the raven doth not hatch a lark.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Yet have I heard—O, could I find it now!—

speaker: LAVINIA
text: The lion, moved with pity, did endure

speaker: LAVINIA
text: To have his princely paws pared all away.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Some say that ravens foster forlorn children,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: The whilst their own birds famish in their nests.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O, be to me, though thy hard heart say no,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Nothing so kind, but something pitiful.

speaker: TAMORA
text: I know not what it means.—Away with her.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O, let me teach thee! For my father’s sake,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: That gave thee life when well he might have slain thee,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Be not obdurate; open thy deaf ears.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Hadst thou in person ne’er offended me,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Even for his sake am I pitiless.—

speaker: TAMORA
text: Remember, boys, I poured forth tears in vain

speaker: TAMORA
text: To save your brother from the sacrifice,

speaker: TAMORA
text: But fierce Andronicus would not relent.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Therefore away with her, and use her as you will;

speaker: TAMORA
text: The worse to her, the better loved of me.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O Tamora, be called a gentle queen,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: And with thine own hands kill me in this place!

speaker: LAVINIA
text: For ’tis not life that I have begged so long;

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Poor I was slain when Bassianus died.

speaker: TAMORA
text: What begg’st thou, then? Fond woman, let me go!

speaker: LAVINIA
text: ’Tis present death I beg, and one thing more

speaker: LAVINIA
text: That womanhood denies my tongue to tell.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: O, keep me from their worse-than-killing lust,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: And tumble me into some loathsome pit

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Where never man’s eye may behold my body.

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Do this, and be a charitable murderer.

speaker: TAMORA
text: So should I rob my sweet sons of their fee.

speaker: TAMORA
text: No, let them satisfy their lust on thee.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: Away, for thou hast stayed us here too long!

speaker: LAVINIA
text: No grace, no womanhood? Ah, beastly creature,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: The blot and enemy to our general name,

speaker: LAVINIA
text: Confusion fall—

speaker: CHIRON
text: Nay, then, I’ll stop your mouth.—Bring thou her husband.

speaker: CHIRON
text: This is the hole where Aaron bid us hide him.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Farewell, my sons. See that you make her sure.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Ne’er let my heart know merry cheer indeed

speaker: TAMORA
text: Till all the Andronici be made away.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Now will I hence to seek my lovely Moor,

speaker: TAMORA
text: And let my spleenful sons this trull deflower.

speaker: AARON
text: Come on, my lords, the better foot before.

speaker: AARON
text: Straight will I bring you to the loathsome pit

speaker: AARON
text: Where I espied the panther fast asleep.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: My sight is very dull, whate’er it bodes.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: And mine, I promise you. Were it not for shame,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Well could I leave our sport to sleep awhile.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: What, art thou fallen? What subtle hole is this,

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Whose mouth is covered with rude-growing briers

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Upon whose leaves are drops of new-shed blood

speaker: QUINTUS
text: As fresh as morning dew distilled on flowers?

speaker: QUINTUS
text: A very fatal place it seems to me.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Speak, brother! Hast thou hurt thee with the fall?

speaker: MARTIUS
text: O, brother, with the dismal’st object hurt

speaker: MARTIUS
text: That ever eye with sight made heart lament!

speaker: AARON
text: Now will I fetch the King to find them here,

speaker: AARON
text: That he thereby may have a likely guess

speaker: AARON
text: How these were they that made away his brother.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Why dost not comfort me and help me out

speaker: MARTIUS
text: From this unhallowed and bloodstainèd hole?

speaker: QUINTUS
text: I am surprisèd with an uncouth fear.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: A chilling sweat o’erruns my trembling joints.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: My heart suspects more than mine eye can see.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: To prove thou hast a true-divining heart,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Aaron and thou look down into this den

speaker: MARTIUS
text: And see a fearful sight of blood and death.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Aaron is gone, and my compassionate heart

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Will not permit mine eyes once to behold

speaker: QUINTUS
text: The thing whereat it trembles by surmise.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: O, tell me who it is, for ne’er till now

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Was I a child to fear I know not what.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Lord Bassianus lies berayed in blood,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: All on a heap, like to a slaughtered lamb,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: In this detested, dark, blood-drinking pit.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: If it be dark, how dost thou know ’tis he?

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Upon his bloody finger he doth wear

speaker: MARTIUS
text: A precious ring that lightens all this hole,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Which like a taper in some monument

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Doth shine upon the dead man’s earthy cheeks

speaker: MARTIUS
text: And shows the ragged entrails of this pit.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: So pale did shine the moon on Pyramus

speaker: MARTIUS
text: When he by night lay bathed in maiden blood.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: O, brother, help me with thy fainting hand—

speaker: MARTIUS
text: If fear hath made thee faint as me it hath—

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Out of this fell devouring receptacle,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: As hateful as Cocytus’ misty mouth.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Reach me thy hand, that I may help thee out,

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Or, wanting strength to do thee so much good,

speaker: QUINTUS
text: I may be plucked into the swallowing womb

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Of this deep pit, poor Bassianus’ grave.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: I have no strength to pluck thee to the brink.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Nor I no strength to climb without thy help.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Thy hand once more. I will not loose again

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Till thou art here aloft or I below.

speaker: QUINTUS
text: Thou canst not come to me. I come to thee.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Along with me! I’ll see what hole is here

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And what he is that now is leapt into it.—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Say, who art thou that lately didst descend

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Into this gaping hollow of the earth?

speaker: MARTIUS
text: The unhappy sons of old Andronicus,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: Brought hither in a most unlucky hour

speaker: MARTIUS
text: To find thy brother Bassianus dead.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: My brother dead! I know thou dost but jest.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: He and his lady both are at the lodge

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Upon the north side of this pleasant chase.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: ’Tis not an hour since I left them there.

speaker: MARTIUS
text: We know not where you left them all alive,

speaker: MARTIUS
text: But, out alas, here have we found him dead.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Where is my lord the King?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Here, Tamora, though grieved with killing grief.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Where is thy brother Bassianus?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Now to the bottom dost thou search my wound.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Poor Bassianus here lies murderèd.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Then all too late I bring this fatal writ,

speaker: TAMORA
text: The complot of this timeless tragedy,

speaker: TAMORA
text: And wonder greatly that man’s face can fold

speaker: TAMORA
text: In pleasing smiles such murderous tyranny.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: An if we miss to meet him handsomely,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Sweet huntsman—Bassianus ’tis we mean—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Do thou so much as dig the grave for him;

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Thou know’st our meaning. Look for thy reward

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Among the nettles at the elder tree

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Which overshades the mouth of that same pit

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Where we decreed to bury Bassianus.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Do this, and purchase us thy lasting friends.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: O Tamora, was ever heard the like?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: This is the pit, and this the elder tree.—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Look, sirs, if you can find the huntsman out

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: That should have murdered Bassianus here.

speaker: AARON
text: My gracious lord, here is the bag of gold.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Two of thy whelps, fell curs of bloody kind,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Have here bereft my brother of his life.—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Sirs, drag them from the pit unto the prison.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: There let them bide until we have devised

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Some never-heard-of torturing pain for them.

speaker: TAMORA
text: What, are they in this pit? O wondrous thing!

speaker: TAMORA
text: How easily murder is discoverèd.

speaker: TITUS
text: High Emperor, upon my feeble knee

speaker: TITUS
text: I beg this boon with tears not lightly shed,

speaker: TITUS
text: That this fell fault of my accursèd sons—

speaker: TITUS
text: Accursèd if the faults be proved in them—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: If it be proved! You see it is apparent.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Who found this letter? Tamora, was it you?

speaker: TAMORA
text: Andronicus himself did take it up.

speaker: TITUS
text: I did, my lord, yet let me be their bail,

speaker: TITUS
text: For by my father’s reverend tomb I vow

speaker: TITUS
text: They shall be ready at your Highness’ will

speaker: TITUS
text: To answer their suspicion with their lives.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Thou shalt not bail them. See thou follow me.—

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Some bring the murdered body, some the murderers.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Let them not speak a word. The guilt is plain.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: For, by my soul, were there worse end than death,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: That end upon them should be executed.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Andronicus, I will entreat the King.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Fear not thy sons; they shall do well enough.

speaker: TITUS
text: Come, Lucius, come. Stay not to talk with them.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: So, now go tell, an if thy tongue can speak,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: Who ’twas that cut thy tongue and ravished thee.

speaker: CHIRON
text: Write down thy mind; bewray thy meaning so,

speaker: CHIRON
text: An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: See how with signs and tokens she can scrowl.

speaker: CHIRON
text: Go home. Call for sweet water; wash thy hands.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: She hath no tongue to call, nor hands to wash;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: And so let’s leave her to her silent walks.

speaker: CHIRON
text: An ’twere my cause, I should go hang myself.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Who is this? My niece, that flies away so fast?—

speaker: MARCUS
text: Cousin, a word. Where is your husband?

speaker: MARCUS
text: If I do dream, would all my wealth would wake me.

speaker: MARCUS
text: If I do wake, some planet strike me down

speaker: MARCUS
text: That I may slumber an eternal sleep.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Speak, gentle niece. What stern ungentle hands

speaker: MARCUS
text: Hath lopped and hewed and made thy body bare

speaker: MARCUS
text: Of her two branches, those sweet ornaments

speaker: MARCUS
text: Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in,

speaker: MARCUS
text: And might not gain so great a happiness

speaker: MARCUS
text: As half thy love? Why dost not speak to me?

speaker: MARCUS
text: Alas, a crimson river of warm blood,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Like to a bubbling fountain stirred with wind,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Doth rise and fall between thy rosèd lips,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Coming and going with thy honey breath.

speaker: MARCUS
text: But sure some Tereus hath deflowered thee,

speaker: MARCUS
text: And lest thou shouldst detect him cut thy tongue.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Ah, now thou turn’st away thy face for shame,

speaker: MARCUS
text: And notwithstanding all this loss of blood,

speaker: MARCUS
text: As from a conduit with three issuing spouts,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titan’s face,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Blushing to be encountered with a cloud.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Shall I speak for thee, shall I say ’tis so?

speaker: MARCUS
text: O, that I knew thy heart, and knew the beast,

speaker: MARCUS
text: That I might rail at him to ease my mind.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Sorrow concealèd, like an oven stopped,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Fair Philomela, why she but lost her tongue,

speaker: MARCUS
text: And in a tedious sampler sewed her mind;

speaker: MARCUS
text: But, lovely niece, that mean is cut from thee.

speaker: MARCUS
text: A craftier Tereus, cousin, hast thou met,

speaker: MARCUS
text: And he hath cut those pretty fingers off

speaker: MARCUS
text: That could have better sewed than Philomel.

speaker: MARCUS
text: O, had the monster seen those lily hands

speaker: MARCUS
text: Tremble like aspen leaves upon a lute

speaker: MARCUS
text: And make the silken strings delight to kiss them,

speaker: MARCUS
text: He would not then have touched them for his life.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Or had he heard the heavenly harmony

speaker: MARCUS
text: Which that sweet tongue hath made,

speaker: MARCUS
text: He would have dropped his knife and fell asleep,

speaker: MARCUS
text: As Cerberus at the Thracian poet’s feet.

speaker: MARCUS
text: Come, let us go and make thy father blind,

speaker: MARCUS
text: For such a sight will blind a father’s eye.

speaker: MARCUS
text: One hour’s storm will drown the fragrant meads;

speaker: MARCUS
text: What will whole months of tears thy father’s eyes?

speaker: MARCUS
text: Do not draw back, for we will mourn with thee.

speaker: MARCUS
text: O, could our mourning ease thy misery!

speaker: TITUS
text: Hear me, grave fathers; noble tribunes, stay.

speaker: TITUS
text: For pity of mine age, whose youth was spent

speaker: TITUS
text: In dangerous wars whilst you securely slept;

speaker: TITUS
text: For all my blood in Rome’s great quarrel shed,

speaker: TITUS
text: For all the frosty nights that I have watched,

speaker: TITUS
text: And for these bitter tears which now you see,

speaker: TITUS
text: Filling the agèd wrinkles in my cheeks,

speaker: TITUS
text: Be pitiful to my condemnèd sons,

speaker: TITUS
text: Whose souls is not corrupted as ’tis thought.

speaker: TITUS
text: For two-and-twenty sons I never wept

speaker: TITUS
text: Because they died in honor’s lofty bed.

speaker: TITUS
text: For these, tribunes, in the dust I write

speaker: TITUS
text: My heart’s deep languor and my soul’s sad tears.

speaker: TITUS
text: Let my tears stanch the earth’s dry appetite.

speaker: TITUS
text: My sons’ sweet blood will make it shame and blush.

speaker: TITUS
text: O Earth, I will befriend thee more with rain

speaker: TITUS
text: That shall distil from these two ancient ruins

speaker: TITUS
text: Than youthful April shall with all his showers.

speaker: TITUS
text: In summer’s drought I’ll drop upon thee still;

speaker: TITUS
text: In winter with warm tears I’ll melt the snow

speaker: TITUS
text: And keep eternal springtime on thy face,

speaker: TITUS
text: So thou refuse to drink my dear sons’ blood.

speaker: TITUS
text: O reverend tribunes, O gentle agèd men,

speaker: TITUS
text: Unbind my sons, reverse the doom of death,

speaker: TITUS
text: And let me say, that never wept before,

speaker: TITUS
text: My tears are now prevailing orators.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: O noble father, you lament in vain.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: The Tribunes hear you not; no man is by,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And you recount your sorrows to a stone.

speaker: TITUS
text: Ah, Lucius, for thy brothers let me plead.—

speaker: TITUS
text: Grave tribunes, once more I entreat of you—

speaker: LUCIUS
text: My gracious lord, no tribune hears you speak.

speaker: TITUS
text: Why, ’tis no matter, man. If they did hear,

speaker: TITUS
text: They would not mark me; if they did mark,

speaker: TITUS
text: They would not pity me. Yet plead I must,

speaker: TITUS
text: And bootless unto them.

speaker: TITUS
text: Therefore I tell my sorrows to the stones,

speaker: TITUS
text: Who, though they cannot answer my distress,

speaker: TITUS
text: Yet in some sort they are better than the Tribunes,

speaker: TITUS
text: For that they will not intercept my tale.

speaker: TITUS
text: When I do weep, they humbly at my feet

speaker: TITUS
text: Receive my tears and seem to weep with me,

speaker: TITUS
text: And were they but attirèd in grave weeds,

speaker: TITUS
text: Rome could afford no tribunes like to these.

speaker: TITUS
text: A stone is soft as wax, tribunes more hard than stones;

speaker: TITUS
text: A stone is silent and offendeth not,

speaker: TITUS
text: And tribunes with their tongues doom men to death.

speaker: TITUS
text: But wherefore stand’st thou with thy weapon drawn?

speaker: LUCIUS
text: To rescue my two brothers from their death,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: For which attempt the Judges have pronounced

speaker: LUCIUS
text: My everlasting doom of banishment.

speaker: TITUS
text: O happy man, they have befriended thee!

speaker: TITUS
text: Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive

speaker: TITUS
text: That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?

speaker: TITUS
text: Tigers must prey, and Rome affords no prey

speaker: TITUS
text: But me and mine. How happy art thou then

speaker: TITUS
text: From these devourers to be banishèd.

speaker: TITUS
text: But who comes with our brother Marcus here?

speaker: MARCUS
text: Titus, prepare thy agèd eyes to weep,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Or, if not so, thy noble heart to break.

speaker: MARCUS
text: I bring consuming sorrow to thine age.

speaker: TITUS
text: Will it consume me? Let me see it, then.

speaker: MARCUS
text: This was thy daughter.

speaker: TITUS
text: Why, Marcus, so she is.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Ay me, this object kills me!

speaker: TITUS
text: Faint-hearted boy, arise and look upon her.—

speaker: TITUS
text: Speak, Lavinia. What accursèd hand

speaker: TITUS
text: Hath made thee handless in thy father’s sight?

speaker: TITUS
text: What fool hath added water to the sea

speaker: TITUS
text: Or brought a faggot to bright-burning Troy?

speaker: TITUS
text: My grief was at the height before thou cam’st,

speaker: TITUS
text: And now like Nilus it disdaineth bounds.—

speaker: TITUS
text: Give me a sword. I’ll chop off my hands too,

speaker: TITUS
text: For they have fought for Rome and all in vain;

speaker: TITUS
text: And they have nursed this woe in feeding life;

speaker: TITUS
text: In bootless prayer have they been held up,

speaker: TITUS
text: And they have served me to effectless use.

speaker: TITUS
text: Now all the service I require of them

speaker: TITUS
text: Is that the one will help to cut the other.—

speaker: TITUS
text: ’Tis well, Lavinia, that thou hast no hands,

speaker: TITUS
text: For hands to do Rome service is but vain.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Speak, gentle sister. Who hath martyred thee?

speaker: MARCUS
text: O, that delightful engine of her thoughts,

speaker: MARCUS
text: That blabbed them with such pleasing eloquence,

speaker: MARCUS
text: Is torn from forth that pretty hollow cage

speaker: MARCUS
text: Where, like a sweet melodious bird, it sung

speaker: MARCUS
text: Sweet varied notes, enchanting every ear.

speaker: LUCIUS

text: came there. God forbid I should be so bold to press

text: to heaven in my young days. Why, I am going with

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: of brawl betwixt my uncle and one of the Emperal’s

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: men.

text: Why, sir, that is as fit as can be to

text: serve for your oration; and let him deliver the pigeons

text: to the Emperor from you.

text: with a grace?

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: grace in all my life.

speaker: TITUS
text: Sirrah, come hither. Make no more ado,

speaker: TITUS
text: But give your pigeons to the Emperor.

text: By me thou shalt have justice at his hands.

speaker: TITUS
text: Hold, hold; meanwhile here’s money for thy

speaker: TITUS
text: charges.—Give me pen and ink.—Sirrah, can you

speaker: TITUS
text: with a grace deliver up a supplication?

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: Ay, sir.

speaker: TITUS
text: Then here is a supplication for you, and when

speaker: TITUS
text: you come to him, at the first approach you must

speaker: TITUS
text: kneel, then kiss his foot, then deliver up your pigeons,

text: and then look for your reward. I’ll be at

speaker: TITUS
text: hand, sir. See you do it bravely.

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: I warrant you, sir. Let me alone.

speaker: TITUS
text: Sirrah, hast thou a knife? Come, let me see it.—

speaker: TITUS
text: Here, Marcus, fold it in the oration,

speaker: TITUS
text: For thou hast made it like an humble suppliant.—

speaker: TITUS
text: And when thou hast given it to the Emperor,

speaker: TITUS
text: Knock at my door and tell me what he says.

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: God be with you, sir. I will.

speaker: TITUS
text: Come, Marcus, let us go.—Publius, follow me.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Why, lords, what wrongs are these! Was ever seen

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: An emperor in Rome thus overborne,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Troubled, confronted thus, and for the extent

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Of equal justice, used in such contempt?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: My lords, you know, as know the mightful gods,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: However these disturbers of our peace

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Buzz in the people’s ears, there naught hath passed

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: But even with law against the willful sons

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Of old Andronicus. And what an if

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: His sorrows have so overwhelmed his wits?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Shall we be thus afflicted in his wreaks,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: His fits, his frenzy, and his bitterness?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And now he writes to heaven for his redress!

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: See, here’s “to Jove,” and this “to Mercury,”

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: This “to Apollo,” this to the god of war.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Sweet scrolls to fly about the streets of Rome!

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: What’s this but libeling against the Senate

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And blazoning our unjustice everywhere?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: A goodly humor is it not, my lords?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: As who would say, in Rome no justice were.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: But if I live, his feignèd ecstasies

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Shall be no shelter to these outrages,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: But he and his shall know that justice lives

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: In Saturninus’ health, whom, if he sleep,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: He’ll so awake as he in fury shall

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Cut off the proud’st conspirator that lives.

speaker: TAMORA
text: My gracious lord, my lovely Saturnine,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Lord of my life, commander of my thoughts,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Calm thee, and bear the faults of Titus’ age,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Th’ effects of sorrow for his valiant sons,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Whose loss hath pierced him deep and scarred his heart,

speaker: TAMORA
text: And rather comfort his distressèd plight

speaker: TAMORA
text: Than prosecute the meanest or the best

speaker: TAMORA
text: For these contempts. Why, thus it shall become

speaker: TAMORA
text: High-witted Tamora to gloze with all.

speaker: TAMORA
text: But, Titus, I have touched thee to the quick.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Thy lifeblood out, if Aaron now be wise,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Then is all safe, the anchor in the port.

text: How now, good fellow, wouldst thou speak with us?

text: Yea, forsooth, an your Mistresship be

text: emperial.

text: Empress I am, but yonder sits the Emperor.

text: ’Tis he!—God and Saint Stephen

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: give you good e’en. I have brought you a letter and

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: a couple of pigeons here.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Go, take him away, and hang him presently.

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: How much money must I have?

text: Come, sirrah, you must be hanged.

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: Hanged! By ’r Lady, then I have

speaker: COUNTRY FELLOW
text: brought up a neck to a fair end.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Despiteful and intolerable wrongs!

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Shall I endure this monstrous villainy?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: I know from whence this same device proceeds.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: May this be borne?—as if his traitorous sons,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: That died by law for murder of our brother,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Have by my means been butchered wrongfully!

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Go, drag the villain hither by the hair.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Nor age nor honor shall shape privilege.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: For this proud mock, I’ll be thy slaughterman,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Sly, frantic wretch, that holp’st to make me great

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: In hope thyself should govern Rome and me.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: What news with thee, Aemilius?

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Arm, my lords! Rome never had more cause.

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: The Goths have gathered head, and with a power

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Of high-resolvèd men bent to the spoil,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: They hither march amain under conduct

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Of Lucius, son to old Andronicus,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Who threats, in course of this revenge, to do

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: As much as ever Coriolanus did.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Is warlike Lucius general of the Goths?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: These tidings nip me, and I hang the head

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: As flowers with frost or grass beat down with storms.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Ay, now begins our sorrows to approach.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: ’Tis he the common people love so much.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Myself hath often heard them say,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: When I have walkèd like a private man,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: That Lucius’ banishment was wrongfully,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And they have wished that Lucius were their emperor.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Why should you fear? Is not your city strong?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Ay, but the citizens favor Lucius

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And will revolt from me to succor him.

speaker: TAMORA
text: King, be thy thoughts imperious like thy name.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Is the sun dimmed that gnats do fly in it?

speaker: TAMORA
text: The eagle suffers little birds to sing

speaker: TAMORA
text: And is not careful what they mean thereby,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Knowing that with the shadow of his wings

speaker: TAMORA
text: He can at pleasure stint their melody.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Even so mayst thou the giddy men of Rome.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Then cheer thy spirit, for know, thou emperor,

speaker: TAMORA
text: I will enchant the old Andronicus

speaker: TAMORA
text: With words more sweet and yet more dangerous

speaker: TAMORA
text: Than baits to fish or honey-stalks to sheep,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Whenas the one is wounded with the bait,

speaker: TAMORA
text: The other rotted with delicious feed.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: But he will not entreat his son for us.

speaker: TAMORA
text: If Tamora entreat him, then he will,

speaker: TAMORA
text: For I can smooth and fill his agèd ears

speaker: TAMORA
text: With golden promises, that were his heart

speaker: TAMORA
text: Almost impregnable, his old ears deaf,

speaker: TAMORA
text: Yet should both ear and heart obey my tongue.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Go thou before to be our ambassador.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Say that the Emperor requests a parley

speaker: TAMORA
text: Of warlike Lucius, and appoint the meeting

speaker: TAMORA
text: Even at his father’s house, the old Andronicus.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Aemilius, do this message honorably,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: And if he stand in hostage for his safety,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Bid him demand what pledge will please him best.

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Your bidding shall I do effectually.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Now will I to that old Andronicus

speaker: TAMORA
text: And temper him with all the art I have

speaker: TAMORA
text: To pluck proud Lucius from the warlike Goths.

speaker: TAMORA
text: And now, sweet emperor, be blithe again,

speaker: TAMORA
text: And bury all thy fear in my devices.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text: Then go successantly, and plead to him.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Approvèd warriors and my faithful friends,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: I have receivèd letters from great Rome

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Which signifies what hate they bear their emperor

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And how desirous of our sight they are.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Therefore, great lords, be as your titles witness,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Imperious, and impatient of your wrongs,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And wherein Rome hath done you any scathe,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Let him make treble satisfaction.

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Brave slip sprung from the great Andronicus,

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Whose name was once our terror, now our comfort,

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Whose high exploits and honorable deeds

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Ingrateful Rome requites with foul contempt,

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Be bold in us. We’ll follow where thou lead’st,

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Like stinging bees in hottest summer’s day

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: Led by their master to the flowered fields,

speaker: FIRST GOTH
text: And be avenged on cursèd Tamora.

speaker: GOTHS
text: And as he saith, so say we all with him.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: I humbly thank him, and I thank you all.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: But who comes here, led by a lusty Goth?

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Renownèd Lucius, from our troops I strayed

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: To gaze upon a ruinous monastery,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: And as I earnestly did fix mine eye

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Upon the wasted building, suddenly

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: I heard a child cry underneath a wall.

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: I made unto the noise, when soon I heard

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: The crying babe controlled with this discourse:

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: “Peace, tawny slave, half me and half thy dame!

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Did not thy hue bewray whose brat thou art,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Had nature lent thee but thy mother’s look,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Villain, thou mightst have been an emperor.

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: But where the bull and cow are both milk white,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: They never do beget a coal-black calf.

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Peace, villain, peace!”—even thus he rates the babe—

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: “For I must bear thee to a trusty Goth

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Who, when he knows thou art the Empress’ babe,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Will hold thee dearly for thy mother’s sake.”

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: With this, my weapon drawn, I rushed upon him,

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: Surprised him suddenly, and brought him hither

speaker: SECOND GOTH
text: To use as you think needful of the man.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: O worthy Goth, this is the incarnate devil

speaker: LUCIUS
text: That robbed Andronicus of his good hand;

speaker: LUCIUS
text: This is the pearl that pleased your empress’ eye;

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And here’s the base fruit of her burning lust.—

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Say, wall-eyed slave, whither wouldst thou convey

speaker: LUCIUS
text: This growing image of thy fiendlike face?

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Why dost not speak? What, deaf? Not a word?—

speaker: LUCIUS
text: A halter, soldiers! Hang him on this tree,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And by his side his fruit of bastardy.

speaker: AARON
text: Touch not the boy. He is of royal blood.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Too like the sire for ever being good.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: First hang the child, that he may see it sprawl,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: A sight to vex the father’s soul withal.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Get me a ladder.

speaker: AARON
text: Lucius, save the child

speaker: AARON
text: And bear it from me to the Empress.

speaker: AARON
text: If thou do this, I’ll show thee wondrous things

speaker: AARON
text: That highly may advantage thee to hear.

speaker: AARON
text: If thou wilt not, befall what may befall,

speaker: AARON
text: I’ll speak no more but “Vengeance rot you all!”

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Say on, and if it please me which thou speak’st,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Thy child shall live, and I will see it nourished.

speaker: AARON
text: And if it please thee? Why, assure thee, Lucius,

speaker: AARON
text: ’Twill vex thy soul to hear what I shall speak;

speaker: AARON
text: For I must talk of murders, rapes, and massacres,

speaker: AARON
text: Acts of black night, abominable deeds,

speaker: AARON
text: Complots of mischief, treason, villainies,

speaker: AARON
text: Ruthful to hear, yet piteously performed.

speaker: AARON
text: And this shall all be buried in my death,

speaker: AARON
text: Unless thou swear to me my child shall live.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Tell on thy mind. I say thy child shall live.

speaker: AARON
text: Swear that he shall, and then I will begin.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Who should I swear by? Thou believest no god.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: That granted, how canst thou believe an oath?

speaker: AARON
text: What if I do not? As indeed I do not.

speaker: AARON
text: Yet, for I know thou art religious

speaker: AARON
text: And hast a thing within thee callèd conscience,

speaker: AARON
text: With twenty popish tricks and ceremonies

speaker: AARON
text: Which I have seen thee careful to observe,

speaker: AARON
text: Therefore I urge thy oath; for that I know

speaker: AARON
text: An idiot holds his bauble for a god

speaker: AARON
text: And keeps the oath which by that god he swears,

speaker: AARON
text: To that I’ll urge him. Therefore thou shalt vow

speaker: AARON
text: By that same god, what god soe’er it be

speaker: AARON
text: That thou adorest and hast in reverence,

speaker: AARON
text: To save my boy, to nourish and bring him up,

speaker: AARON
text: Or else I will discover naught to thee.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Even by my god I swear to thee I will.

speaker: AARON
text: First know thou, I begot him on the Empress.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: O, most insatiate and luxurious woman!

speaker: AARON
text: Tut, Lucius, this was but a deed of charity

speaker: AARON
text: To that which thou shalt hear of me anon.

speaker: AARON
text: ’Twas her two sons that murdered Bassianus.

speaker: AARON
text: They cut thy sister’s tongue, and ravished her,

speaker: AARON
text: And cut her hands, and trimmed her as thou sawest.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: O detestable villain, call’st thou that trimming?

speaker: AARON
text: Why, she was washed, and cut, and trimmed; and ’twas

speaker: AARON
text: Trim sport for them which had the doing of it.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: O, barbarous beastly villains, like thyself!

speaker: AARON
text: Indeed, I was their tutor to instruct them.

speaker: AARON
text: That codding spirit had they from their mother,

speaker: AARON
text: As sure a card as ever won the set;

speaker: AARON
text: That bloody mind I think they learned of me,

speaker: AARON
text: As true a dog as ever fought at head.

speaker: AARON
text: Well, let my deeds be witness of my worth.

speaker: AARON
text: I trained thy brethren to that guileful hole

speaker: AARON
text: Where the dead corpse of Bassianus lay.

speaker: AARON
text: I wrote the letter that thy father found,

speaker: AARON
text: And hid the gold within that letter mentioned,

speaker: AARON
text: Confederate with the Queen and her two sons.

speaker: AARON
text: And what not done that thou hast cause to rue,

speaker: AARON
text: Wherein I had no stroke of mischief in it?

speaker: AARON
text: I played the cheater for thy father’s hand,

speaker: AARON
text: And, when I had it, drew myself apart

speaker: AARON
text: And almost broke my heart with extreme laughter.

speaker: AARON
text: I pried me through the crevice of a wall

speaker: AARON
text: When, for his hand, he had his two sons’ heads,

speaker: AARON
text: Beheld his tears, and laughed so heartily

speaker: AARON
text: That both mine eyes were rainy like to his.

speaker: AARON
text: And when I told the Empress of this sport,

speaker: AARON
text: She sounded almost at my pleasing tale,

speaker: AARON
text: And for my tidings gave me twenty kisses.

speaker: GOTH
text: What, canst thou say all this and never blush?

speaker: AARON
text: Ay, like a black dog, as the saying is.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Art thou not sorry for these heinous deeds?

speaker: AARON
text: Ay, that I had not done a thousand more.

speaker: AARON
text: Even now I curse the day—and yet, I think,

speaker: AARON
text: Few come within the compass of my curse—

speaker: AARON
text: Wherein I did not some notorious ill,

speaker: AARON
text: As kill a man, or else devise his death;

speaker: AARON
text: Ravish a maid or plot the way to do it;

speaker: AARON
text: Accuse some innocent and forswear myself;

speaker: AARON
text: Set deadly enmity between two friends;

speaker: AARON
text: Make poor men’s cattle break their necks;

speaker: AARON
text: Set fire on barns and haystalks in the night,

speaker: AARON
text: And bid the owners quench them with their tears.

speaker: AARON
text: Oft have I digged up dead men from their graves

speaker: AARON
text: And set them upright at their dear friends’ door,

speaker: AARON
text: Even when their sorrows almost was forgot,

speaker: AARON
text: And on their skins, as on the bark of trees,

speaker: AARON
text: Have with my knife carvèd in Roman letters

speaker: AARON
text: “Let not your sorrow die, though I am dead.”

speaker: AARON
text: But I have done a thousand dreadful things

speaker: AARON
text: As willingly as one would kill a fly,

speaker: AARON
text: And nothing grieves me heartily indeed

speaker: AARON
text: But that I cannot do ten thousand more.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Bring down the devil, for he must not die

speaker: LUCIUS
text: So sweet a death as hanging presently.

speaker: AARON
text: If there be devils, would I were a devil,

speaker: AARON
text: To live and burn in everlasting fire,

speaker: AARON
text: So I might have your company in hell

speaker: AARON
text: But to torment you with my bitter tongue.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Sirs, stop his mouth, and let him speak no more.

speaker: GOTH
text: My lord, there is a messenger from Rome

speaker: GOTH
text: Desires to be admitted to your presence.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Let him come near.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Welcome, Aemilius. What’s the news from Rome?

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Lord Lucius, and you princes of the Goths,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: The Roman Emperor greets you all by me;

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: And, for he understands you are in arms,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: He craves a parley at your father’s house,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: Willing you to demand your hostages,

speaker: AEMILIUS
text: And they shall be immediately delivered.

speaker: GOTH
text: What says our general?

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Aemilius, let the Emperor give his pledges

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Unto my father and my uncle Marcus,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And we will come. March away.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Thus, in this strange and sad habiliment

speaker: TAMORA
text: I will encounter with Andronicus

text: And say I am Revenge, sent from below

speaker: TAMORA
text: To join with him and right his heinous wrongs.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Knock at his study, where they say he keeps

speaker: TAMORA
text: To ruminate strange plots of dire revenge.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Tell him Revenge is come to join with him

text: And work confusion on his enemies.

speaker: TITUS
text: Who doth molest my contemplation?

speaker: TITUS
text: Is it your trick to make me ope the door,

speaker: TITUS
text: That so my sad decrees may fly away

speaker: TITUS
text: And all my study be to no effect?

speaker: TITUS
text: You are deceived, for what I mean to do,

speaker: TITUS
text: See here, in bloody lines I have set down,

speaker: TITUS
text: And what is written shall be executed.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Titus, I am come to talk with thee.

speaker: TITUS
text: No, not a word. How can I grace my talk,

speaker: TITUS
text: Wanting a hand to give it action?

speaker: TITUS
text: Thou hast the odds of me; therefore, no more.

speaker: TAMORA
text: If thou didst know me, thou wouldst talk with me.

speaker: TITUS
text: I am not mad. I know thee well enough.

speaker: TITUS
text: Witness this wretched stump; witness these crimson lines;

speaker: TITUS
text: Witness these trenches made by grief and care;

speaker: TITUS
text: Witness the tiring day and heavy night;

speaker: TITUS
text: Witness all sorrow that I know thee well

speaker: TITUS
text: For our proud empress, mighty Tamora.

speaker: TITUS
text: Is not thy coming for my other hand?

speaker: TAMORA
text: Know, thou sad man, I am not Tamora.

speaker: TAMORA
text: She is thy enemy, and I thy friend.

speaker: TAMORA
text: I am Revenge, sent from th’ infernal kingdom

speaker: TAMORA
text: To ease the gnawing vulture of thy mind

speaker: TAMORA
text: By working wreakful vengeance on thy foes.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Come down and welcome me to this world’s light.

speaker: TAMORA
text: Confer with me of murder and of death.

speaker: TAMORA
text: There’s not a hollow cave or lurking-place,

speaker: TAMORA
text: No vast obscurity or misty vale

speaker: TAMORA
text: Where bloody murder or detested rape

speaker: TAMORA
text: Can couch for fear but I will find them out,

speaker: TAMORA
text: And in their ears tell them my dreadful name,

speaker: TAMORA
