text: If one good deed in all my life I did,

speaker: AARON
text: I do repent it from my very soul.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Some loving friends convey the Emperor hence,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And give him burial in his fathers’ grave.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: My father and Lavinia shall forthwith

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Be closèd in our household’s monument.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: As for that ravenous tiger, Tamora,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: No funeral rite, nor man in mourning weed;

speaker: LUCIUS
text: No mournful bell shall ring her burial;

speaker: LUCIUS
text: But throw her forth to beasts and birds to prey.

speaker: LUCIUS
text: Her life was beastly and devoid of pity,

speaker: LUCIUS
text: And being dead, let birds on her take pity.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: In Troy there lies the scene. From isles of Greece

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: The princes orgulous, their high blood chafed,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Have to the port of Athens sent their ships

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Fraught with the ministers and instruments

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Of cruel war. Sixty and nine, that wore

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Their crownets regal, from th’ Athenian bay

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Put forth toward Phrygia, and their vow is made

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: To ransack Troy, within whose strong immures

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: The ravished Helen, Menelaus’ queen,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: With wanton Paris sleeps; and that’s the quarrel.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: To Tenedos they come,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: And the deep-drawing barks do there disgorge

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Their warlike fraughtage. Now on Dardan plains

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: The fresh and yet unbruisèd Greeks do pitch

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Their brave pavilions. Priam’s six-gated city—

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Dardan and Timbria, Helias, Chetas, Troien,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: And Antenorides—with massy staples

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: And corresponsive and fulfilling bolts,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Spar up the sons of Troy.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Now expectation, tickling skittish spirits

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: On one and other side, Trojan and Greek,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Sets all on hazard. And hither am I come,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: A prologue armed, but not in confidence

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Of author’s pen or actor’s voice, but suited

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: In like conditions as our argument,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: To tell you, fair beholders, that our play

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Leaps o’er the vaunt and firstlings of those broils,

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Beginning in the middle, starting thence away

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: To what may be digested in a play.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Like, or find fault; do as your pleasures are.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text: Now, good or bad, ’tis but the chance of war.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Call here my varlet; I’ll unarm again.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Why should I war without the walls of Troy

speaker: TROILUS
text: That find such cruel battle here within?

speaker: TROILUS
text: Each Trojan that is master of his heart,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Let him to field; Troilus, alas, hath none.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Will this gear ne’er be mended?

speaker: TROILUS
text: The Greeks are strong and skilful to their strength,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Fierce to their skill, and to their fierceness valiant;

speaker: TROILUS
text: But I am weaker than a woman’s tear,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Tamer than sleep, fonder than ignorance,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Less valiant than the virgin in the night,

speaker: TROILUS
text: And skilless as unpracticed infancy.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Well, I have told you enough of this. For my

speaker: PANDARUS
text: part, I’ll not meddle nor make no farther. He that will

speaker: PANDARUS
text: have a cake out of the wheat must tarry the grinding.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Have I not tarried?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Ay, the grinding; but you must tarry the

speaker: PANDARUS
text: bolting.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Have I not tarried?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Ay, the bolting; but you must tarry the

speaker: PANDARUS
text: leavening.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Still have I tarried.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Ay, to the leavening; but here’s yet in the word

speaker: PANDARUS
text: hereafter the kneading, the making of the cake, the

speaker: PANDARUS
text: heating the oven, and the baking. Nay, you must stay

speaker: PANDARUS
text: the cooling too, or you may chance burn your lips.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Patience herself, what goddess e’er she be,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Doth lesser blench at suff’rance than I do.

speaker: TROILUS
text: At Priam’s royal table do I sit

speaker: TROILUS
text: And when fair Cressid comes into my thoughts—

speaker: TROILUS
text: So, traitor! “When she comes”? When is she thence?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Well, she looked yesternight fairer than ever

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I saw her look, or any woman else.

speaker: TROILUS
text: I was about to tell thee: when my heart,

speaker: TROILUS
text: As wedgèd with a sigh, would rive in twain,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Lest Hector or my father should perceive me,

speaker: TROILUS
text: I have, as when the sun doth light a-scorn,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Buried this sigh in wrinkle of a smile;

speaker: TROILUS
text: But sorrow that is couched in seeming gladness

speaker: TROILUS
text: Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: An her hair were not somewhat darker than

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Helen’s—well, go to—there were no more comparison

speaker: PANDARUS
text: between the women. But, for my part, she is

speaker: PANDARUS
text: my kinswoman; I would not, as they term it, praise

speaker: PANDARUS
text: her, but I would somebody had heard her talk yesterday,

speaker: PANDARUS
text: as I did. I will not dispraise your sister Cassandra’s

speaker: PANDARUS
text: wit, but—

speaker: TROILUS
text: O, Pandarus! I tell thee, Pandarus:

speaker: TROILUS
text: When I do tell thee there my hopes lie drowned,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Reply not in how many fathoms deep

speaker: TROILUS
text: They lie indrenched. I tell thee I am mad

speaker: TROILUS
text: In Cressid’s love. Thou answer’st she is fair;

speaker: TROILUS
text: Pourest in the open ulcer of my heart

speaker: TROILUS
text: Her eyes, her hair, her cheek, her gait, her voice;

speaker: TROILUS
text: Handiest in thy discourse—O—that her hand,

speaker: TROILUS
text: In whose comparison all whites are ink

speaker: TROILUS
text: Writing their own reproach, to whose soft seizure

speaker: TROILUS
text: The cygnet’s down is harsh, and spirit of sense

speaker: TROILUS
text: Hard as the palm of plowman. This thou tell’st me,

speaker: TROILUS
text: As true thou tell’st me, when I say I love her.

speaker: TROILUS
text: But, saying thus, instead of oil and balm

speaker: TROILUS
text: Thou lay’st in every gash that love hath given me

speaker: TROILUS
text: The knife that made it.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I speak no more than truth.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Thou dost not speak so much.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Faith, I’ll not meddle in it. Let her be as she

speaker: PANDARUS
text: is. If she be fair, ’tis the better for her; an she be

speaker: PANDARUS
text: not, she has the mends in her own hands.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Good Pandarus—how now, Pandarus?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I have had my labor for my travail, ill thought

speaker: PANDARUS
text: on of her, and ill thought on of you; gone between

speaker: PANDARUS
text: and between, but small thanks for my labor.

speaker: TROILUS
text: What, art thou angry, Pandarus? What, with

speaker: TROILUS
text: me?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Because she’s kin to me, therefore she’s not

speaker: PANDARUS
text: so fair as Helen; an she were not kin to me, she

speaker: PANDARUS
text: would be as fair o’ Friday as Helen is on Sunday.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: But what care I? I care not an she were a blackamoor;

speaker: PANDARUS
text: ’tis all one to me.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Say I she is not fair?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I do not care whether you do or no. She’s a

speaker: PANDARUS
text: fool to stay behind her father. Let her to the Greeks,

speaker: PANDARUS
text: and so I’ll tell her the next time I see her. For my

speaker: PANDARUS
text: part, I’ll meddle nor make no more i’ th’ matter.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Pandarus—

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Not I.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Sweet Pandarus—

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Pray you speak no more to me. I will leave

speaker: PANDARUS
text: all as I found it, and there an end.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Peace, you ungracious clamors! Peace, rude sounds!

speaker: TROILUS
text: Fools on both sides! Helen must needs be fair

speaker: TROILUS
text: When with your blood you daily paint her thus.

speaker: TROILUS
text: I cannot fight upon this argument;

speaker: TROILUS
text: It is too starved a subject for my sword.

speaker: TROILUS
text: But Pandarus—O gods, how do you plague me!

speaker: TROILUS
text: I cannot come to Cressid but by Pandar,

speaker: TROILUS
text: And he’s as tetchy to be wooed to woo

speaker: TROILUS
text: As she is stubborn-chaste against all suit.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Tell me, Apollo, for thy Daphnes love,

speaker: TROILUS
text: What Cressid is, what Pandar, and what we.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Her bed is India; there she lies, a pearl.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Between our Ilium and where she resides,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Let it be called the wild and wand’ring flood,

speaker: TROILUS
text: Ourself the merchant, and this sailing Pandar

speaker: TROILUS
text: Our doubtful hope, our convoy, and our bark.

speaker: AENEAS
text: How now, Prince Troilus? Wherefore not afield?

speaker: TROILUS
text: Because not there. This woman’s answer sorts,

speaker: TROILUS
text: For womanish it is to be from thence.

speaker: TROILUS
text: What news, Aeneas, from the field today?

speaker: AENEAS
text: That Paris is returnèd home, and hurt.

speaker: TROILUS
text: By whom, Aeneas?

speaker: AENEAS
text: Troilus, by Menelaus.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Let Paris bleed. ’Tis but a scar to scorn;

speaker: TROILUS
text: Paris is gored with Menelaus’ horn.

speaker: AENEAS
text: Hark what good sport is out of town today!

speaker: TROILUS
text: Better at home, if “would I might” were “may.”

speaker: TROILUS
text: But to the sport abroad. Are you bound thither?

speaker: AENEAS
text: In all swift haste.

speaker: TROILUS
text: Come, go we then together.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Who were those went by?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Queen Hecuba and Helen.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: And whither go they?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Up to the eastern tower,

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Whose height commands as subject all the vale,

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: To see the battle. Hector, whose patience

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Is as a virtue fixed, today was moved.

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: He chid Andromache and struck his armorer;

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: And, like as there were husbandry in war,

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Before the sun rose he was harnessed light,

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: And to the field goes he, where every flower

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Did as a prophet weep what it foresaw

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: In Hector’s wrath.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: What was his cause of anger?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: The noise goes, this: there is among the Greeks

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: A lord of Trojan blood, nephew to Hector.

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: They call him Ajax.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Good; and what of him?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: They say he is a very man per se

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: And stands alone.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: So do all men unless they are drunk, sick,

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: or have no legs.

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: This man, lady, hath robbed many beasts

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: of their particular additions. He is as valiant as the

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: lion, churlish as the bear, slow as the elephant, a

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: man into whom nature hath so crowded humors

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: that his valor is crushed into folly, his folly sauced

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: with discretion. There is no man hath a virtue that

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: he hath not a glimpse of, nor any man an attaint

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: but he carries some stain of it. He is melancholy

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: without cause and merry against the hair. He hath

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: the joints of everything, but everything so out of

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: joint that he is a gouty Briareus, many hands and

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: no use, or purblind Argus, all eyes and no sight.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: But how should this man that makes me

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: smile make Hector angry?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: They say he yesterday coped Hector in the

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: battle and struck him down, the disdain and

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: shame whereof hath ever since kept Hector fasting

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: and waking.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Who comes here?

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: Madam, your Uncle Pandarus.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Hector’s a gallant man.

speaker: ALEXANDER
text: As may be in the world, lady.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: What’s that? What’s that?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Good morrow, Uncle Pandarus.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Good morrow, Cousin Cressid. What do you

speaker: PANDARUS
text: talk of?— Good morrow, Alexander.—How do you,

speaker: PANDARUS
text: cousin? When were you at Ilium?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: This morning, uncle.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: What were you talking of when I came?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Was Hector armed and gone ere you came to

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Ilium? Helen was not up, was she?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Hector was gone, but Helen was not up.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: E’en so. Hector was stirring early.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: That were we talking of, and of his anger.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Was he angry?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: So he says here.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: True, he was so. I know the cause too. He’ll

speaker: PANDARUS
text: lay about him today, I can tell them that; and

speaker: PANDARUS
text: there’s Troilus will not come far behind him. Let

speaker: PANDARUS
text: them take heed of Troilus, I can tell them that too.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: What, is he angry too?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Who, Troilus? Troilus is the better man of

speaker: PANDARUS
text: the two.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: O Jupiter, there’s no comparison.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: What, not between Troilus and Hector? Do

speaker: PANDARUS
text: you know a man if you see him?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Ay, if I ever saw him before and knew him.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Well, I say Troilus is Troilus.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Then you say as I say, for I am sure he is not

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Hector.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: No, nor Hector is not Troilus in some degrees.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: ’Tis just to each of them; he is himself.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Himself? Alas, poor Troilus, I would he were.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: So he is.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Condition I had gone barefoot to India.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: He is not Hector.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Himself? No, he’s not himself. Would he

speaker: PANDARUS
text: were himself! Well, the gods are above. Time must

speaker: PANDARUS
text: friend or end. Well, Troilus, well, I would my heart

speaker: PANDARUS
text: were in her body. No, Hector is not a better man

speaker: PANDARUS
text: than Troilus.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Excuse me.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: He is elder.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Pardon me, pardon me.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Th’ other's not come to ’t. You shall tell me

speaker: PANDARUS
text: another tale when th’ other’s come to ’t. Hector

speaker: PANDARUS
text: shall not have his wit this year.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: He shall not need it, if he have his own.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Nor his qualities.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: No matter.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Nor his beauty.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: ’Twould not become him. His own ’s better.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: You have no judgment, niece. Helen herself

speaker: PANDARUS
text: swore th’ other day that Troilus, for a brown favor—

speaker: PANDARUS
text: for so ’tis, I must confess—not brown neither—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: No, but brown.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Faith, to say truth, brown and not brown.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: To say the truth, true and not true.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: She praised his complexion above Paris’.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Why, Paris hath color enough.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: So he has.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Then Troilus should have too much. If she

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: praised him above, his complexion is higher than

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: his. He having color enough, and the other higher,

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: is too flaming a praise for a good complexion. I

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: had as lief Helen’s golden tongue had commended

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Troilus for a copper nose.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I swear to you, I think Helen loves him better

speaker: PANDARUS
text: than Paris.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Then she’s a merry Greek indeed.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Nay, I am sure she does. She came to him

speaker: PANDARUS
text: th’ other day into the compassed window—and

speaker: PANDARUS
text: you know he has not past three or four hairs on his

speaker: PANDARUS
text: chin—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Indeed, a tapster’s arithmetic may soon bring

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: his particulars therein to a total.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Why, he is very young, and yet will he within

speaker: PANDARUS
text: three pound lift as much as his brother Hector.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Is he so young a man and so old a lifter?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: But to prove to you that Helen loves him: she

speaker: PANDARUS
text: came and puts me her white hand to his cloven

speaker: PANDARUS
text: chin—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Juno have mercy! How came it cloven?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Why, you know ’tis dimpled. I think his

speaker: PANDARUS
text: smiling becomes him better than any man in all

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Phrygia.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: O, he smiles valiantly.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Does he not?

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: O yes, an ’twere a cloud in autumn.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Why, go to, then. But to prove to you that

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Helen loves Troilus—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Troilus will stand to the proof if you’ll

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: prove it so.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Troilus? Why, he esteems her no more than

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I esteem an addle egg.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: If you love an addle egg as well as you love

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: an idle head, you would eat chickens i’ th’ shell.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I cannot choose but laugh to think how she

speaker: PANDARUS
text: tickled his chin. Indeed, she has a marvellous

speaker: PANDARUS
text: white hand, I must needs confess—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Without the rack.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: And she takes upon her to spy a white hair

speaker: PANDARUS
text: on his chin.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Alas, poor chin! Many a wart is richer.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: But there was such laughing! Queen Hecuba

speaker: PANDARUS
text: laughed that her eyes ran o’er—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: With millstones.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: And Cassandra laughed—

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: But there was a more temperate fire under

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: the pot of her eyes. Did her eyes run o’er too?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: And Hector laughed.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: At what was all this laughing?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Marry, at the white hair that Helen spied on

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Troilus’ chin.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: An ’t had been a green hair, I should have

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: laughed too.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: They laughed not so much at the hair as at

speaker: PANDARUS
text: his pretty answer.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: What was his answer?

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Quoth she “Here’s but two-and-fifty hairs

speaker: PANDARUS
text: on your chin, and one of them is white.”

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: This is her question.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: That’s true, make no question of that. “Two-and-fifty

speaker: PANDARUS
text: hairs,” quoth he, “and one white. That

speaker: PANDARUS
text: white hair is my father, and all the rest are his

speaker: PANDARUS
text: sons.” “Jupiter!” quoth she, “which of these hairs

speaker: PANDARUS
text: is Paris, my husband?” “The forked one,” quoth he.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: “Pluck ’t out, and give it him.” But there was such

speaker: PANDARUS
text: laughing, and Helen so blushed, and Paris so

speaker: PANDARUS
text: chafed, and all the rest so laughed that it passed.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: So let it now, for it has been a great while

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: going by.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Well, cousin, I told you a thing yesterday.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Think on ’t.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: So I do.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: I’ll be sworn ’tis true. He will weep you an

speaker: PANDARUS
text: ’twere a man born in April.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: And I’ll spring up in his tears an ’twere a nettle

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: against May.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Hark, they are coming from the field. Shall

speaker: PANDARUS
text: we stand up here and see them as they pass toward

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Ilium? Good niece, do, sweet niece Cressida.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: At your pleasure.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Here, here, here’s an excellent place. Here

speaker: PANDARUS
text: we may see most bravely. I’ll tell you them all by

speaker: PANDARUS
text: their names as they pass by, but mark Troilus

speaker: PANDARUS
text: above the rest.

speaker: CRESSIDA
text: Speak not so loud.

speaker: PANDARUS
text: That’s Aeneas. Is not that a brave man? He’s

speaker: PANDARUS
text: one of the flowers of Troy, I can tell you. But mark

speaker: PANDARUS
text: Troilus; you shall see anon.

speaker: CRESSIDA
